questions.doc_title: ToMAToMP: Robust and Multi-Parameter Topological Clustering
questions.question: How does the ToMAToMP topological clustering algorithm combine several input functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{p}$ using a family of diagonal lines, and what is the complexity of the algorithm?
questions.question_ru: Как алгоритм топологической кластеризации ToMAToMP объединяет несколько входных функций $f_{1},\dots,f_{p}$ с помощью семейства диагональных линий и какова сложность алгоритма?
questions.reference_answer: ToMAToMP starts from a family of diagonal lines, computes a ToMATo clustering on every line, relates the clusters across lines using the intervals appearing in the MMA decomposition (so all clusters are indexed by MMA intervals), and assigns each point $x$ to the most frequent ToMATo cluster it belongs to across the lines. Its complexity is driven by computing MMA decompositions, which is cubic in the number of graph nodes and edges.

evidence.text: The main idea is quite simple: start with a family of diagonal lines $\mathcal{L}$, compute the ToMATo clusterings on every line, relate the ToMATo clusters of different lines together using the intervals appearing in the MMA decomposition (so that all ToMATo clusters are now indexed by the MMA intervals), and, for every data point $x$, assign it to the most frequent ToMATo cluster that it belongs to across the lines. See Algorithm 1. Its complexity is driven by the one of computing MMA decompositions, which is cubic in the number of graph nodes and edges.

questions.doc_title: ToMAToMP: Robust and Multi-Parameter Topological Clustering
questions.question: What are the main limitations of the ToMATo topological clustering algorithm that motivate the development of a multi-parameter extension?
questions.question_ru: Каковы основные ограничения алгоритма топологической кластеризации ToMATo, которые мотивируют разработку многопараметрического расширения?
questions.reference_answer: ToMATo requires building a graph $G$ whose tuning is left to the user but is critical for clustering quality; it is sensitive to outlier function values, since only a few aberrant points can destroy the clusters; and it can only handle one function at a time, whereas many applications need the modes of several functions such as pairs or triplets of gene expressions.

evidence.text: However, ToMATo suffers from a few weaknesses. First, deciding whether a data point is a regular point, a saddle, a local minimum or a local maximum requires to build a graph $G$ on top of the data points (point types are then assessed based on the neighbor values). Such graph is a hyper-parameter whose tuning is left to the user, despite being critical for the clustering quality. Second, while the PH framework allows to guarantee that ToMATo clusters are robust to small function perturbations, ToMATo is sensitive to *outlier* values: only a few points with aberrant function values are sufficient to destroy ToMATo clusters. Finally, there are many applications where the modes of *several* functions are relevant (for instance, pairs or triplets of gene expressions), but ToMATo can only handle one function at a time.
section_path: ToMAToMP: Robust and Multi-Parameter Topological Clustering

questions.question_ru: В топологической кластеризации с помощью ToMATo диаграмма персистентности используется для построения иерархии мод. Что означает, что диаграмма персистентности ${\rm Dgm}_{0}(f)$ является $(d_{1},d_{2})$-разделённой для двух параметров $0\leq d_{1}<d_{2}$?

evidence.text:
The robustness property of ToMATo requires that the PD points are sufficiently separated:

**Definition 1 ((6, Definition 4.1)).** Let $0\leq d_{1}<d_{2}$. The PD ${\rm Dgm}_{0}(f)$ is called *$(d_{1},d_{2})$-separated* if its points have prominences either less than $d_{1}$ or more than $d_{2}$. See Figure1.

questions.question: In the Manifold Topology Divergence framework, how is the Cross-Barcode_i(P,Q) of two point clouds P and Q defined, and in which filtered simplicial complex are the birth and death times of its features recorded?
questions.question_ru: В рамках фреймворка Manifold Topology Divergence как определяется Cross-Barcode_i(P,Q) для двух облаков точек P и Q и в каком фильтрованном симплициальном комплексе регистрируются времена рождения и смерти его топологических признаков?
questions.reference_answer: Cross-Barcode_i(P,Q) is the set of intervals recording the birth and death times of i-dimensional topological features in the filtered simplicial complex R_α(Γ_{P∪Q}, m_{(P∪Q)/Q}).

evidence.text: **Definition.** The $\text{Cross-Barcode}_{i}(P,Q)$ is the set of intervals recording the “births" and “deaths" times of $i-$dimensional topological features in the filtered simplicial complex $R_{\alpha}(\Gamma_{P\cup Q},m_{(P\cup Q)/Q})$.

questions.reference_answer: The average Kendall-tau rank correlation with the disturbance level is 0.89 for MTop-Div(D,M) and only 0.36 for the Geometry Score.

evidence.text: Figure 5 shows the results. Ideally, the quality measure should monotonically increase with the disturbance level. We conclude that Geometry Score is monotone only for ‘mode invention’ and ‘intra-mode collapse’ while MTop-Div(D,M) is almost monotone for all the cases. The average Kendall-tau rank correlation between MTop-Div(D,M) and disturbance level is 0.89, while for Geometry Score the rank correlation is only 0.36.

questions.doc_title: Manifold Topology Divergence: a Framework for Comparing Data Manifolds
questions.question: What limitations of the Geometry Score (GScore) as a GAN evaluation measure are pointed out, regarding its sensitivity to simple transformations of point clouds and the computational cost of its barcodes?
questions.question_ru: Какие ограничения Geometry Score (GScore) как метрики оценки GAN указываются — в отношении её чувствительности к простым преобразованиям облаков точек и вычислительной стоимости её штрих-кодов?
questions.reference_answer: GScore is not sensitive even to simple transformations such as constant shift, dilation, or reflection, and its barcodes are computed approximately from approximate witness complexes on 64 landmark points, making the procedure stochastic and requiring several thousand repetitions, so its calculation can be prohibitively long for large datasets.

evidence.text: The *Geometry Score* (GScore) [19] is the L2-distance between mean Relative Living Times (RLT) of topological features calculated for the model distribution and the true data distribution. The GScore is domain agnostic, does not involve auxiliary pretrained networks and is not limited to 2D images. However, GScore is not sensitive even to some simple transformations - like constant shift, dilation, or reflection (see our Fig. 2, 4). The barcodes in GScore are calculated approximately, based only on the approximate witness complexes on $64$ landmark points sampled from each distribution. That’s why the procedure is stochastic and should be repeated several thousand times for averaging. Thus, the calculation of GScore can be prohibitively long for large datasets.

questions.question_ru: В методах, сравнивающих много-масштабную топологию двух облаков точек $P$ и $\tilde{P}$ одинакового размера с помощью взвешенного графа с удвоенным числом вершин $\hat{\mathcal{G}}^{w,\tilde{w}}$, что именно фиксирует величина R-Cross-Barcode$_i(P,\tilde{P})$ и что означает полный R-Cross-Barcode$_*(P,\tilde{P})$?
questions.reference_answer: R-Cross-Barcode$_i(P,\tilde{P})$ is the set of intervals recording the births and deaths of $i$-dimensional topological features in the filtered simplicial complex $R_\alpha(\hat{\mathcal{G}}^{w,\tilde{w}})$; the full R-Cross-Barcode$_*(P,\tilde{P})$ records the differences in the multiscale topology of the two embeddings, and features with longer lifespans generally indicate the essential features.

evidence.text:
**Definition**. The *R-Cross-Barcode${}_{i}(P,\tilde{P})$* is the set of intervals recording the “births” and “deaths” of $i$-dimensional topological features in the filtered simplicial complex $R_{\alpha}(\hat{\mathcal{G}}^{w,\tilde{w}})$.

The *R-Cross-Barcode${}_{*}(P,\tilde{P})$* (for *Representations’ Cross-Barcode*) records the differences in the multiscale topology of the two embeddings. The topological features with longer lifespans indicate in general the essential features.

questions.question: In the RTD computation pipeline, how are the pairwise distance matrices of two point clouds normalized before building the Vietoris-Rips complex, and what property is this normalization intended to guarantee?
questions.question_ru: В вычислительном конвейере RTD как нормируются матрицы попарных расстояний двух облаков точек перед построением комплекса Вьеториса–Рипса и какое свойство должна гарантировать эта нормировка?
questions.reference_answer: The metrics in the two ambient spaces are normalized so that the 0.9 quantiles of pairwise distances in the two point clouds coincide; this ensures the score has scaling invariance, a reasonable property of a good representation similarity measure.

evidence.text: First we compute the *R-Cross-Barcode${}_{1}(P,\tilde{P})$* on two representations $P,\tilde{P}$ of a sample $V$. For this we calculate the matrices of pairwise distances $w$, $\tilde{w}$ within the point clouds $P$, $\tilde{P}$. We assume that the metrics in the ambient spaces of representations are normalized so that the two point clouds are of comparable size, namely their $0.9$ quantile of pairwise distances coincide. This ensures that our score has scaling invariance, the reasonable property of a good representation similarity measure, as argued in e.g. (Kornblith et al. 2019).

questions.doc_title: Induced Matchings and the Algebraic Stability of Persistence Barcodes
questions.question: What advantages does the algebraic stability theorem for persistence barcodes offer over the earlier stability result for the persistent homology of $\mathbb{R}$-valued functions?
questions.question_ru: Какие преимущества даёт алгебраическая теорема устойчивости для штрихкодов персистентности по сравнению с более ранним результатом устойчивости для персистентной гомологии $\mathbb{R}$-значных функций?
questions.reference_answer: It removes some technical conditions required by the earlier stability result for $\mathbb{R}$-valued functions, generalizing it to a wider class of functions, and it provides a formalism for comparing barcodes of functions on different domains or of data that do not arise from functions at all; this flexibility yields approximation and inference theorems for persistent homology that would otherwise be harder to establish.

evidence.text: While the earlier stability result for the persistent homology of $\mathbb{R}$-valued functions [14] is itself a powerful result with several important applications, the more general algebraic stability theorem offers significant advantages. First, it allows us to dispense with some technical conditions on the stability result for functions of [14], thereby yielding a generalization of that result to a wider class of functions. Second and perhaps more importantly, the algebraic stability theorem offers a formalism for comparing the barcode invariants of functions defined on different domains, or for comparing barcode invariants of data that do not directly arise from functions at all. In practice, this added flexibility is quite valuable: It allows us to establish fundamental approximation and inference theorems for persistent homology that would otherwise be much harder to come by [9, 11, 8, 13, 20].
section_path: Induced Matchings and the Algebraic Stability of Persistence Barcodes

questions.doc_title: Induced Matchings and the Algebraic Stability of Persistence Barcodes
questions.question: In the induced matching theorem, what is asserted about a matched pair of intervals $\mathcal{X}_f\langle b,d\rangle=\langle b',d'\rangle$ of a morphism $f:M\to N$ of pointwise finite dimensional persistence modules when $\coker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial, and dually when $\ker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial?
questions.question_ru: Что утверждается в теореме об индуцированном спаривании о спаренной паре интервалов $\mathcal{X}_f\langle b,d\rangle=\langle b',d'\rangle$ морфизма $f:M\to N$ поточечно конечномерных модулей персистентности, когда $\coker f$ является $\epsilon$-тривиальным, и двойственно, когда $\ker f$ является $\epsilon$-тривиальным?
questions.reference_answer: For a matched pair, $b'\leq b<d'\leq d$. If $\coker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial then $\mathcal{B}_N^\epsilon\subseteq\im\mathcal{X}_f$ and $b'\leq b\leq b'+\epsilon$; dually, if $\ker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial then $\mathcal{B}_M^\epsilon\subseteq\coim\mathcal{X}_f$ and $d-\epsilon\leq d'\leq d$.

evidence.text:
**Theorem 6.1 (Induced Matching Theorem).** Let $f:M\to N$ be a morphism of pointwise finite dimensional persistence modules and suppose $\mathcal{X}_{f}{\langle b\mkern 1.0mu,d\rangle}={\langle b^{\prime}\mkern 1.0mu,d^{\prime}\rangle}$. Then

- (i) $b^{\prime}\leq b<d^{\prime}\leq d$.

- (ii) If $\coker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial, then $\mathcal{B}_{N}^{\epsilon}\subseteq\im\mathcal{X}_{f}$ and

$$
b^{\prime}\leq b\leq b^{\prime}+\epsilon.
$$

- (iii) Dually, if $\ker f$ is $\epsilon$-trivial, then $\mathcal{B}_{M}^{\epsilon}\subseteq\coim\mathcal{X}_{f}$ and

$$
d-\epsilon\leq d^{\prime}\leq d.
$$
section_path: Induced Matchings and the Algebraic Stability of Persistence Barcodes

questions.doc_title: Induced Matchings and the Algebraic Stability of Persistence Barcodes
questions.question: What does the algebraic stability theorem for q-tame persistence modules (those whose transition maps have finite rank) state about the bottleneck distance between the undecorated barcodes $\mathcal{U}_M$, $\mathcal{U}_N$ and the interleaving distance?
questions.question_ru: Что утверждает теорема алгебраической устойчивости для q-tame модулей персистентности (у которых переходные отображения имеют конечный ранг) о расстоянии узкого места (bottleneck distance) между недекорированными штрихкодами $\mathcal{U}_M$, $\mathcal{U}_N$ и расстоянием интерливинга?
questions.reference_answer: If $M$ and $N$ are q-tame and are $(\delta+\epsilon)$-interleaved for every $\epsilon>0$, then there exists a $\delta$-matching between the undecorated barcodes $\mathcal{U}_M$ and $\mathcal{U}_N$, so that $d_B(\mathcal{U}_M,\mathcal{U}_N)\leq d_I(M,N)$.

evidence.text:
**Theorem 7.4 (Algebraic Stability for q-Tame Modules [10, Theorem 4.20]).** If $M$ and $N$ are q-tame and are $(\delta+\epsilon)$-interleaved for all $\epsilon>0$, then there is a $\delta$-matching between $\mathcal{U}_{M}$ and $\mathcal{U}_{N}$. In particular,

$$
d_{B}(\mathcal{U}_{M},\mathcal{U}_{N})\leq d_{I}(M,N).
$$

questions.doc_title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
questions.question: In the theoretical analysis of flow matching, a random variable $W$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is called $\lambda$-regular for some $\lambda \geq 1$. State the precise definition: which Gaussian perturbation is added, and what operator-norm inequality must the conditional covariance of this perturbation satisfy for every $\mathbf{x}$?
questions.question_ru: В теоретическом анализе flow matching случайная величина $W$ в $\mathbb{R}^d$ называется $\lambda$-регулярной для некоторого $\lambda \geq 1$. Сформулируйте точное определение: какое гауссово возмущение добавляется и какому неравенству в операторной норме должна удовлетворять условная ковариация этого возмущения для всех $\mathbf{x}$?
questions.reference_answer: An $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued random variable $W$ is $\lambda$-regular if for every $\tau \in (0,\infty)$, taking $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2 I_d)$ independently of $W$ and setting $W' = W + \xi$, one has $\|\mathrm{cov}_{\xi | W' = \mathbf{x}}(\xi)\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq \lambda \tau^2$ for all $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d$. A distribution is $\lambda$-regular when its associated random variable is.

evidence.text:
**Definition 1.** For a real number $\lambda\geq 1$, we say an $\mathbb{R}^{d}$-valued random variable $W$ is $\lambda$**-regular** if, whenever we take $\tau\in(0,\infty)$ and $\xi\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\tau^{2}I_{d})$ independently of $W$ and set $W^{\prime}=W+\xi$, for all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ we have

$$
\left\|{\cov}_{\xi|W^{\prime}=\mathbf{x}}(\xi)\right\|_{\textup{op}}\leq\lambda\tau^{2}.
$$

We say that a distribution on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is $\lambda$-regular if the associated random variable is $\lambda$-regular.

questions.doc_title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
questions.question: Consider a flow matching procedure in which $v_\theta$ is an approximate velocity field satisfying an $L^2$ approximation error bound $\varepsilon$ and a time-dependent spatial Lipschitz condition. What upper bound on the 2-Wasserstein distance $W_2(\hat{\pi}_1, \pi_1)$ between the law $\hat{\pi}_1$ of the generated endpoint $Y_1$ and the target distribution $\pi_1$ is obtained?
questions.question_ru: Рассмотрим процедуру flow matching, в которой $v_\theta$ — приближённое поле скоростей, удовлетворяющее границе ошибки аппроксимации в $L^2$, равной $\varepsilon$, и зависящему от времени условию Липшица по пространственной переменной. Какая верхняя оценка на расстояние Вассерштейна $W_2(\hat{\pi}_1, \pi_1)$ между распределением $\hat{\pi}_1$ сгенерированной концевой точки $Y_1$ и целевым распределением $\pi_1$ получается?
questions.reference_answer: Under Assumptions 1-3, $W_2(\hat{\pi}_1, \pi_1) \leq \varepsilon \exp\{\int_0^1 L_t\,\mathrm{d}t\}$, where $Y$ is the flow starting in $\pi_0$ with velocity field $v_\theta$ and $\hat{\pi}_1$ is the law of $Y_1$. The error depends linearly on the $L^2$ approximation error $\varepsilon$ and exponentially on the integral of the approximate flow's Lipschitz constant $L_t$.

evidence.text:
**Theorem 1.** Suppose that $\pi_{0}$, $\pi_{1}$ are probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, that $Y$ is the flow starting in $\pi_{0}$ with velocity field $v_{\theta}$, and $\hat{\pi}_{1}$ is the law of $Y_{1}$. Then, under Assumptions 1-3, we have

$$
W_{2}(\hat{\pi}_{1},\pi_{1})\leq\varepsilon\myexp\Big\{\int_{0}^{1}L_{t}\;\mathrm{d}t\Big\}.
$$

We see that the error depends linearly on the $L^{2}$ approximation error $\varepsilon$ and exponentially on the integral of the Lipschitz constant of the approximate flow $L_{t}$.

This is required in practice because $L_t$ often explodes as $t \rightarrow 0$ or $1$, as happens for example when $\pi_0$ or $\pi_1$ do not have full support.

evidence.text: We remark that our Theorem 1 is similar in content to Proposition 3 in Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden 2023. The crucial difference is that we work with a time-varying Lipschitz constant, which is required in practice since in many cases $L_{t}$ explodes as $t\rightarrow 0$ or $1$, as happens for example if $\pi_{0}$ or $\pi_{1}$ do not have full support.

questions.doc_title: Towards a topological-geometrical theory of group equivariant non-expansive operators for data analysis and machine learning
questions.question: What is a Group Equivariant Non-Expansive Operator (GENEO) associated with a homomorphism between two perception pairs?
questions.question_ru: Что такое групповой эквивариантный нерастягивающий оператор (GENEO), ассоциированный с гомоморфизмом между двумя парами восприятия?
questions.reference_answer: A GENEO associated with a fixed homomorphism $T:G\to H$ is a perception map $F$ from $(\varPhi,G)$ to $(\varPsi,H)$ with respect to $T$ that is also non-expansive, i.e. $D_{\varPsi}(F(\varphi_{1}),F(\varphi_{2}))\leq D_{\varPhi}(\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2})$ for every $\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2}\in\varPhi$.

evidence.text: **Definition 4.11.** Assume that $(\varPhi,G)$,$(\varPsi,H)$ are two perception pairs and that a homomorphism $T:G\to H$ has been fixed. If $F$ is a perception map from $(\varPhi,G)$ to $(\varPsi,H)$ with respect to $T$ and $F$ is non-expansive (i.e., $D_{\varPsi}\left(F(\varphi_{1}),F(\varphi_{2})\right)\leq D_{\varPhi}\left(\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2}\right)$ for every $\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2}\in\varPhi$), then $F$ is called a *Group Equivariant Non-Expansive Operator (GENEO) associated with $T:G\to H$*.

questions.doc_title: Towards a topological-geometrical theory of group equivariant non-expansive operators for data analysis and machine learning
questions.question: Why does the group equivariant non-expansive operator framework keep a pseudo-metric on the measurement space X instead of quotienting X by the equivalence relation that identifies points at pseudo-distance zero?
questions.question_ru: Почему в рамках теории групповых эквивариантных нерастягивающих операторов на пространстве измерений X сохраняют псевдометрику вместо факторизации X по отношению эквивалентности, отождествляющему точки на псевдорасстоянии ноль?
questions.reference_answer: Because several different sets of admissible measurements can be defined on the same set $X$, giving different quotient spaces; keeping the original $X$ lets one link equivalence classes across different $\varPhi$ and study how points relate when $\varPhi$ changes, so the framework retains pseudo-metrics rather than passing to metrics.

evidence.text: The reader could think better to change the pseudo-metric $D_{X}$ into a metric $D^{\prime}$ by quotienting out $X$ by the equivalence relation $x_{1}Rx_{2}\iff D_{X}(x_{1},x_{2})=0$ and defining $D^{\prime}([x_{1}],[x_{2}])=D_{X}(x_{1},x_{2})$ for any $[x_{1}],[x_{2}]\in X/R$. The reason we do not do this is that several different sets of admissible measurements can be considered on the same set $X$. For two different sets $\varPhi_{1}$, $\varPhi_{2}$ of admissible functions, we obtain two different quotient spaces $X/R_{1}$, $X/R_{2}$. If we forget about the original space $X$, we lose the possibility of linking the equivalence classes in $X/R_{1}$ with the ones in $X/R_{2}$. On the contrary, we prefer to preserve the identity of points in $X$, studying how they link to each other when we change the set $\varPhi$. This observation leads us to work with pseudo-metrics instead of metrics.
section_path: Towards a topological-geometrical theory of group equivariant non-expansive operators for data analysis and machine learning

questions.doc_title: Towards a topological-geometrical theory of group equivariant non-expansive operators for data analysis and machine learning
questions.question: How is an Isometry Equivariant Non-Expansive Operator (IENEO) F_p built from a parameter tuple p in S: what is its convolutional kernel G_p and what integral defines the output function psi?
questions.question_ru: Как строится изометрически эквивариантный нерастягивающий оператор (IENEO) F_p по кортежу параметров p из S: что такое его свёрточное ядро G_p и каким интегралом задаётся выходная функция psi?
questions.reference_answer: Given $p=(a_{1},\tau_{1},\ldots,a_{k},\tau_{k})\in S$, the kernel is $G_{p}(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{i}g_{\tau_{i}}(\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}})$, and $F_{p}$ maps $\varphi$ to $\psi(x,y)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\varphi(\alpha,\beta)\cdot\frac{G_{p}(x-\alpha,y-\beta)}{\|G_{p}\|_{L^{1}}}\ d\alpha\ d\beta$; it is equivariant with respect to the group $I$ of Euclidean plane isometries.

evidence.text:
For each $p=(a_{1},\tau_{1},\ldots,a_{k},\tau_{k})\in S$, we then consider the function $G_{p}:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined as

$$
G_{p}(x,y):=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{i}g_{\tau_{i}}\left(\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right).
$$

If we denote by $F_{p}$ the convolutional operator mapping each continuous function with compact support $\varphi:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\mathbb{R}$ to the continuous and with compactly supported function $\psi:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined as

$$
\psi(x,y):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\varphi(\alpha,\beta)\cdot\frac{G_{p}(x-\alpha,y-\beta)}{\|G_{p}\|_{L^{1}}}\ d\alpha\ d\beta.
$$

Then, the operator $F_{p}$ is a group equivariant non-expansive operator with respect to the group $I$ of Euclidean plane isometries. We call $F_{p}$ a IENEO (Isometry Equivariant Non-Expansive Operator).
section_path: Towards a topological-geometrical theory of group equivariant non-expansive operators for data analysis and machine learning

questions.doc_title: Optimal Unsupervised Domain Translation
questions.question: In CycleGAN-based Unsupervised Domain Translation, what are the two constraints the approach is built on, what exactly does coherence ensure about the transformations, and how is inversibility usually enforced as a loss?
questions.question_ru: На каких двух ограничениях (constraints) основывают свой подход CycleGAN и его расширения в Unsupervised Domain Translation, что именно обеспечивает coherence относительно преобразований и как обычно реализуется inversibility в виде функции потерь?
questions.reference_answer: The two constraints are coherence and inversibility. Coherence ensures the transformations exactly map the two domains one onto the other and is enforced by a discrepancy loss D(T♯α,β)+D(S♯β,α), while inversibility constructs information-preserving transformations and is usually enforced via a cycle-consistent loss ∥S∘T−id∥ + ∥T∘S−id∥.

evidence.text:
CycleGAN [5] and its extensions [8–11] base their approach on the two following constraints:

_Coherence_ ensures that the transformations exactly map the two domains one onto the other. Usually, it is enforced by using a loss term of the form _D_ ( _T♯α, β_ )+ _D_ ( _S♯β, α_ ), where _D_ corresponds to some measure of discrepancy between probability distributions. _D_ may be implemented using generative adversarial training [5], a denoising auto-encoder loss [8, 10], a distance in a shared projection space [12], etc. _Inversibility_ was proposed as a way to construct information preserving transformations and is usually enforced via a _cycle-consistent loss_<sup>4</sup> : _∥S ◦ T −_ id _∥Lp_ ( _α_ ) + _∥T ◦ S −_ id _∥Lp_ ( _β_ ).

questions.doc_title: Optimal Unsupervised Domain Translation
questions.question: Which conditions on the measures and on the transport cost function guarantee, according to the uniqueness theorem for optimal mappings in Unsupervised Domain Translation, that a unique pair of transformations (T, S) exists, and what properties does that pair satisfy?
questions.question_ru: Какие условия на меры и на функцию стоимости переноса гарантируют, согласно теореме о единственности оптимальных отображений в Unsupervised Domain Translation, существование единственной пары преобразований (T, S), и какими свойствами эта пара обладает?
questions.reference_answer: If α and β are absolutely continuous and the cost has the form c(x,y)=h(x−y) with h strictly convex, then there exists a unique couple (T,S) with T♯α=β and S♯β=α, where C(T) is minimal and S is the minimal transport from β to α.

evidence.text:
**Theorem 1.** _Let α, β be absolute continuous measures. If c_ ( _x, y_ ) = _h_ ( _x − y_ ) _where h is strictly convex, then there_ **_exists a unique_** _couple_ ( _T, S_ ) _of transformations such that:_

- _T♯α_ = _β, and S♯β_ = _α,_

- _C_ ( _T_ ) _is minimal, and S is the minimal transport from β to α._
section_path: 1.3 Unpaired Domain Translation as Optimal Transport

questions.doc_title: Optimal Unsupervised Domain Translation
questions.question: What inductive bias is proposed to explain why standard Unsupervised Domain Translation methods do not suffer in practice from their many theoretically bad solutions, and what relationship is found between network initialization gain, pairing accuracy, and transportation cost?
questions.question_ru: Какой индуктивный сдвиг (inductive bias) предлагается для объяснения того, почему стандартные методы Unsupervised Domain Translation на практике не страдают от множества теоретически плохих решений, и какая связь установлена между начальным масштабом инициализации сети, точностью спаривания и транспортной стоимостью?
questions.reference_answer: Standard UDT methods must yield an inductive bias that restricts the space of solutions, which the authors try to characterize. They find that accuracy is highly correlated with initialization gain of network parameters (accuracy decreases as gain increases), and that large initialization gain leads to high transportation w.r.t. the Euclidean cost, linking mapping accuracy to transportation cost.

evidence.text:
We have seen that standard approaches for UDT yield numerous (bad) solutions in theory, although this seems not to be a problem in practice. These methods must yield an inductive bias, effectively restricting the space of solutions. In this Section, using simple tasks (that nevertheless reflect usual UDT) , we attempt to characterize this bias. We find that:

- Accuracy of these methods is highly correlated with initialization gain of network parameters: as gain is increased, accuracy decreases.

- Large initialization gain leads to high transportation _w.r.t._ the Euclidean cost,

From this, it is possible to make the link between accuracy of the mapping and transportation cost.
section_path: B On of the Effect of Initialization Gain on UDT and Transport

questions.doc_title: Expected Batch Optimal Transport Plans and Consequences for Flow Matching
questions.question: In minibatch optimal transport for flow matching, what is the expected batch optimal transport plan $\overline{\pi}_{k}$ the law of, in terms of drawing random source and target batches and selecting matched pairs?
questions.question_ru: В мини-батчевом оптимальном транспорте для flow matching: законом чего является ожидаемый батчевый план оптимального транспорта $\overline{\pi}_{k}$ — опишите через розыгрыш случайных батчей источника и цели и выбор согласованных пар?
questions.reference_answer: The expected batch OT plan $\overline{\pi}_{k}$ is the law of the pair obtained by first drawing independent batches $(\mathbf{X}_{k},\mathbf{Y}_{k})\sim\mu^{\otimes k}\otimes\nu^{\otimes k}$, then solving OT between the empirical measures $\widehat{\mu}_{k}$ and $\widehat{\nu}_{k}$, and finally selecting one of the $k$ matched pairs uniformly at random; in the fully discrete case it is the averaged minibatch transport matrix of Fatras et al., 2021b.

evidence.text: Hence, $\overline{\pi}_{k}$ is the law of the pair obtained as follows: first draw $(\mathbf{X}_{k},\,\mathbf{Y}_{k})\sim\mu^{\otimes k}\otimes\nu^{\otimes k}$, then solve OT between $\widehat{\mu}_{k}$ and $\widehat{\nu}_{k}$, and finally select one of the $k$ matched pairs uniformly at random. This construction specializes, in the fully discrete case, to the averaged minibatch transport matrix of Fatras et al., 2021b. It also matches the marginalized minibatch coupling $q^{(k)}$ used in batch OT-FM by Pooladian et al., 2023a.

questions.doc_title: Expected Batch Optimal Transport Plans and Consequences for Flow Matching
questions.question: In the tractable two-atom model with standard Gaussian source and target $\operatorname{Unif}\{-1,\,1\}$, how does the Euler integration error behave asymptotically as the number of Euler steps $n$ grows, compared with increasing the OT batch size $k$?
questions.question_ru: В модельной задаче с двумя атомами, где источник — стандартное нормальное распределение, а цель — $\operatorname{Unif}\{-1,\,1\}$, как асимптотически ведёт себя ошибка эйлеровской интеграции при росте числа шагов Эйлера $n$ по сравнению с увеличением размера OT-батча $k$?
questions.reference_answer: In the two-atom model $\log\mathscr{E}_{n,\,1}\sim-\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}}n^{2/3}$ as $n\to\infty$, so the Euler error decays like $\exp(-cn^{2/3})$, whereas $\log\mathscr{E}_{1,\,k}\sim-\frac{1}{2}\log k$, i.e. only a $k^{-1/2}$-type decay with the OT batch size; increasing the NFE is therefore considerably more effective.

evidence.text:
**Proposition 4.3 (Asymptotic comparison between OT batch size and NFE).** Let $\mu=\mathcal{N}(0,\,1)$ and $\nu=\operatorname{Unif}\{-1,\,1\}$. Then $\log\mathscr{E}_{n,\,1}\sim-\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}}n^{\frac{2}{3}}$ as $n\to\infty$ and $\log\mathscr{E}_{1,\,k}\sim-\frac{1}{2}\log k$ as $k\to\infty$.

Increasing the number of Euler steps thus causes the integration error to decay as $\exp(-cn^{2/3})$, whereas increasing the OT batch size only yields a $k^{-1/2}$-type decay. In this specific setting, the influence of the NFE is considerably more pronounced, and this asymmetry remains clear even outside the asymptotic regime. Figure 5 displays the level sets of $\mathscr{E}_{n,\,k}$ in the $(n,\,k)$ plane. It shows for example that to compensate for a reduction in NFE from $25$ to $10$, one needs to increase OT batch size $k$ from $1$ to $90$, well beyond the two-atom support size.

questions.doc_title: Schrödinger Bridge Flow for Unpaired Data Translation
questions.question: In Entropic Optimal Transport between two distributions π0 and π1 on R^d, what optimization problem defines the entropic OT coupling Π⋆, and what does the hyperparameter ε control?
questions.question_ru: В задаче энтропийного оптимального транспорта между двумя распределениями π0 и π1 на R^d какую оптимизационную задачу решает энтропийная OT-связка Π⋆ и что регулирует гиперпараметр ε?
questions.reference_answer: The EOT coupling Π⋆ minimizes over couplings Π with marginals π0, π1 the objective ∫ over R^d×R^d of (1/2)‖x−y‖² dΠ(x,y) − εH(Π), where H(Π) is the differential entropy of Π and ε>0 is the entropic regularization hyperparameter (ε=0 recovers standard OT).

evidence.text:
Among an infinite number of such so-called coupling distributions $\Pi$, we are here interested in finding the Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) coupling $\Pi^{\star}$ defined as

$$
\Pi^{\star}=\mathrm{argmin}_{\Pi\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})}\left\{\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}}\frac{1}{2}\|x-y\|^{2}\mathrm{d}\Pi(x,y)-\varepsilon\mathrm{H}(\Pi)\ ;\ \Pi_{0}=\pi_{0},\ \Pi_{1}=\pi_{1}\right\}, \tag{2}
$$

where $\mathrm{H}(\Pi)$ is the differential entropy of $\Pi$ and $\varepsilon>0$ is a regularisation hyperparameter (Peyré et al., 2019). For $\varepsilon=0$, we recover the standard OT.
section_path: Schrödinger Bridge Flow for Unpaired Data Translation

questions.doc_title: Schrödinger Bridge Flow for Unpaired Data Translation
questions.question: In the α-IMF algorithm for solving the Schrödinger Bridge, what update rule defines the path measure P̂^{n+1} from P̂^n, and which known procedure is recovered when the stepsize α equals 1?
questions.question_ru: В алгоритме α-IMF для решения задачи Шрёдингера-моста какое правило обновления задаёт меру путей P̂^{n+1} через P̂^n и какая известная процедура восстанавливается при шаге α=1?
questions.reference_answer: α-IMF sets P̂^{n+1} = (1−α)P̂^n + α proj_R(proj_M(P̂^n)) together with P^n = proj_M(P̂^n); when α=1 this recovers the IMF procedure.

evidence.text:
Next, for any $\alpha\in(0,1]$, we define the following discretisation of (5) called $\alpha$-IMF:

$$
\hat{\mathbb{P}}^{n+1}=(1-\alpha)\hat{\mathbb{P}}^{n}+\alpha\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\hat{\mathbb{P}}^{n})), \tag{6}
$$

and $\mathbb{P}^{n}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\hat{\mathbb{P}}^{n})$. Note that for any $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\hat{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\in\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{Q})$. This recovers the IMF procedure (Shi et al., 2023; Peluchetti, 2023) when $\alpha=1$.
section_path: Schrödinger Bridge Flow for Unpaired Data Translation

questions.doc_title: Schrödinger Bridge Flow for Unpaired Data Translation
questions.question: For the flow of path measures (P^s, P̂^s) defined by ∂s P̂^s = proj_R(proj_M(P̂^s)) − P̂^s, what is the only fixed point of the flow, and how is it identified?
questions.question_ru: Для потока мер путей (P^s, P̂^s), задаваемого уравнением ∂s P̂^s = proj_R(proj_M(P̂^s)) − P̂^s, какова единственная неподвижная точка потока и как она отождествляется?
questions.reference_answer: The only fixed point is the Schrödinger Bridge: a fixed point satisfies P̄ = proj_R(proj_M(P̄)), which makes it a limit point of IMF and therefore equal to the SB P⋆ given by problem (3).

evidence.text: Crucially, the only fixed point of (5) is the SB. Indeed, let $\bar{\mathbb{P}}$ be a fixed point of $(\mathbb{P}^{s})_{s\geq 0}$ in (5). Then, we have that $\bar{\mathbb{P}}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\bar{\mathbb{P}}))$. Hence, we get $\bar{\mathbb{P}}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\dots(\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}}(\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\bar{\mathbb{P}})))\dots))$. Hence, under mild assumptions, $\bar{\mathbb{P}}$ is a limit point of IMF and therefore $\bar{\mathbb{P}}$ is the SB $\mathbb{P}^{\star}$ given by (3), see (Peluchetti, 2023, Theorem 2).

questions.doc_title: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces
questions.question: How is the discrete Gromov-Wasserstein discrepancy between two distributions defined, over what set is the coupling matrix optimized, and which loss function L makes the square root of the discrepancy a true distance?
questions.question_ru: Как определяется дискретное расхождение Громова–Вассерштейна между двумя распределениями, по какому множеству оптимизируется матрица связи (coupling) и какая функция потерь L делает квадратный корень из этого расхождения истинной метрикой?
questions.reference_answer: Given distance matrices and probability vectors (D,p) and (D̄,q), the discrete GW discrepancy is GW(D,D̄,p,q) := min over couplings T in U_{p,q} of Σ_{ijkl} L(D_ik,D̄_jl) T_ij T_kl, where U_{p,q} contains all couplings with marginals p and q. With the loss L(a,b)=L2(a,b)=½|a−b|², GW^{1/2} is a true distance.

evidence.text:
Given $n$ samples of the compared distributions $p\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $q\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y})$, the discrete formulation of the GW distance needs a similarity (or distance) matrix between the samples and a probability vector for each space, say $(D,\mathbf{p})$ and $(\bar{D},\mathbf{q})$, with $(D,\mathbf{p})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\times\Sigma_{n}$, where $\Sigma_{n}:=\{\mathbf{p}\in\mathbb{R}^{+}_{n};\sum_{i}\mathbf{p}_{i}=1\}$ is the $n$-dimensional probability simplex. Then, the GW discrepancy is

$$
\begin{split}\text{GW}(D,\bar{D},\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q})&:=\min_{T\in\mathcal{U}_{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q}}}\mathcal{E}_{D,\bar{D}}(T)\\ &:=\min_{T\in\mathcal{U}_{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q}}}\sum_{ijkl}L(D_{ik},\bar{D}_{jl})T_{ij}T_{kl},\end{split} \tag{1}
$$

where $\mathcal{U}_{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q}}:=\{T\in(\mathbb{R}_{+})^{n\times n};T\mathds{1}_{n}=\mathbf{p},T^{\top}\mathds{1}_{n}=\mathbf{q}\}$ is the set of all couplings $T$ between $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$. The loss function $L$ in our case is $L(a,b)=L_{2}(a,b):=\frac{1}{2}|a-b|^{2}$. If $L=L_{2}$, then $\text{GW}^{1/2}$ defines a (true) distance (Mémoli 2011).
section_path: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces

questions.doc_title: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces
questions.question: In the Gromov-Wasserstein GAN, how is the adversary network regularized so that it acts as an approximately orthogonal operator, and what closed-form solution exists for the optimal orthogonal matrix when the feature-space dimension equals the input dimension?
questions.question_ru: В Gromov-Wasserstein GAN как регуляризуется сеть-оппонент, чтобы она действовала как приблизительно ортогональный оператор, и какое решение в замкнутой форме существует для оптимальной ортогональной матрицы, когда размерность пространства признаков совпадает с размерностью входа?
questions.reference_answer: The adversary is regularized by the term R_β(f_ω(X),X)=β‖f_ω(X)−X P*ᵀ‖_F², where P* is the orthogonal matrix that most closely maps X to f_ω(X) and is found by solving an orthogonal Procrustes problem. When the feature dimension s equals the input dimension, P*=UVᵀ, with UΣVᵀ=SVD(f_ω(X)ᵀX).

evidence.text:
To enforce the approximation of $f_{\omega}$ as an orthogonal operator, we introduce a new orthogonal regularization approach, which ensures orthogonality of a network by minimizing the distance to the closest orthogonal matrix $P^{*}$. The regularization term is defined as

$$
R_{\beta}(f_{\omega}(X),X):=\beta\|f_{\omega}(X)-XP^{*\top}\|_{F}^{2}, \tag{5}
$$

where $P^{*}$ is an orthogonal matrix that most closely maps $X$ to $f_{\omega}(X)$, and $\beta$ is a hyperparameter. The matrix $P^{*}=\arg\min_{P\in O(s)}\|f_{\omega}(X)-XP^{\top}\|_{F}$, where $O(s)=\left\{P\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times s}\;|\;P^{\top}P=I\right\}$ and $s$ is the dimensionality of the feature space, can be obtained by solving an orthogonal Procrustes problem. If the dimensionality $s$ of the feature space equals the input dimension, then $P^{*}$ has a closed-form solution $P^{*}=UV^{\top}$, where $U$ and $V$ are the left and right singular vectors of $f_{\omega}(X)^{\top}X$, i.e. $U\Sigma V^{\top}=\textrm{SVD}(f_{\omega}(X)^{\top}X)$ (Schönemann 1966).
section_path: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces

questions.doc_title: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces
questions.question: Why does entropy regularization make the Gromov-Wasserstein discrepancy unsuitable as a loss in its original form, and how is a normalized version constructed to remove the resulting bias?
questions.question_ru: Почему энтропийная регуляризация делает расхождение Громова–Вассерштейна непригодным в качестве функции потерь в исходном виде и как строится его нормализованная версия, устраняющая возникающее смещение?
questions.reference_answer: With entropy regularization the discrepancy of identical metric measure spaces is no longer zero, so GW_ε is not a distance and its estimation from samples yields biased gradients. The normalized version subtracts the self-terms: GW̄_ε(D,D̄,p,q) := 2 GW_ε(D,D̄,p,q) − GW_ε(D,D,p,p) − GW_ε(D̄,D̄,q,q).

evidence.text:
With entropy regularization, $\text{GW}_{\epsilon}$ is not a distance any more, as the discrepancy of identical metric measure spaces is then no longer zero. Similar to the Wasserstein metric (Bellemare et al. 2017), the estimation of $\text{GW}_{\epsilon}$ from samples yields biased gradients. Inspired by Bellemare et al. 2017, we use a normalized entropy-regularized Gromov-Wasserstein discrepancy defined as

$$
\begin{split}\overline{\text{GW}}_{\epsilon}(D,\bar{D},\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q}):=\ 2\times\text{GW}_{\epsilon}(D,\bar{D},\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q})&\\ -\text{GW}_{\epsilon}(D,D,\mathbf{p},\mathbf{p})-\text{GW}_{\epsilon}(\bar{D},\bar{D},\mathbf{q},\mathbf{q})&.\end{split} \tag{7}
$$
section_path: Learning Generative Models across Incomparable Spaces

questions.doc_title: Transport based embeddings with topological guarantees
questions.question: In the optimal-transport-based embedding method where the data is encoded as a positive m x n stochastic matrix Q=(q_ij), how is the potential function psi on the positive probability simplex defined via the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the rows of Q, and what does a high value of psi indicate?
questions.question_ru: В методе вложения, основанном на оптимальном транспорте, где данные кодируются положительной стохастической матрицей Q=(q_ij), как определяется потенциальная функция psi на положительном вероятностном симплексе через дивергенцию Кульбака—Лейблера до строк Q, и что означает большое значение psi?
questions.reference_answer: The potential is $\psi(p)=\log\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}\exp(-\KL(p\lVert q_{i\bullet}))$ with coefficients $c_{i}>0$, where $\KL$ is the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the rows $q_{i\bullet}$ of $Q$. It takes high values on distributions $p$ that are similar to many rows of $Q$, analogous to a statistical density estimator.

evidence.text:
Our proposed potential function $\psi:\Delta_{n}^{+}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ can now be defined by

$$
\psi(p)=\log\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}\exp(-\KL(p\lVert q_{i\bullet})) \tag{1.6}
$$

for some coefficients $c_{i}>0$. This function has high values on distributions $p\in\Delta_{n}$ which are similar to many rows of $Q$, analogous to a statistical density estimator.
section_path: Transport based embeddings with topological guarantees

questions.doc_title: Transport based embeddings with topological guarantees
questions.question: How does the AlphaKL pipeline convert a Euclidean point cloud into the positive stochastic matrix Q used by its transport construction, specifically how is each per-point scale t_i chosen in the stochastic-neighbors random walk?
questions.question_ru: Как конвейер AlphaKL преобразует евклидово облако точек в положительную стохастическую матрицу Q, используемую в его транспортной конструкции, и, в частности, как выбирается каждый масштаб t_i в случайном блуждании по стохастическим соседям?
questions.reference_answer: It starts with the first step of the t-SNE algorithm: from scales $t_{i}$ a random-walk transition matrix $P$ is formed whose $i$th row is $p_{i\bullet}=[\exp(-t_{i}\lVert x_{i}-x_{j}\rVert^{2})]_{j=1}^{n}$, normalized to sum to one, with the diagonal $p_{ii}$ set to zero before normalization. For a target entropy $H>0$ the unique scale $t_{i}$ is selected so that $p_{i\bullet}$ has entropy $H$.

evidence.text:
Starting with a point cloud $\mathcal{D}=\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we first generate a Markov chain using stochastic neighbors, which is the first step of the $t$-SNE algorithm [15] defined as follows. Given a vector of scales $t=(t_{i})_{i=1}^{n}$, let $P=(p_{ij})$ be the transition matrix of a random walk whose $i$th row is

$$
p_{i\bullet}=\bigl[\exp(-t_{i}\lVert x_{i}-x_{j}\rVert^{2})\bigr]_{j=1}^{n}, \tag{4.1}
$$

after normalizing the row to sum to one. We will also use the convention of setting the diagonal entry $p_{ii}$ to zero before normalization. Given an entropy value $H>0$, we then select the unique scale $t_{i}$ which arranges that $p_{i\bullet}$ has entropy $H$.

questions.question: In the SYMSOL tetrahedron pose-estimation experiment using all 45,000 images with the coarse-grained Markov chain, what Betti numbers were computed over Z/3 and over Z/2, and what topology do these values match?

questions.reference_answer: Over $\mathbb{Z}/3$ the first three Betti numbers through dimension two were $(1,1,1)$, while over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ they were $(1,0,0)$. These values are consistent with the expected topology of $SO(3)/A_{4}$, where $A_{4}$ is the rotational symmetry group of the tetrahedron.

evidence.text: From the resulting data we constructed an alpha complex and computed its homology. The first three Betti numbers over $\mathbb{Z}/3$ were $(1,1,1)$ through dimension two, while over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ they were $(1,0,0)$, which is consistent with the expected topology of $SO(3)/A_{4}$, where $A_{4}$ is the rotational symmetry group of the tetrahedron. Using Javaplex in MATLAB, one can reconstruct representatives of these one-cycles over $\mathbb{Z}/3$ from the vertices of the alpha complex and animate the corresponding sequence of tetrahedral views. Along such a cycle, one corner maps to itself, while the other three rotate in a cycle.

questions.doc_title: Optimizing persistent homology based functions
questions.question: In the framework for optimizing persistence-based functions, what permutation-invariance property must a real-valued function E of a persistence diagram satisfy in order to be called a "function of persistence"?
questions.question_ru: В рамках оптимизации функций, основанных на персистентности, каким свойством инвариантности к перестановкам должна обладать вещественнозначная функция E от диаграммы персистентности, чтобы называться «функцией персистентности» (function of persistence)?
questions.reference_answer: E must be invariant to permutations of the points of the persistence diagram: for any permutation α of the p finite points and any permutation β of the q essential coordinates, one must have E(p_{α(1)},...,p_{α(p)},e_{β(1)},...,e_{β(q)}) = E(p_1,...,p_p,e_1,...,e_q).

evidence.text:
**Definition 4.1.** A function $E\colon\mathbb{R}^{|K|}=(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{p}\times\mathbb{R}^{q}\to\mathbb{R}$ is said to be a *function of persistence* if it is invariant to permutations of the points of the persistence diagram: for any $(p_{1},\dots,p_{p},e_{1},\dots,e_{q})\in(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{p}\times\mathbb{R}^{q}$ and any permutations $\alpha,\beta$ of the sets $\{1,\dots,p\}$ and $\{1,\dots,q\}$, respectively, one has

$$
E(p_{\alpha(1)},\dots,p_{\alpha(p)},e_{\beta(1)},\dots,e_{\beta(q)})=E(p_{1},\dots,p_{p},e_{1},\dots,e_{q}).
$$

questions.doc_title: Optimizing persistent homology based functions
questions.question: After the persistence-pairing algorithm has produced a set of paired simplices and a set of unpaired simplices from a filtering function Φ, how is the persistence diagram constructed from them, and how many finite and infinite points does it contain?
questions.question_ru: После того как алгоритм вычисления пар персистентности построил множество спаренных и неспаренных симплексов по функции фильтрации, как по ним строится диаграмма персистентности и сколько конечных и бесконечных точек она содержит?
questions.reference_answer: Each persistent pair (σ_{l(j)}, σ_j) is mapped to the finite point (Φ_{σ_{l(j)}}, Φ_{σ_j}), and each unpaired simplex σ_l is mapped to the point (Φ_{σ_l}, +∞). With p persistence pairs and q unpaired simplices (so |K| = 2p+q), the diagram D(Φ) consists of p points in R^2 counted with multiplicity and q points, also counted with multiplicity, with infinite second coordinate.

evidence.text:
The persistence diagram of the filter function $\Phi$ is now obtained by associating to each persistent pair $(\sigma_{l(j)},\sigma_{j})$ the point $(\Phi_{\sigma_{l(j)}},\Phi_{\sigma_{j}})$. Moreover, to each unpaired simplex $\sigma_{l}$ is associated the point $(\Phi_{\sigma_{l}},+\infty)$.

If $p$ is the number of persistence pairs and $q$ is the number of unpaired simplices, then $|K|=2p+q$ and the persistence diagram $D(\Phi)$ of the filtration $\Phi$ of $K$ is made of $p$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ (counted with multiplicity) and $q$ points (also counted with multiplicity) with infinite second coordinate.

questions.question: What are the three assumptions on the learning rates and random perturbations under which the stochastic subgradient iterations x_{k+1}=x_k−α_k(y_k+ζ_k) converge almost surely to a critical point of a locally Lipschitz persistence-based loss?
questions.question_ru: Каковы три предположения относительно скоростей обучения и случайных возмущений, при которых итерации стохастического субградиента x_{k+1}=x_k−α_k(y_k+ζ_k) почти наверное сходятся к критической точке локально липшицевой функции потерь, основанной на персистентности?
questions.reference_answer: (1) α_k ≥ 0, Σ_k α_k = +∞ and Σ_k α_k^2 < +∞; (2) sup_k ||x_k|| < +∞ almost surely; and (3) denoting by F_k the increasing sequence of σ-algebras F_k = σ(x_j, y_j, ζ_j, j<k), there exists a function p from R^d to R bounded on bounded sets such that almost surely E[ζ_k|F_k] = 0 and E[||ζ_k||^2|F_k] < p(x_k).

questions.doc_title: Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport
questions.question: In the context of minibatch optimal transport with batch size $N$, what does it mean for a set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and for a transport plan $\gamma$ to be $N$-cyclically monotone?
questions.question_ru: В контексте минибатчевого оптимального транспорта с размером батча $N$, что означает, что множество $A\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ и транспортный план $\gamma$ являются $N$-циклически монотонными?
questions.reference_answer: A set $A$ is $N$-cyclically monotone for $N\geq 2$ if for all $(x^{(i)},y^{(i)})\in A$ and every permutation $\tau\in\Sigma_{N}$, the squared distances satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|x^{(i)}-y^{(i)}\|^{2}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|x^{(i)}-y^{(\tau(i))}\|^{2}$. A transport plan $\gamma\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is $N$-cyclically monotone if its support is.

evidence.text:
**Definition 6.** We call a set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ $N$-cyclically monotone for $N\geq 2$ if it holds for all $(x^{(i)},y^{(i)})\in A$ and $\tau\in\Sigma_{N}$ that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|x^{(i)}-y^{(i)}\|^{2}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|x^{(i)}-y^{(\tau(i))}\|^{2}.
$$

Similarly, we call a transport plan $\gamma\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})$ $N$-cyclically monotone if $\mathrm{supp}(\gamma)$ is $N$-cyclically monotone.

questions.doc_title: Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport
questions.question: Which two problems of the reflow procedure (iteratively recomputing the rectified coupling) prevent its limit points from necessarily giving a one-step generation model?
questions.question_ru: Какие две проблемы процедуры reflow (итеративного пересчёта выпрямляющей связи) не позволяют её предельным точкам гарантированно давать одношаговую генеративную модель?
questions.reference_answer: The first problem is that limit points of reflow are not necessarily rectifiable: the coupling defined by $\int\psi(x,y)\mathrm{d}\gamma(x,y)=\int\psi(x,-x)\mathrm{d}\mathcal{N}(0,I)(x)$ fulfills $\gamma\in\mathcal{R}(\gamma)$ and is therefore a limit point of reflow. The second is that the loss function $\min_{v_{t}\in L^{2}(\mu_{t})}\mathcal{L}(v_{t}|\gamma)$ is not lower semicontinuous, so one cannot conclude that reflow limit points are straight couplings.

evidence.text:
They show that the loss function $\min_{v_{t}\in L^{2}(\mu_{t,n})}\mathcal{L}(v_{t}|\gamma_{n})$ converges to zero. However, we point out two problems, which show that this does not necessarily lead to a one-step generation model in the limit.

First, limit points of reflow are not necessarily rectifiable. An example is given by the coupling defined by $\int\psi(x,y)\mathrm{d}\gamma(x,y)=\int\psi(x,-x)\mathrm{d}\mathcal{N}(0,I)(x)$ which was considered in [13, Section 4.2] as an example for non-rectifiable couplings, see also Appendix B.1. This coupling fulfills $\gamma\in\mathcal{R}(\gamma)$ and is consequently also a limit point of reflow.

Second, the loss function $\min_{v_{t}\in L^{2}(\mu_{t})}\mathcal{L}(v_{t}|\gamma)$ is not lower semicontinuous. In particular, we cannot conclude that limit points of the sequence $(\gamma_{n})_{n}$ in the reflow algorithm are really straight couplings.

questions.question: Under which conditions is an $N$-cyclically monotone coupling $\gamma$ between $\mu_{0}$ and $\mu_{1}$ guaranteed to be an optimal transport plan when the velocities are additionally constrained to be gradients?
questions.question_ru: При каких условиях $N$-циклически монотонная связь $\gamma$ между $\mu_{0}$ и $\mu_{1}$ гарантированно оказывается оптимальным транспортным планом, если скорости дополнительно ограничены градиентами?
questions.reference_answer: If $\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})$ with $\mu_{0},\mu_{1}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is $N$-cyclically monotone, fulfills $\min_{w_{t}\in\mathrm{T}_{\mu_{t}}}\mathcal{L}(w_{t}|\gamma)=0$ for the interpolations $\mu_{t}$ from (2), and if for some $t\in(0,1)$ the measure $\mu_{t}$ is absolutely continuous with $\mu_{t}^{-1}\in L^{1}_{\textup{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, then $\gamma$ is an optimal transport plan between $\mu_{0}$ and $\mu_{1}$.

evidence.text: **Theorem 16.** Let $\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})$ for $\mu_{0},\mu_{1}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ be $N$-cyclically monotone and assume that it fulfills $\min_{w_{t}\in\mathrm{T}_{\mu_{t}}}\mathcal{L}(w_{t}|\gamma)=0$ for the interpolations $\mu_{t}$ from (2). Further, assume that there exists some $t\in(0,1)$ such that $\mu_{t}$ is absolutely continuous and that $\mu_{t}^{-1}\in L^{1}_{\textup{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$. Then, $\gamma$ is an optimal transport plan between $\mu_{0}$ and $\mu_{1}$.

questions.question: In topological data analysis, define the α-witness complex C_W^α(L) of a landmark set L relative to a witness set W: what does it mean for a point w ∈ W to α-witness a k-simplex σ with vertices in L, and how is the complex itself defined?
questions.question_ru: В топологическом анализе данных дайте определение α-свидетельского комплекса C_W^α(L) набора ориентиров L относительно набора свидетелей W: что означает, что точка w ∈ W является α-свидетелем k-симплекса σ с вершинами в L, и как определяется сам комплекс?
questions.reference_answer: A point w ∈ W is an α-witness of a k-simplex σ with vertices in L if the vertices of σ lie within Euclidean distance d_k(w) + α of w, where d_k(w) is the Euclidean distance from w to its (k+1)-th nearest landmark. The α-witness complex C_W^α(L) is the maximum abstract simplicial complex with vertices in L whose faces are α-witnessed by points of W.

evidence.text:
- Given a point $w\in W$ and a $k$-simplex $\sigma$ with vertices in ${L}$, $w$ is an $\alpha$*-witness* of $\sigma$ (or, equivalently, $w$ $\alpha$*-witnesses* $\sigma$) if the vertices of $\sigma$ lie within Euclidean distance $({\rm d}_{k}(w)+\alpha)$ of $w$, where ${\rm d}_{k}(w)$ denotes the Euclidean distance between $w$ and its $(k+1)$th nearest landmark in the Euclidean metric.
- The $\alpha$*-witness complex* of ${L}$ *relative to* $W$, or ${\cal C}_{W}^{\alpha}({L})$ for short, is the maximum abstract simplicial complex, with vertices in ${L}$, whose faces are $\alpha$-witnessed by points of $W$.

questions.question: Let X ⊂ R^d be a compact set and L a finite point set whose Hausdorff distance to X satisfies d_H(X, L) < ε for some ε < (1/4) wfs(X). For which ranges of the scales α and α' does the image of the homomorphism induced by the inclusion C^α(L) ↪ C^{α'}(L) recover the homology of the offset X^λ, and what exactly is the statement?
questions.question_ru: Пусть X ⊂ R^d — компакт, а L — конечное множество точек, расстояние Хаусдорфа от которого до X удовлетворяет d_H(X, L) < ε для некоторого ε < (1/4) wfs(X). Для каких диапазонов масштабов α и α' образ гомоморфизма, индуцированного включением C^α(L) ↪ C^{α'}(L), восстанавливает гомологии смещения X^λ, и в чём состоит точная формулировка?
questions.reference_answer: For all α, α' ∈ [ε, wfs(X) − ε] with α' − α > 2ε, and for all λ ∈ (0, wfs(X)), one has H_k(X^λ) ≅ im j_* for every k, where j_* is the homomorphism induced by the inclusion C^α(L) ↪ C^{α'}(L); the same result holds for homotopy groups with base-point x_0 ∈ X.

evidence.text: **Theorem 3.5** Let $X$ be a compact set and ${L}$ a finite set in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, such that ${\rm d}_{\cal H}(X,{L})<\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon<\frac{1}{4}\;{\rm wfs}(X)$. Then, for all $\alpha,\alpha^{\prime}\in\left[\varepsilon,{\rm wfs}(X)-\varepsilon\right]$ such that $\alpha^{\prime}-\alpha>2\varepsilon$, and for all $\lambda\in\left(0,{\rm wfs}(X)\right)$, we have: $\forall k\in\mathbb{N}$, $H_{k}(X^{\lambda})\cong{\rm im}\;j_{*}$, where $j_{*}:H_{k}({\cal C}^{\alpha}({L}))\rightarrow H_{k}({\cal C}^{\alpha^{\prime}}({L}))$ is the homomorphism between homology groups induced by the canonical inclusion $j:{\cal C}^{\alpha}({L})\hookrightarrow{\cal C}^{\alpha^{\prime}}({L})$. Given an arbitrary point $x_{0}\in X$, the same result holds for homotopy groups with base-point $x_{0}$.

questions.doc_title: Towards Persistence-Based Reconstruction in Euclidean Spaces
questions.question: Describe the greedy-refinement reconstruction algorithm that processes a finite point cloud W in an arbitrary metric space: how is a new landmark selected at each iteration, how is the scale ε updated, which complexes and which quantity are maintained, and when does the process stop?
questions.question_ru: Опишите алгоритм реконструкции на основе жадного уточнения, обрабатывающий конечное облако точек W в произвольном метрическом пространстве: как выбирается новый ориентир на каждой итерации, как обновляется масштаб ε, какие комплексы и какая величина поддерживаются и когда процесс останавливается?
questions.reference_answer: Starting from L = ∅ and ε = +∞, each iteration inserts into L the point of W lying farthest from L in the metric, sets ε to max over W of the distance to the nearest landmark, updates R^{4ε}(L) and R^{16ε}(L), and computes the persistent homology of R^{4ε}(L) ↪ R^{16ε}(L) with the persistence algorithm. It terminates when L = W and outputs the diagram of the evolution of persistent Betti numbers versus ε.

evidence.text:
The input is a finite point set $W$ drawn from an arbitrary metric space, together with the pairwise distances $l(w,w^{\prime})$ between the points of $W$. In the sequel, $W$ is identified as the set of witnesses.

Initially, ${L}=\emptyset$ and $\varepsilon=+\infty$. At each iteration, the point of $W$ lying furthest away \[Footnote: At the first iteration, since ${L}$ is empty, an arbitrary point of $W$ is chosen.\] from ${L}$ in the metric $l$ is inserted in ${L}$, and $\varepsilon$ is set to $\max_{w\in W}\min_{v\in{L}}l(w,v)$. Then, ${\cal R}^{4\varepsilon}({L})$ and ${\cal R}^{16\varepsilon}({L})$ are updated, and the persistent homology of ${\cal R}^{4\varepsilon}({L})\hookrightarrow{\cal R}^{16\varepsilon}({L})$ is computed using the persistence algorithm [38]. The algorithm terminates when ${L}=W$. The output is the diagram showing the evolution of the persistent Betti numbers versus $\varepsilon$, which have been maintained throughout the process.

questions.question: In the theory of multivalued maps between filtered simplicial complexes, how is an ε-simplicial multivalued map defined, and what condition must the image of a simplex satisfy?
questions.question_ru: В теории многозначных отображений между фильтрованными симплициальными комплексами как определяется ε-симплициальное многозначное отображение и какому условию должен удовлетворять образ симплекса?
questions.reference_answer: Given filtered simplicial complexes S and T with vertex sets X and Y, a multivalued map C: X ⇉ Y is ε-simplicial from S to T if for every a and every simplex σ in S_a, every finite subset of the image C(σ) is a simplex of T_{a+ε}.

evidence.text: **Definition 3.2.** Let ${\mathbb{S}}$ and ${\mathbb{T}}$ be two filtered simplicial complexes with vertex sets $X$ and $Y$ respectively. A multivalued map $C:X\rightrightarrows Y$ is $\varepsilon$**-simplicial** from ${\mathbb{S}}$ to ${\mathbb{T}}$ if for any $a\in{\mathbf{R}}$ and any simplex $\sigma\in{\mathbb{S}}_{a}$, every finite subset of $C(\sigma)$ is a simplex of ${\mathbb{T}}_{a+\varepsilon}$.

questions.question: Why is there no equivalent stability result for the witness complex when the landmark set is perturbed while the witness set is fixed, and what explicit counterexample demonstrates this?

**Example 4.14.** On the real line, consider the sets $W=L=\{0,1\}$ and $L^{\prime}=\{-\delta,0,1,1+\delta\}$, where $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ is arbitrary. Then

$$
\operatorname{\mathrm{Wit}}(L,W;a)=\{[0],\ [1],\ [0,1]\}
$$

for all $a\geq 0$, whereas

$$
\operatorname{\mathrm{Wit}}(L^{\prime},W;a)=\{[-\delta],\ [0],\ [1],\ [1+\delta],\ [-\delta,0],\ [1,1+\delta]\}
$$

for all $a\in[\delta,1-\delta)$. Thus, $\operatorname{H}(\operatorname{\mathbb{W}\mathrm{it}}(L,W))$ and $\operatorname{H}(\operatorname{\mathbb{W}\mathrm{it}}(L^{\prime},W))$ are not $\varepsilon$-interleaved for any $\varepsilon<1-2\delta$, whereas $\mathrm{d_{H}}(L,L^{\prime})=\delta$ can be made arbitrarily small compared to $1-2\delta$.

questions.question: How are the Vietoris-Rips complex and the Čech complex of a metric space defined at a scale α, and what inclusion relation holds between them and the Vietoris-Rips complex at scale 2α?
questions.question_ru: Как определяются комплекс Виеториса–Рипса и комплекс Чеха метрического пространства на масштабе α и какое соотношение включения между ними и комплексом Виеториса–Рипса на масштабе 2α выполняется?
questions.reference_answer: At scale α the Vietoris-Rips complex consists of the simplices [x0,…,xk] whose points are pairwise at distance at most α, while the Čech complex consists of the simplices whose k+1 closed balls B(xi,α) have a non-empty intersection. The two are related by Rips_α(X) ⊆ Cech_α(X) ⊆ Rips_{2α}(X), and both depend only on the pairwise distances between the points of X.

evidence.text: Given a metric space $\mathbb{X}$ which will also serve as the vertex set, the *Vietoris-Rips complex* $\operatorname{\mathrm{Rips}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$ is the set of simplices $[x_{0},\ldots,x_{k}]$ such that $d_{\mathbb{X}}(x_{i},x_{j})\leq\alpha$ for all $(i,j)$. The *Čech complex* $\operatorname{\mathrm{Cech}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$ is similarly defined as the set of simplices $[x_{0},\ldots,x_{k}]$ such that the $k+1$ closed balls $B(x_{i},\alpha)$ have a non-empty intersection. Note that these two complexes are related by $\operatorname{\mathrm{Rips}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})\subseteq\operatorname{\mathrm{Cech}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})\subseteq\operatorname{\mathrm{Rips}}_{2\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$. Note also that these two families of complexes only depend on the pairwise distances between the points of $\mathbb{X}$.

questions.question: When the ambient metric space M is unknown and the observations are known only through their pairwise distances, why is it useful to estimate the support using the Gromov-Hausdorff distance rather than relying on an embedding?
questions.question_ru: Когда объемлющее метрическое пространство M неизвестно, а наблюдения известны лишь через попарные расстояния, почему полезно оценивать носитель с помощью расстояния Громова–Хаусдорфа, а не опираясь на вложение?
questions.reference_answer: Estimating the support X_μ as an element of the space K of isometry classes of compact metric spaces is of practical interest because in some applications the ambient space M is unknown and the observations X_1,…,X_n are known only through their pairwise distances ρ(X_i,X_j). Using the Gromov-Hausdorff distance then allows one to treat the sample as an abstract metric space of cardinality n, independently of how it is embedded in M.

evidence.text: Note that this general strategy of estimating $\mathbb{X}_{\mu}$ in $\mathcal{K}$ is not only of theoretical interest. Indeed as mentioned in the introduction, in some cases the space $\mathbb{M}$ is unknown and the observations $X_{1}\dots,X_{n}$ are just known through their matrix of pairwise distances $\rho(X_{i},X_{j})$, $i,j=1,\cdots,n$. The use of the Gromov-Hausdorff distance then allows to consider this set of observations as an abstract metric space of cardinality $n$ without taking care of the way it is embedded in $\mathbb{M}$.

questions.question: In the numerical experiment on the rotating shape space M_4 built from grayscale images of a 3D character, how many point sets were sampled, which complex was used, and what topological features appear in the persistence diagrams?
questions.question_ru: В численном эксперименте на пространстве вращающихся форм M_4, построенном из полутоновых изображений 3D-персонажа, сколько наборов точек было выбрано, какой комплекс использовался и какие топологические особенности появляются на диаграммах персистентности?
questions.reference_answer: The 1-dimensional homology persistence diagrams of the Vietoris-Rips filtrations were computed on 20 sets of 250 points each randomly sampled on M_4. Because M_4 consists of images taken from a rotating viewpoint it carries a cycle structure: all diagrams have one point clearly off the diagonal (this cycle), plus a second point much closer to the diagonal that probably corresponds to a pinching visible at the bottom left of the MDS projection.

evidence.text: **Results for $\mathbb{M}_{4}$:** As in that case we do not know the persistence diagram of the Vietoris-Rips filtration built on top of $\mathbb{M}_{4}$, we only computed the $1$-dimensional homology persistence diagrams of the Vietoris-Rips filtrations built on top of $20$ sets of $250$ points each, randomly sampled on $\mathbb{M}_{4}$. All these diagrams have been plotted on the same Figure 11, left. The right of Figure 11 represents a 2D embedding of one of the $250$ points sampled data set using the Multidimensional Scaling algorithm (MDS). Since $\mathbb{M}_{4}$ is a set of images taken according a rotating point of view, it carries a cycle structure. This structure is reflected in the persistence diagrams that all have one point which is clearly off the diagonal. Notice also a second point off the diagonal which is much closer to it and that probably corresponds to the pinching in $\mathbb{M}_{4}$ visible at the bottom left of the MDS projection.

questions.doc_title: Persistence-Based Clustering in Riemannian Manifolds
questions.question: For a finite point cloud L in a metric space with distance dX, how is the Rips graph Rδ(L, dX) defined for a parameter δ > 0, and which pairs of points are connected by its edges?
questions.question_ru: Пусть задано конечное облако точек L в метрическом пространстве с расстоянием dX. Как определяется граф Рипса Rδ(L, dX) для параметра δ > 0 и какие пары точек соединяются его рёбрами?
questions.reference_answer: Given a finite point cloud L in a metric space (X, dX) and a parameter δ > 0, the Rips graph Rδ(L, dX) is the graph whose vertex set is L and whose edges correspond to the pairs of points x, y ∈ L such that dX(x, y) ≤ δ.

evidence.text: Definition 2.1 Given a finite point cloud L in a metric space (X, dX), and a parameter δ > 0, the Rips graph Rδ(L, dX) is the graph of vertex set L whose edges correspond to the pairs of points x, y ∈ L such that dX(x, y) ≤ δ.

questions.question: In mode-seeking density-based clustering such as Mean-Shift, why is it problematic to directly study the gradient flow and extremal points of the density function f, and what difficulty arises because the true density is unknown?
questions.question_ru: В кластеризации методом поиска мод по плотности, например в Mean-Shift, почему проблематично напрямую изучать градиентный поток и экстремальные точки функции плотности f и какая трудность возникает из-за того, что истинная плотность неизвестна?
questions.reference_answer: The gradient flow and extremal points of the density are differential quantities that are notoriously unstable under even arbitrarily small perturbations of f, and since the true density f is usually unknown, one must rely on an estimator f̃ whose basins of attraction are very unlikely to coincide with those of the true density.

evidence.text: A common problem faced by these methods is that the gradient flow and extremal points of the density function f are differential quantities that are notoriously unstable under (even arbitrarily small) perturbations of f . Since f remains usually unknown to us, we are dependent on an estimator f<sup>˜</sup> , whose basins of attraction are very unlikely to coincide with the ones of the true density.

questions.doc_title: Subsampling Methods for Persistent Homology
questions.question: In the multiple-samples approach to persistent homology, how is the closest-sample landscape estimator defined from n independent samples of size m, and in which distance is closeness to the support measured?
questions.question_ru: В подходе многократных выборок для персистентной гомологии как определяется оценка ландшафта по ближайшей выборке из n независимых выборок размера m и в каком расстоянии измеряется близость к носителю?
questions.reference_answer: Among n independent samples S_1^m, ..., S_n^m of size m from μ^{⊗m}, the closest sample is Ĉ_n^m = argmin over S of H(S, X_μ), i.e. the sample minimizing the Hausdorff distance to the support X_μ; the corresponding landscape estimator is λ̂_n^m = λ_{Ĉ_n^m}.

evidence.text:
In addition to the average, we also consider using the *closest sample* to $\mathbb{X}_{\mu}$ in Hausdorff distance. The closest sample method consists in choosing a sample of $m$ points of $\mathbb{X}$, as close as possible to $\mathbb{X}_{\mu}$, and then use this sample to build a landscape that approximates $\lambda_{{\mathbb{X}_{\mu}}}$. Let $S_{1}^{m},\dots,S_{n}^{m}$ be $n$ independent samples of size $m$ from $\mu^{\otimes m}$. The closest sample is

$$
\widehat{C^{m}_{n}}=\arg\min_{S\in\{S_{1}^{m},\dots,S_{n}^{m}\}}H(S,X_{\mu}) \tag{5}
$$

and the corresponding landscape function is $\widehat{\lambda_{n}^{m}}=\lambda_{{\widehat{C^{m}_{n}}}}.$

questions.doc_title: Subsampling Methods for Persistent Homology
questions.question: What is the computational complexity of computing the persistent homology of a full point cloud X_N, of computing the average landscape from n subsamples of size m, and of computing the persistent homology of the closest sample?
questions.question_ru: Какова вычислительная сложность вычисления персистентной гомологии полного облака точек X_N, вычисления среднего ландшафта по n подвыборкам размера m и вычисления персистентной гомологии ближайшей выборки?
questions.reference_answer: Computing the persistent homology of X_N is O(exp(N)); computing the average landscape is O(n exp(m)); and computing the persistent homology of the closest sample is O(nmN + exp(m)).

evidence.text:
Of course, the method requires the support of $\mu$ to be a known quantity.

**Remark 2.** Computing the persistent homology of $X_{N}$ is $O(\exp(N))$, whereas computing the average landscape is $O(n\exp(m))$ and the persistent homology of the closest sample is $O(nmN+\exp(m))$.

questions.doc_title: Subsampling Methods for Persistent Homology
questions.question: How do the risks of the closest-subsample estimator and the average-landscape estimator compare, including their convergence rates when r_0 is negligible, and which of the two is robust to outliers?
questions.question_ru: Как соотносятся риски оценки по ближайшей подвыборке и оценки среднего ландшафта, включая их скорости сходимости при пренебрежимо малом r_0, и какая из двух оценок устойчива к выбросам?
questions.reference_answer: The risk of the closest-subsample method can in principle be smaller than that of the average landscape; for the discrete uniform μ sampled from an (a,b,0)-standard measure, r_0 is of the order (log N / N)^{1/b}, and when r_0 is negligible the rates of Theorems 8 and 9 are comparable, both of order O((log m / m)^{1/b}); however, the average method is robust to outliers.

evidence.text: **Remark 10.** The risk of the closest subsample method can in principle be smaller than the average landscape method. In Appendix C we show that if $\mu$ is the discrete uniform measure on a point cloud of size $N$, sampled from a measure satisfying the $(a,b,0)$-standard assumption, then $r_{0}$ is of the order of $(\frac{\log N}{N})^{1/b}$. When $r_{0}$ is negligible, the rates of theorems 8 and 9 are comparable, both of the order of $O(\frac{\log m}{m})^{1/b}$. However, the average method has another advantage: it is robust to outliers. This point is discussed in detail in Appendix D.

questions.doc_title: An introduction to Topological Data Analysis: fundamental and practical aspects for data scientists
questions.question: In topological data analysis, what conditions must a cover of a topological space satisfy for the Nerve Theorem to hold, and what does the theorem conclude about the space and the nerve of the cover? What does this imply for the Čech complex of a finite point set and the union of balls?
questions.question_ru: В топологическом анализе данных каким условиям должно удовлетворять покрытие топологического пространства, чтобы выполнялась теорема о нерве, и что эта теорема утверждает о пространстве и нерве покрытия? Что из этого следует для комплекса Чеха $\operatorname{\mathrm{Cech}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$ конечного множества точек и объединения шаров?
questions.reference_answer: Under the condition that a cover $\mathcal{U}=(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ of $X$ consists of open sets whose intersections of any subcollection are either empty or contractible, the Nerve Theorem states that $X$ and its nerve $C(\mathcal{U})$ are homotopy equivalent. In particular, since convex sets are contractible, the Čech complex $\operatorname{\mathrm{Cech}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$ of a point set is homotopy equivalent to the union of balls $\cup_{x\in\mathbb{X}}B(x,\alpha)$.

evidence.text:
**Theorem 1 (Nerve theorem).** Let $\mathcal{U}=(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ be a cover of a topological space $X$ by open sets such that the intersection of any subcollection of the $U_{i}$’s is either empty or contractible. Then, $X$ and the nerve $C(\mathcal{U})$ are homotopy equivalent.

It is easy to verify that convex subsets of Euclidean spaces are contractible. As a consequence, if $\mathcal{U}=(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a collection of convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ then $C(\mathcal{U})$ and $\cup_{i\in I}U_{i}$ are homotopy equivalent. In particular, if $\mathbb{X}$ is a set of points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, then the Čech complex $\operatorname{\mathrm{Cech}}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{X})$ is homotopy equivalent to the union of balls $\cup_{x\in\mathbb{X}}B(x,\alpha)$.

questions.doc_title: An introduction to Topological Data Analysis: fundamental and practical aspects for data scientists
questions.question: In the Mapper algorithm applied with a real-valued filter function, what are the "resolution" and "gain" parameters of the cover and how do they control the output? What happens to the output nerve when the gain is chosen below 50%, and why is the Mapper output considered unstable with respect to these parameters?
questions.question_ru: В алгоритме Mapper с вещественной функцией-фильтром что представляют собой параметры покрытия «resolution» и «gain» и как они управляют результатом? Что происходит с выходным нервом, если gain выбран ниже $50\%$, и почему результат Mapper считается неустойчивым к выбору этих параметров?
questions.reference_answer: The resolution $r$ is the common length of the regularly spaced intervals forming the cover of $f(\mathbb{X})$, and the gain $g$ is the percentage of overlap between two consecutive intervals. If $g$ is below $50\%$ every point of the real line is covered by at most two open sets and the resulting nerve is a graph. The Mapper output is very sensitive to $\mathcal{U}$: small changes in resolution and gain can cause very large changes, so a standard strategy is to explore a range of parameters and select the most informative output.

evidence.text: When $f$ is a real valued function, a standard choice is to take $\mathcal{U}$ to be a set of regularly spaced intervals of equal length $r>0$ covering the set $f(\mathbb{X})$. The real $r$ is sometimes called the *resolution* of the cover and the percentage $g$ of overlap between two consecutive intervals is called the the *gain* of the cover. Note that if the gain $g$ is chosen below $50\%$, then every point of the real line is covered by at most 2 open sets of $\mathcal{U}$ and the output nerve is a graph. It is important to notice that the output of the Mapper is very sensitive to the choice of $\mathcal{U}$ and small changes in the resolution and gain parameters may results in very large changes in the output, making the method very unstable. A classical strategy consists in exploring some range of parameters and select the ones that turn out to provide the most informative output from the user perspective.
