questions.doc_title: An introduction to Topological Data Analysis: fundamental and practical aspects for data scientists
questions.question: Why is the plain distance function to a point cloud unreliable for topological data analysis in the presence of outliers, and how is the distance-to-a-measure $\delta_{P,u}$ defined for a probability distribution $P$?
questions.question_ru: Почему обычная функция расстояния до облака точек ненадёжна для топологического анализа данных при наличии выбросов, и как определяется расстояние до меры $\delta_{P,u}$ для вероятностного распределения $P$?
questions.reference_answer: The distance function to a point cloud can change dramatically when even a single outlier is added, so distance-based methods fail completely in the presence of outliers. The distance-to-a-measure is defined for a distribution $P$ and a parameter $0\leq u\leq 1$ by $\delta_{P,u}(x)=\inf\{t>0\,;\,P(B(x,t))\geq u\}$, the smallest radius $t$ such that the closed Euclidean ball $B(x,t)$ has probability at least $u$ under $P$.

evidence.text:
It is well known that distance-based methods in tda may fail completely in the presence of outliers. Indeed, adding even a single outlier to the point cloud can change the distance function dramatically, see Figure 8 for an illustration. To answer this drawback, Chazal et al., 2011b have introduced an alternative distance function which is robust to noise, the *distance-to-a-measure*.

Given a probability distribution $P$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and a real parameter $0\leq u\leq 1$, the notion of distance to the support of $P$ may be generalized as the function

$$
\delta_{P,u}:x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\mapsto\inf\{t>0\,;\,P(B(x,t))\geq u\},
$$

where $B(x,t)$ is the closed Euclidean ball of center $x$ and radius $t$.

questions.doc_title: Local Distance Preserving Auto-encoders using Continuous k-Nearest Neighbours Graphs
questions.question: In the continuous k-nearest neighbours (CkNN) graph construction used for local-distance-preserving auto-encoders, how is the connectivity between two data points x_i and x_j of a batch X_b defined in terms of their pairwise distance and their kNN radii, and what does the condition simplify to when the parameter δ equals 1?
questions.question_ru: В построении графа непрерывных k ближайших соседей (CkNN), используемом для автоэнкодеров, сохраняющих локальные расстояния, как определяется связность между двумя точками данных x_i и x_j батча X_b через их попарное расстояние и их kNN-радиусы, и во что упрощается условие, когда параметр δ равен 1?
questions.reference_answer: The CkNN graph over X_b includes the pair (i,j) when d_X(x_i,x_j)^2 ≤ δ^2 · d(x_i, x_{κ(x_i;k,X_b)}) · d(x_j, x_{κ(x_j;k,X_b)}); for δ = 1 two points are connected if their distance is smaller than the geometric mean of their kNN radii.

evidence.text:
Let $\kappa(x;k,X_{b})$ be the index of the k-th nearest neighbour of $x$ in $X_{b}$. Then the CkNN graph over the set $X_{b}$ is defined via the connectivity (Berry & Sauer 2019)

$$
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{X_{b}}(\delta,k)=\big\{(i,j):d_{X}(x_{i},x_{j})^{2}\leq\delta^{2}\>d(x_{i},x_{\kappa(x_{i};k,X_{b})})\>d(x_{j},x_{\kappa(x_{j};k,X_{b})}),\kern 5.0ptx_{i},x_{j}\in X_{b}\big\}.
$$

In other words, for $\delta=1$, two points are connected if their distance is smaller than the geometric mean of they kNN radius/distance.

questions.doc_title: Local Distance Preserving Auto-encoders using Continuous k-Nearest Neighbours Graphs
questions.question: How does the computational cost of constructing the continuous k-nearest neighbours (CkNN) graph compare with that of the Vietoris–Rips-based graph used in topological auto-encoders, in terms of big-O complexity in the batch size?
questions.question_ru: Как вычислительная стоимость построения графа непрерывных k ближайших соседей (CkNN) соотносится со стоимостью графа на основе комплексов Вьеториса–Рипса, используемого в топологических автоэнкодерах, с точки зрения асимптотической сложности по размеру батча?
questions.reference_answer: VR requires computing a minimum spanning tree on the full distance matrix, costing O(n_batch^2 log n_batch), whereas CkNN only needs the smallest k distances for each node, costing O(n_batch^2 log k) and being highly parallelisable, so CkNN is significantly faster.

evidence.text: An additional advantage of CkNN is that it seems to be significantly faster to compute when compared to VR. For VR the computation of the minimum spanning tree is required on the (full) distance matrix resulting in $\mathcal{O}(n_{\mathrm{batch}}^{2}\log n_{\mathrm{batch}})$ while for CkNN we only need to compute the smallest $k$ distances for each node, this is only $\mathcal{O}(n_{\mathrm{batch}}^{2}\log k)$ and is also highly paralleliseable.

questions.doc_title: Local Distance Preserving Auto-encoders using Continuous k-Nearest Neighbours Graphs
questions.question: Why was the training of local-distance-preserving auto-encoders and variational auto-encoders formulated as a constrained optimisation problem (with one loss as the objective and the others as constraints) rather than as a weighted sum of regularisers?
questions.question_ru: Почему обучение автоэнкодеров и вариационных автоэнкодеров, сохраняющих локальные расстояния, было сформулировано как задача ограниченной оптимизации (с одной функцией потерь в качестве цели, а остальными — в качестве ограничений), а не как взвешенная сумма регуляризаторов?
questions.reference_answer: The constraint optimisation approach trains better than simple regularisation when objectives have different scales; using one loss as the objective and the rest as constraints enables automatic weight tuning via Lagrange multipliers, and constraint bounds are easy to choose (topological from data-space distances, reconstruction from the reconstruction error).

evidence.text: In our experience the constraint optimisation approach leads to better training performance than simple regularisation when one has to fit objectives with different scales. In principle any of the three losses or weighted combinations of some/all can be considered as the main objective. To have automatic "weight tuning" via Lagrange multipliers it is reasonable to have one loss as objective and the rest as constraints. We have made the above choices, because it is relatively easy to come up with constraint boundary candidates: for the topological one we are informed by the distances in the data space, while for the reconstruction one by the reconstruction error.

questions.doc_title: Overcoming Spurious Solutions in Semi-Dual Neural Optimal Transport: A Smoothing Approach for Learning the Optimal Transport Plan
questions.question: In Kantorovich optimal transport, what is the semi-dual formulation of the problem expressed in terms of c-concave functions, and how is the c-transform of a potential V defined?
questions.question_ru: Какова полудуальная (semi-dual) формулировка задачи Канторовича об оптимальном транспорте через $c$-вогнутые функции, и как определяется $c$-преобразование потенциала $V$?
questions.reference_answer: The semi-dual form is $S(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{V\in S_{c}}[\int_{\mathcal{X}}V^{c}(x)d\mu(x)+\int_{\mathcal{Y}}V(y)d\nu(y)]$, where $S_{c}$ is the collection of $c$-concave functions $\psi:\mathcal{Y}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ and $V^{c}$ is the $c$-transform $V^{c}(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}[c(x,y)-V(y)]$.

evidence.text:
The semi-dual formulation of the OT problem is given as follows: For a general cost function $c(\cdot,\cdot)$ that is lower semicontinuous and bounded below, the Kantorovich OT problem (Eq. 4) has the following *semi-dual form* (Villani et al. 2009, Thm. 5.10), (Santambrogio 2015, Prop. 1.11):

$$
S(\mu,\nu):=\!\!\sup_{V\in S_{c}}\left[\int_{\mathcal{X}}V^{c}(x)d\mu(x)\!+\!\!\int_{\mathcal{Y}}V(y)d\nu(y)\right], \tag{5}
$$

where $S_{c}$ denotes the collection of $c$-concave functions $\psi:\mathcal{Y}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ and $V^{c}$ denotes the $c$-transform of $V$, i.e.,

$$
V^{c}(x)=\underset{y\in\mathcal{Y}}{\inf}\left[c(x,y)-V(y)\right]. \tag{6}
$$

questions.doc_title: Overcoming Spurious Solutions in Semi-Dual Neural Optimal Transport: A Smoothing Approach for Learning the Optimal Transport Plan
questions.question: In the OTP (Optimal Transport Plan) model, what two smoothing distributions are used to construct the smoothed source measure $\mu_{\epsilon}$, and how do they satisfy the conditions (c1) and (c2)?
questions.question_ru: В модели OTP (Optimal Transport Plan) какие два сглаживающих распределения используются для построения сглаженной меры источника $\mu_{\epsilon}$, и как они удовлетворяют условиям (c1) и (c2)?
questions.reference_answer: The two options are (1) Gaussian convolution $\mu_{\epsilon_{k}}=\mu*\mathcal{N}(0,\epsilon_{k}I)$ and (2) variance-preserving convolution $\mu_{\epsilon_{k}}=(\sqrt{1-\epsilon_{k}}Id)_{\#}\mu*\mathcal{N}(0,\epsilon_{k}I)$ with $\epsilon_{k}\searrow 0$. Both satisfy (c1) and (c2): for Gaussian convolution $\mu_{\epsilon}$ is absolutely continuous with positive density on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, and as $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$, $\mu_{\epsilon}\rightharpoonup\mu$; a similar argument holds for the variance-preserving case.

evidence.text: Motivated by diffusion models (Ho et al. 2020; Song et al. 2021), we consider **two options for the smoothing distribution**: (1) Gaussian convolution $\mu_{\epsilon_{k}}=\mu\,*\,\mathcal{N}(0,\epsilon_{k}I)$ and (2) Variance-preserving convolution $\mu_{\epsilon_{k}}=\left(\sqrt{1-\epsilon_{k}}Id\right)_{\#}\mu\,*\,\mathcal{N}(0,\epsilon_{k}I)$ with a predefined noise level $\epsilon_{k}\searrow 0$. For noise-level scheduling, we follow Song et al. 2021. Note that both of these smoothing distributions satisfy conditions (c1) and (c2). Specifically, for Gaussian convolution, for any $\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, (c1) $\mu_{\epsilon}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure and has positive density on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Moreover, (c2) as $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$, $\mu_{\epsilon}\rightharpoonup\mu$. A similar argument works for the Variance-preserving convolution case.

questions.doc_title: Overcoming Spurious Solutions in Semi-Dual Neural Optimal Transport: A Smoothing Approach for Learning the Optimal Transport Plan
questions.question: Why are optimal transport plans, i.e. stochastic transport maps, argued to be more suitable than deterministic OT maps for real-world applications such as image-to-image translation, colorization, and image inpainting?
questions.question_ru: Почему оптимальные планы транспорта, то есть стохастические отображения транспорта, считаются более подходящими, чем детерминированные OT-отображения, для практических задач, таких как перевод изображений, колоризация и восстановление (inpainting)?
questions.reference_answer: Because OT plans are a theoretical generalization of deterministic OT maps and are inherently more suitable for real-world machine learning applications: in image-to-image translation stochastic OT plans can model the diversity of plausible outputs, and in inverse problems such as colorization or image inpainting they are highly desirable because these tasks inherently involve multiple possible solutions.

evidence.text: Our OTP model is for learning the OT Plan, i.e., the stochastic transport map. In fact, OT Plans are not only a theoretical generalization of deterministic OT Maps, but are also inherently more suitable for various real-world machine learning applications. For instance, in image-to-image translation tasks, stochastic OT Plans can effectively model the diversity of plausible outputs. Similarly, in inverse problems such as colorization or image inpainting, stochastic OT Plans are also highly desirable because these tasks inherently involve multiple possible solutions.

questions.doc_title: Revisiting invariances and introducing priors in Gromov-Wasserstein distances
questions.question: Why can the invariance of the Gromov-Wasserstein distance to isometric transformations be undesirable, and what handwritten-digit example is given to illustrate this limitation?
questions.question_ru: Почему инвариантность расстояния Громова-Вассерштейна к изометрическим преобразованиям может быть нежелательной, и какой пример с рукописной цифрой приводится для иллюстрации этого ограничения?
questions.reference_answer: Because there are infinitely many isometries and GW assigns them all the same value, so it cannot tell apart objects that should be distinguished. For instance, rotating the digit $6$ leads either to a slight variation for small angles or to a digit 9 near 180 degrees, yet the GW distance remains unchanged in both cases.

evidence.text: In other words, GW distance remains unchanged under any isometric transformation of input data. This favorable property has contributed much to the success and popularity of GW distance, where in many applications, the isometries naturally appear. However, since there are infinitely many isometries, not all are equally desirable. For instance, a rotation of the digit $6$ seen as a discrete measure can either lead to its slight variation for small angles or to a digit 9 when the angle is close to 180 degrees. In both cases, however, the GW distance remains unchanged, although it is clearly detrimental for telling the two distinct objects apart.
section_path: Revisiting invariances and introducing priors in Gromov-Wasserstein distances

questions.doc_title: Revisiting invariances and introducing priors in Gromov-Wasserstein distances
questions.question: For the Augmented Gromov-Wasserstein distance $\text{AGW}_\alpha$ with interpolation parameter $\alpha\in[0,1]$, what values does it tend to as $\alpha\to 0$ and as $\alpha\to 1$, and what inequality does it satisfy for any three input matrices $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y},\mathbf{Z}$?
questions.question_ru: Для расстояния Augmented Gromov-Wasserstein $\text{AGW}_\alpha$ с параметром интерполяции $\alpha\in[0,1]$, к каким величинам оно стремится при $\alpha\to 0$ и $\alpha\to 1$, и какому неравенству оно удовлетворяет для любых трёх входных матриц $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y},\mathbf{Z}$?
questions.reference_answer: As $\alpha\to 0$, $\text{AGW}_\alpha(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})\to\text{COOT}(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, and as $\alpha\to 1$ it tends to $\text{GW}(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$. It satisfies the relaxed triangle inequality $\text{AGW}_\alpha(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})\leq 2\big(\text{AGW}_\alpha(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Z})+\text{AGW}_\alpha(\mathbf{Z},\mathbf{Y})\big)$.

evidence.text:
**Proposition 1.** For every $\alpha\in[0,1]$,

1. Given two input matrices ${\bf X}$ and ${\bf Y}$, when $\alpha\to 0$ (or $1$), one has $\text{$\text{AGW}$}_{\alpha}({\bf X},{\bf Y})\to\text{COOT}({\bf X},{\bf Y})$ (or $\text{GW}({\bf X},{\bf Y})$).
2. AGW satisfies the relaxed triangle inequality: for any input matrices ${\bf X},{\bf Y},{\bf Z}$, one has $\text{$\text{AGW}$}_{\alpha}({\bf X},{\bf Y})\leq 2\big(\text{$\text{AGW}$}_{\alpha}({\bf X},{\bf Z})+\text{$\text{AGW}$}_{\alpha}({\bf Z},{\bf Y})\big)$.
section_path: Revisiting invariances and introducing priors in Gromov-Wasserstein distances

questions.doc_title: Revisiting invariances and introducing priors in Gromov-Wasserstein distances
questions.question: How does the Augmented Gromov-Wasserstein (AGW) divergence differ from the Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) distance in terms of the use cases it targets and the meaning and relationship of the feature space to the sample space?
questions.question_ru: Чем дивергенция Augmented Gromov-Wasserstein (AGW) отличается от расстояния Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) с точки зрения решаемых задач, а также смысла пространства признаков и его связи с пространством образцов?
questions.reference_answer: AGW tackles cross-domain applications that are inaccessible to FGW and can be used on empirical measures defined for any set of objects, whereas FGW is mostly used for structured objects endowed with additional feature information. In FGW the feature space is associated with the sample space, while in AGW the two spaces are independent.

evidence.text: Despite the resemblance to FGW, AGW serves a very different purpose and covers different use cases. First and foremost, AGW is a divergence that tackles cross-domain applications that are inaccessible to FGW. Second, FGW is mostly used for structured objects endowed with additional feature information, while AGW can be used on empirical measures defined for any set of objects. Finally, the feature space in the case of FGW is associated with the sample space, whereas in AGW the two spaces are independent.

questions.doc_title: TPOT: Topology Preserving Optimal Transport in Retinal Fundus Image Enhancement
questions.question: How is Monge's optimal transport problem formulated for the task of retinal fundus image enhancement, specifically the objective defining the optimal mapping f* and the pushforward constraint that aligns the two probability measures μ and ν?
questions.question_ru: Как формулируется задача Монжа об оптимальном транспорте для задачи повышения качества изображений глазного дна, а именно целевая функция, определяющая оптимальное отображение $f^{*}$, и ограничение типа pushforward, согласующее две вероятностные меры $\mu$ и $\nu$?
questions.reference_answer: The enhancement task is framed as solving Monge's optimal transport problem, in which the optimal mapping f* is the infimum over candidate mappings f of the integral of the cost C(x, f(x)) with respect to μ(x). The constraint f_# μ = ν is a pushforward condition that ensures alignment between the two probability measures.

evidence.text:
The retinal fundus image enhancement task can be naturally framed as solving *Monge’s* optimal transport problem, which is formulated as follows:

$$
\begin{split}f^{*}&=\inf_{f}\int_{\mathbf{X}}C(\mathbf{x},f(\mathbf{x}))d\mu(\mathbf{x})\\ &\text{subject to}\ f_{\#}\mu=\nu\end{split} \tag{1}
$$

where $C(\cdot,\cdot):\mathbf{X}\times\mathbf{Y}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}$ represents the cost function, $f$ denotes the candidate mapping functions, and the constraint ensures alignment between the two probability measures.
section_path: TPOT: Topology Preserving Optimal Transport in Retinal Fundus Image Enhancement

questions.doc_title: TPOT: Topology Preserving Optimal Transport in Retinal Fundus Image Enhancement
questions.question: In a topology-preserving regularization that minimizes the difference between persistence diagrams of segmentation likelihood maps, how is the topology regularization C_topo(x, G_θ(x)) defined in terms of the persistent points, and how is the optimal correspondence between the points of the two diagrams determined?
questions.question_ru: В топологически сохраняющей регуляризации, минимизирующей различие между диаграммами персистентности карт вероятностей сегментации, как определяется топологическая регуляризация $C_{topo}(\mathbf{x},G_{\theta}(\mathbf{x}))$ через персистентные точки и как определяется оптимальное соответствие между точками двух диаграмм?
questions.reference_answer: C_topo(x, G_θ(x)) is defined as the minimum over α of the sum over persistent points P^G in Dgm(S_N(G_θ)) of ||P^G − α(P^G)||², equivalently the sum (b2 − α*(b2))² + (d2 − α*(d2))², where (α*(d2), α*(b2)) ∈ P. The optimal correspondence α* between points of P^G and P is calculated based on the persistence (e.g., |d1 − b1|) of the critical points in P and P^G.

evidence.text:
Following the ideal outlined in [10], the topology regularization, $C_{topo}(\mathbf{x},G_{\theta}(\mathbf{x}))$, is defined as:

$$
\begin{split}C_{topo}(\mathbf{x},G_{\theta}(\mathbf{x}))&=\min_{\alpha}\sum_{P^{G}\in\textit{Dgm}(S_{N}(G_{\theta}))}||P^{G}-\alpha(P^{G})||^{2}\\ =\sum_{P^{G}\in\textit{Dgm}(S_{N}(G_{\theta}))}&(b_{2}-\alpha^{*}(b_{2}))^{2}+(d_{2}-\alpha^{*}(d_{2}))^{2}\end{split} \tag{3}
$$

where $(\alpha^{*}(d_{2}),\alpha^{*}(b_{2}))\in P$ and $\alpha^{*}$ represents the optimal correspondence of points between $P$ and $P^{G}$. This correspondence is calculated based on the persistence (e.g., $|d_{1}-b_{1}|$ ) of the critical points in $P$ and $P^{G}$.

questions.doc_title: TPOT: Topology Preserving Optimal Transport in Retinal Fundus Image Enhancement
questions.question: Why did research on retinal fundus image quality enhancement shift from supervised to unsupervised algorithms, and how do these unsupervised approaches typically model the enhancement task?
questions.question_ru: Почему исследования по повышению качества изображений глазного дна сместились от алгоритмов с учителем к алгоритмам без учителя, и как такие подходы без учителя обычно моделируют задачу улучшения?
questions.reference_answer: The shift occurred because collecting paired degraded and clean retinal images is both difficult and costly. These unsupervised approaches typically model enhancement as an end-to-end image-to-image (I2I) translation task using GANs, where low-quality images X are transformed into their high-quality counterparts Y, with CycleGAN as a common strategy due to its cycle consistency regularization.

evidence.text: Since it is both difficult and costly to collect paired degraded and clean retinal images, research on retinal fundus image quality enhancement has shifted from supervised algorithms [6] to unsupervised algorithms, leading to remarkable improvements in image quality. These unsupervised approaches typically model retinal quality enhancement as an end-to-end image-to-image (I2I) translation task using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), where low-quality images $X$ are transformed into their high-quality counterparts $Y$. Specifically, CycleGAN [7] serves as a common strategy, as its cycle consistency regularization enables learning meaningful bidirectional mappings and improves generation alignment, albeit with additional computational cost and potential artifacts.

questions.doc_title: POT: Python Optimal Transport
questions.question: In optimal transport, why does the Wasserstein distance compare favorably to f-divergences such as Kullback-Leibler, Jensen-Shannon and Total Variation, and in what way does the optimal transport solution differ from integral probability metrics like maximum mean discrepancy?
questions.question_ru: Почему в оптимальном транспорте расстояние Васерштейна выгодно отличается от f-дивергенций, таких как Кульбака-Лейблера, Йенсена-Шеннона и полной вариации, и чем решение задачи оптимального транспорта отличается от интегральных вероятностных метрик, таких как максимальное среднее расхождение (MMD)?
questions.reference_answer: The Wasserstein distance compares favourably to f-divergences (including Kullback-Leibler, Jensen-Shannon and Total Variation) when the support of the two distributions is disjoint. Unlike integral probability metrics such as MMD, the OT solution is a probabilistic (coupling) function that provides soft-assignments between the points in the supports of the two distributions, which can be used for their further matching.

evidence.text: The success of OT in different scientific areas resides in two main features. On the one hand, OT-based Wasserstein distance compares favourably to popular _f_ -divergences including popular Kullback-Leibler, Jensen-Shannon divergences and Total Variation distance, when the support of the two distributions is disjoint. On the other hand, and contrary to other popular integral probability metrics (IPMs) such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), the solution of the OT problem is given by a probabilistic (coupling) function that provides soft-assignments between the points in the supports of the two distributions, which can be used for their further matching.

questions.doc_title: POT: Python Optimal Transport
questions.question: In the discrete Kantorovich optimal transport problem, what constraints must a coupling matrix T satisfy to be a valid transport plan, and under what condition is the optimal value of the problem called the Wasserstein distance?
questions.question_ru: В дискретной задаче оптимального транспорта Канторовича каким ограничениям должна удовлетворять матрица связи T, чтобы быть допустимым планом перевозки, и при каком условии оптимальное значение задачи называется расстоянием Васерштейна?
questions.reference_answer: T must belong to the set Π(a, b) = {T ≥ 0, T1_{n2} = a, T^⊤1_{n1} = b}, i.e. it must be nonnegative with row and column sums equal to the marginals a and b. When the ground cost is a metric, the optimal value of the OT problem is also a metric and is called the Wasserstein distance.

evidence.text: **Kantorovich optimal transport problems** . This is the most typical OT problem. It seeks an optimal coupling **_T_** which minimizes the displacement cost of a discrete measure **_a_** to a discrete measure **_b_** with respect to a ground cost **_M_** _∈_ R<sup>_n_1</sup><sup>_×n_2</sup> . In order to be a transport plan, **_T_** must be part of the set Π( **a** _,_ **b** ) = _{_ **_T_** _≥_ **0** _,_ **_T_ 1** _n_ 2 = **_a_** _,_ **_T_**<sup>_⊤_</sup> **1** _n_ 1 = **_b_** _}_ . When the ground cost is a metric, the optimal value of the OT problem is also a metric (Rubner et al., 2000; Cuturi and Avis, 2014) and is called the _Wasserstein distance_ .

questions.doc_title: POT: Python Optimal Transport
questions.question: How does the GeomLoss toolbox compare with the POT and OTJulia packages in terms of scope and intended use, and what underlying framework is GeomLoss built on?
questions.question_ru: Как инструмент GeomLoss соотносится с пакетами POT и OTJulia по охвату и целевому применению, и на каком фреймворке основан GeomLoss?
questions.reference_answer: OTJulia is a more complete package seen as a Julia counterpart of POT, but it misses some features related to recent algorithmic developments and is a wrapper around POT for its exact EMD OT solver. GeomLoss is a more specific toolbox for solving very large scale Sinkhorn on CPU and GPU with a PyTorch API, is based on the KeOps framework, and is currently a better alternative to POT for using Sinkhorn losses in deep learning architectures.

evidence.text: The OTJulia is a more complete package that can be seen as a Julia counterpart of POT. It implements several OT solvers with detailed documentation, but still misses some features related to recent algorithmic developments, and interestingly is a wrapper around POT for its exact EMD OT solver. Finally, GeomLoss (Feydy et al., 2019) is a more specific toolbox for solving very large scale Sinkhorn on CPU and GPU with a PyTorch API. It is based on the very elegant KeOps framework (Charlier et al., 2020), and is currently a better alternative to POT for using Sinkhorn losses in deep learning architectures.

questions.doc_title: Latent Functional Maps: a spectral framework for representation alignment
questions.question: In the Latent Functional Map framework, how is the weighted graph Laplacian of a symmetric k-nearest neighbor graph defined, what properties does it have, and what form does its eigendecomposition take?
questions.question_ru: В рамках метода Latent Functional Map как определяется взвешенный лапласиан графа симметричного k-ближайших соседей, какими свойствами он обладает и какой вид имеет его спектральное разложение?
questions.reference_answer: The weighted graph Laplacian is $\mathcal{L}_{G}=\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{D}^{-1/2}\mathbf{W}\mathbf{D}^{-1/2}$, where $\mathbf{D}$ is the diagonal degree matrix with entries $\mathbf{D}_{i,i}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf{W}_{i,j}$. It is a positive semi-definite, self-adjoint operator, so it admits the eigendecomposition $\mathcal{L}_{G}=\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}\mathbf{\Lambda}_{G}\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}^{T}$, whose eigenvectors form an orthonormal basis of the functions defined on the graph nodes.

evidence.text: Next, we define the associated weighted graph Laplacian operator $\mathcal{L}_{G}=\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{D}^{-1/2}\mathbf{W}\mathbf{D}^{-1/2}$, where $\mathbf{D}$ is the diagonal degree matrix with entries $\mathbf{D}_{i,i}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf{W}_{i,j}$. $\mathcal{L}_{G}$ is a positive semi-definite, self-adjoint operator [56]), therefore, it admits an eigendecomposition $\mathcal{L}_{G}=\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}\mathbf{\Lambda}_{G}\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}^{T}$, where $\mathbf{\Lambda}_{G}$ is a diagonal matrix containing the eigenvalues, and $\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}$ is a matrix whose columns are the corresponding eigenvectors. The eigenvectors form an orthonormal basis for the space of functions defined on the graph nodes (i.e., $\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}^{T}\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}=\mathbf{I}$).

questions.doc_title: Latent Functional Maps: a spectral framework for representation alignment
questions.question: What optimization problem is solved to compute a latent functional map C between two latent spaces, and what do its regularization terms represent?
questions.question_ru: Какая задача оптимизации решается для вычисления латентной функциональной карты C между двумя латентными пространствами и что представляют собой её члены регуляризации?
questions.reference_answer: The latent functional map is obtained by minimizing $\|\mathbf{C}\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G_{X}}-\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G_{Y}}\|_{F}^{2}+\alpha\rho_{\mathcal{L}}(\mathbf{C})+\beta\rho_{f}(\mathbf{C})$, where $\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G}=\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}^{T}\mathbf{F}_{G}$ are the spectral coefficients of the descriptors. The terms $\rho_{\mathcal{L}}$ and $\rho_{f}$ are the Laplacian and descriptor operator commutativity regularizers.

evidence.text:
Given the set of descriptors $\mathbf{F}_{G_{X}}=[f^{G_{X}}_{1},\ldots,f^{G_{X}}_{n_{f}}]$ and $\mathbf{F}_{G_{Y}}=[f^{G_{Y}}_{1},\ldots,f^{G_{Y}}_{n_{f}}]$, we consider the optimization problem defined in Equation 1 and incorporate two regularizers which enforce commutativity for the Laplacian and the descriptors, respectively, with the map $\mathbf{C}$:

$$
\underset{\mathbf{C}}{\arg\min}\|\mathbf{C}\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G_{X}}-\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G_{Y}}\|_{F}^{2}+\alpha\rho_{\mathcal{L}}(\mathbf{C})+\beta\rho_{f}(\mathbf{C}) \tag{2}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{F}}_{G}=\mathbf{\Phi}_{G}^{T}\mathbf{F}_{G}$ are the spectral coefficients of the functions $\mathbf{F}_{G}$, $\rho_{\mathcal{L}}$ and $\rho_{f}$ are the Laplacian and descriptor operator commutativity regularizers respectively, akin to [41].

questions.doc_title: Latent Functional Maps: a spectral framework for representation alignment
questions.question: How is the similarity measure sim(X,Y) between two latent spaces defined from the functional map matrix C, and on what property of isometric transformations is it based?
questions.question_ru: Как определяется мера схожести sim(X,Y) между двумя латентными пространствами на основе матрицы функциональной карты C и на каком свойстве изометрических преобразований она основана?
questions.reference_answer: For volume-preserving (isometric) transformations the functional map is orthogonal and the matrix $\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C}$ is diagonal. The similarity is defined as the ratio of the off-diagonal norm to the full-matrix norm, $sim(X,Y)=1-\frac{||\text{off}((\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C})||_{F}^{2}}{||\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C}||_{F}^{2}}$.

evidence.text: Once computed, the functional map $\mathbf{C}$ can serve as a measure of similarity between spaces. The reason is that for isometric transformations between manifolds, the functional map is volume preserving (see Thm 5.1 in [44]), and this is manifested in orthogonal $\mathbf{C}$. By defining the inner product between functions $h_{1},h_{2}\in\mathcal{F}({M})$ as $\langle h_{1},h_{2}\rangle=\int_{\mathcal{M}}h_{1}(x)h_{2}(x)\mu(x)$, it holds that $\langle h_{1},h_{2}\rangle=\langle\hat{h}_{1},\hat{h}_{2}\rangle$ when the map preserves the local area, where $\hat{h}$ denotes the functional representation of $h$. In other words, when the transformation between the two manifolds is an isometry, the matrix $\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C}$ will be diagonal. By measuring the ratio between the norm of the off-diagonal elements of $\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C}$ and the norm of the full matrix, we can define a measure of similarity $sim(X,Y)=1-\frac{||\text{off}((\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C})||_{F}^{2}}{||\mathbf{C}^{T}\mathbf{C}||_{F}^{2}}$.
section_path: Latent Functional Maps: a spectral framework for representation alignment

questions.doc_title: Fast Topological Signal Identification and Persistent Cohomological Cycle Matching
questions.question: In bootstrapping-based topological data analysis, how is the prevalence score of a persistence interval $\alpha$ computed from a reference space $X_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $K$ resampling spaces $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(K)}$, and what value is used when no matching exists?
questions.question_ru: В топологическом анализе данных на основе бутстрэпа как вычисляется prevalence score интервала персистентности $\alpha$ по референсному пространству $X_{\mathrm{ref}}$ и $K$ пространствам ресемплинга $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(K)}$, и какое значение используется, если соответствие не найдено?
questions.reference_answer: The prevalence score is $\mathrm{prev}(\alpha) := \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho(\alpha,\beta_{k}(\alpha))$, where $\beta_{k}(\alpha)$ is the unique bar in $X^{(k)}$ matched to $\alpha$ using $Z=X_{\mathrm{ref}}\cup X^{(k)}$ as a comparison space and the inclusions into the union as the connecting maps $f$ and $g$; if a matching does not exist, $\rho$ is set to 0.

evidence.text:
**Definition 8 (Prevalence score, Reani & Bobrowski, 2021b).** Given some reference space $X=X_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and resampling spaces $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(K)}$ , any $\alpha\in\mathrm{Pers}(H_{*}(X_{\bullet}))$ has a *prevalence score* defined by

$$
\mathrm{prev}(\alpha):=\dfrac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho(\alpha,\beta_{k}(\alpha)),
$$

where $\beta_{k}(\alpha)$ is the unique bar in $X^{(k)}$, for $1\leq k\leq K$, matched to $\alpha$ using $Z=X_{\mathrm{ref}}\cup X^{(k)}$ as a comparison space and the inclusions into the union as the connecting maps $f:X_{\mathrm{ref}}\to Z$ and $g:X^{(k)}\to Z$ (if a matching does not exist, set $\rho=0$).

questions.doc_title: Fast Topological Signal Identification and Persistent Cohomological Cycle Matching
questions.question: In the parallelized prevalence and cycle-matching pipeline, what is the true computational bottleneck, and how does the median runtime scale with the number of sampled points $N$, including the effect of increasing $N$ by a factor of 10?
questions.question_ru: В параллелизуемом конвейере prevalence и cycle matching что является истинным вычислительным узким местом и как медианное время работы масштабируется с числом выборочных точек $N$, в том числе при увеличении $N$ в 10 раз?
questions.reference_answer: The bottleneck is not the number of matchings $K$ but the number of sampled points $N$ and $N_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Median runtime grows as a power law $T \sim \mathrm{cst}\cdot N^{p}$ with $p \simeq 3.266$, so increasing $N$ by a factor of 10 raises runtime by a factor of about $10^{3.266} \simeq 1845$.

evidence.text: The computational bottleneck here is not the number of matchings $K$ but the number of points $N$ and $N_{\mathrm{ref}}$ sampled in the respective spaces for each matching instead. The number of matchings could be increased arbitrarily (up to the capacity of the HPC) without affecting the computational runtime while maintaining it on the order of minutes or a few hours. Increasing it here allows for more precise estimations of, for instance, the average runtime needed to find all possible matchings between two spaces. However, median runtime increases following a power law $T\sim\mathrm{cst}\cdot N^{p}$ where $\mathrm{cst}$ is a constant and $p\simeq 3.266$ (see Figure 16), so that increasing the number of sampled points $N$ by a factor of $10$ would result in increasing runtime by a factor of $10^{p}\simeq 1845$.

questions.doc_title: Fast Topological Signal Identification and Persistent Cohomological Cycle Matching
questions.question: How does the matching affinity $D$ behave differently from the matching affinities $A$, $B$, and $C$ when the spatial overlap between matched cycles decreases, and in what application would affinity $D$ be advantageous?
questions.question_ru: Чем поведение matching affinity $D$ отличается от matching affinities $A$, $B$ и $C$ при уменьшении пространственного перекрытия совпадающих циклов, и в каком приложении affinity $D$ была бы предпочтительнее?
questions.reference_answer: Affinities $A$, $B$, and $C$ drop when the spatial overlap between cycles decreases because they include the Jaccard indices between bars and image-bars; affinity $D$ omits that comparison and remains at a higher value until there is no match, then drops abruptly. Affinity $D$ is advantageous when matching topological features that shrink, enlarge, or appear misplaced in the samples, since it assigns them a higher prevalence score.

evidence.text: It also makes sense that the matching affinities $A,B,$ and $C$ drop when the spatial overlap between cycles decreases. This happens because these affinities include the Jaccard indices between bars and image-bars, which are influenced by this overlap. The matching affinity $D$ does not consider such a comparison, and thus, remains at a higher value until there is no match anymore, when it drops abruptly. Such a behavior could be useful in certain situations. In real-life applications, it might happen that we are interested in matching topological features that shrink or enlarge significantly, or which appear misplaced in the samples. Matching affinity $D$ would then be more sensitive to these matches, by assigning a higher prevalence score to them.

questions.doc_title: On the Transfer of Inductive Bias from Simulation to the Real World: a New Disentanglement Dataset
questions.question: In disentangled representation learning with variational auto-encoders, how does the β-VAE modify the training objective, and why does this modification encourage a factorized latent space?
questions.question_ru: В обучении дизенглд-представлениям с помощью вариационных автоэнкодеров как β-VAE изменяет целевую функцию обучения и почему эта модификация способствует факторизованному латентному пространству?
questions.reference_answer: The β-VAE penalizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence term in the VAE objective more strongly. Because the standard objective imposes no structure on the latent space beyond similarity to the isotropic Gaussian prior, this stronger penalty encourages similarity to the factorized prior distribution.

evidence.text: Since the above objective does not enforce any structure on the latent space, except for some similarity to the typically chosen isotropic Gaussian prior $p(\bm{z})$, various proposals for more structure imposing regularization have been made. Using some sort of supervision [43, 4, 35, 40, 9, e.g.] or proposing completely unsupervised [19, 24, 7, 27, 13, e.g.] learning approaches. [19] proposed the $\beta$-VAE penalizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KL) term in the VAE objective more strongly, which encourages similarity to the factorized prior distribution.

questions.doc_title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
questions.question: According to the non-vanishing null interaction energy result, what is the expected squared Frobenius norm of the normalized cross-covariance operator between two independent, row-centered representation matrices with zero-mean, identity-covariance i.i.d. rows, and what null baseline does it imply for CKA?
questions.question_ru: Согласно результату о неисчезающей нулевой энергии взаимодействия, чему равно ожидаемое значение квадрата нормы Фробениуса нормированного кросс-ковариационного оператора между двумя независимыми центрированными по строкам матрицами представлений с независимыми одинаково распределёнными строками с нулевым средним и единичной ковариацией, и какой нулевой базовый уровень (null baseline) из этого следует для CKA?
questions.reference_answer: Under independence with zero-mean, identity-covariance i.i.d. rows, the expected squared Frobenius norm of the normalized sample cross-covariance is $d_x d_y/(n-1)$. Because CKA is normalized by self-similarity terms of order $\sqrt{d}$, this gives a null baseline of order $\mathcal{O}(d/n)$.

evidence.text:
**Proposition 4.1 (Non-vanishing null interaction energy).** Assume the rows are i.i.d. with $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{i}]=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{y}_{i}]=0$, $\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf{x}_{i})=\mathbf{I}_{d_{x}}$, $\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf{y}_{i})=\mathbf{I}_{d_{y}}$, and $\mathbf{x}_{i}$ and $\mathbf{y}_{i}$ are independent. Then

$$
\mathbb{E}_{H_{0}}\left[\|\widetilde{\mathbf{C}}\|_{F}^{2}\right]\;=\;\frac{d_{x}d_{y}}{n-1}. \tag{3}
$$

*Proof.* See Section D.4.

Since CKA is scaled by the normalized self-similarity terms, which each scale as $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{d})$, the resulting null baseline for the metric is thus $\mathcal{O}(d/n)$.

questions.doc_title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
questions.question: What are the four steps of the null-calibration procedure that turns a raw representational similarity score into a calibrated score, and when should scalar calibration be used rather than aggregation-aware calibration?
questions.question_ru: Каковы четыре шага процедуры нулевой калибровки, преобразующей исходную оценку сходства представлений в калиброванную оценку, и в каком случае следует использовать скалярную калибровку, а не агрегационно-осознанную (aggregation-aware)?
questions.reference_answer: The four steps are (i) fix a significance level α such as 0.05; (ii) generate K null scores by permuting sample correspondences; (iii) compute the critical value τ as the ⌈(1−α)(K+1)⌉-th order statistic of the combined observed+null set; (iv) return the calibrated score s_cal or T_cal. Scalar calibration is used for a single pair of representations; aggregation-aware calibration is used when reporting a summary statistic such as a maximum over multiple layer pairs.

evidence.text:
To compute a calibrated similarity score: *(i)* fix a significance level $\alpha$ (*e.g.*, $\alpha=0.05$); *(ii)* generate $K$ null scores by permuting sample correspondences; *(iii)* compute critical value $\tau$ as the $\lceil(1-\alpha)(K+1)\rceil$-th order statistic of the combined set (observed + null scores); *(iv)* return calibrated score, either $s_{\mathrm{cal}}$ or $T_{\mathrm{cal}}$.

Use *scalar calibration* (Section 5.1) when comparing a single pair of representations. Use *aggregation-aware calibration* (Section 5.2) when reporting a summary statistic (*e.g.*, maximum) over multiple layer pairs. Appendix E provides pseudocode for both procedures.

questions.doc_title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
questions.question: When the Platonic Representation Hypothesis is re-evaluated using image–text pairs and a maximum-over-layer-pairs aggregation, how do calibrated global spectral CKA scores and calibrated local neighborhood metrics such as mKNN behave as model scale increases, and what do the local metrics reveal about agreement on neighborhood identity versus pairwise distances?
questions.question_ru: При пересмотре гипотезы платоновской репрезентации с использованием пар изображение–текст и агрегации по максимуму среди пар слоёв: как ведут себя калиброванные глобальные спектральные оценки CKA и калиброванные локальные метрики соседства, такие как mKNN, с ростом масштаба модели, и что локальные метрики показывают относительно согласия по идентичности соседей и по попарным расстояниям?
questions.reference_answer: Uncalibrated CKA increases with model scale, but this trend disappears after calibration—calibrated CKA shows no systematic increase with model size—indicating the apparent global convergence was largely due to width and depth confounders. In contrast, local neighborhood metrics retain strong cross-modal alignment after calibration: models increasingly agree on which points are neighbors but not on pairwise distances.

evidence.text:
For the *global* similarity, we find that uncalibrated CKA scores increase with model scale (dotted lines in Figure 6a), reproducing the trend interpreted as evidence of cross-modal convergence (20). However, this trend disappears after our calibration (solid lines): calibrated CKA shows no systematic increase with model size. This indicates that global convergence in uncalibrated CKA is largely attributable to width and depth confounders rather than a genuine increase in representational similarity.

In contrast, for the *local* similarity, evidence of cross-modal convergence remains strong for neighborhood-based metrics even under our calibration (Figure 6b). The same qualitative conclusion holds for other neighborhood-based measures (cycle-$k$NN and CKNNA; Section F.7) and different choices of $\alpha$ (Section F.10). Further analysis (Section F.9) reveals that models converge in local neighborhood structure: models increasingly agree on which points are neighbors, but do not agree on the pairwise distances, since CKA-RBF with a small bandwidth shows no alignment after calibration.

questions.question: Why is the CP decomposition of the third moment tensor not directly usable as a practical statistical and computational method for certifying identifiability, even though it gives a clean theoretical characterization?
questions.question_ru: Почему CP-разложение тензора третьего момента не пригодно напрямую как практический статистический и вычислительный метод сертификации идентифицируемости, несмотря на даваемую им чистую теоретическую характеризацию?
questions.reference_answer: Third moment tensor decompositions are statistically sensitive to noise and require large sample sizes to be stable, and computationally the CP decomposition is NP hard to compute, with efficient approximations that do not provide the guarantees needed for a certificate.

evidence.text: While Proposition 3.3 provides a clean theoretical characterization of identifiability for many probabilistic models, it is not a statistically or computationally efficient approach for providing identifiability guarantees. Statistically, third moment tensor decompositions can be sensitive to noise and require large sample sizes to be stable. Computationally, the CP decomposition is NP hard to compute and efficient approximations do not provide the types of guarantees needed for a certificate. We overcome these challenges by developing an alternative randomized algorithm that efficiently certifies the lack of linear symmetries without explicit computation of third moment conditions.

questions.doc_title: Canonicalizing Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning
questions.question: When a linear map aligning two independently trained multimodal contrastive models is shown to be an isometry, a diversity condition on the embeddings is required. What does it mean for a set of vectors $S\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be $\mathrm{Sym}(d)$-spanning? Give both the rank-one-matrix definition and the equivalent quadratic-form condition.
questions.question_ru: Когда линейное отображение, выравнивающее две независимо обученные мультимодальные контрастивные модели, оказывается изометрией, требуется условие разнообразия на эмбеддинги. Что означает, что множество векторов $S\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ является $\mathrm{Sym}(d)$-spanning? Приведите как определение через матрицы ранга один, так и эквивалентное условие через квадратичную форму.
questions.reference_answer: A set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is $\mathrm{Sym}(d)$-spanning if the rank-one matrices $\{xx^{\top}:x\in S\}$ span the space of symmetric matrices $\mathrm{Sym}(d)$. Equivalently, if $M\in\mathrm{Sym}(d)$ and $x^{\top}Mx=0$ for all $x\in S$, then $M=0$, which follows from the identity $x^{\top}Mx=\langle xx^{\top},M\rangle$.

evidence.text: **Definition 5.4.** ($\mathrm{Sym}(d)$-spanning) A set of vectors $S\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is *$\mathrm{Sym}(d)$-spanning* if the rank-one matrices $\{xx^{\top}:x\in S\}$ span the space of symmetric matrices $\mathrm{Sym}(d)$. Equivalently: if $M\in\mathrm{Sym}(d)$ and $x^{\top}Mx=0$ for all $x\in S$, then $M=0$. This equivalence follows from the identity $x^{\top}Mx=\langle xx^{\top},M\rangle$.

questions.doc_title: Canonicalizing Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning
questions.question: A method aligns two independently trained multimodal contrastive encoders by fitting a map on one modality using paired embeddings. What optimization objective defines the optimal orthogonal map $\hat{Q}$, and what is its closed-form solution via an SVD of the cross-covariance, including how unequal embedding dimensions $d<\tilde{d}$ are handled?
questions.question_ru: Метод выравнивает два независимо обученных мультимодальных контрастивных энкодера, подбирая отображение по одной модальности на парных эмбеддингах. Какой целевой функцией определяется оптимальное ортогональное отображение $\hat{Q}$ и каково его решение в замкнутой форме через SVD кросс-ковариационной матрицы, включая обработку случая неравных размерностей $d<\tilde{d}$?
questions.reference_answer: The optimal map solves the Orthogonal Procrustes problem $\hat{Q}=\text{argmin}_{Q^{\top}Q=I}\|\tilde{X}-QX\|_{F}^{2}$. Its closed form is $\hat{Q}=UI_{\tilde{d}\times d}V^{\top}$ where $U\Sigma V^{\top}=\text{SVD}(\tilde{X}X^{\top})$; the rectangular identity $I_{\tilde{d}\times d}$ naturally handles $d<\tilde{d}$, making $\hat{Q}$ semi-orthogonal with $Q^{\top}Q=I_{d}$.

evidence.text: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times N}$ and $\tilde{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{\tilde{d}\times N}$ be the data matrices containing the centered, normalized embeddings $f(x_{i})$ and $\tilde{f}(x_{i})$ as columns. We solve for the optimal isometry $\hat{Q}$ by minimizing the transport cost subject to an orthogonality constraint: $\hat{Q}=\text{argmin}_{Q^{\top}Q=I}\|\tilde{X}-QX\|_{F}^{2}$. This is the classic *Orthogonal Procrustes Problem*, which has a closed-form solution via the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the cross-covariance matrix $M=\tilde{X}X^{\top}$. Let $U\Sigma V^{\top}=\text{SVD}(M)$, then $\hat{Q}=UI_{\tilde{d}\times d}V^{\top}.$ Here, $I_{\tilde{d}\times d}$ is a rectangular identity matrix. This formulation naturally handles $d<\tilde{d}$, where $\hat{Q}$ becomes a semi-orthogonal i.e. $Q^{\top}Q=I_{d}$.

questions.question: When comparing orthogonal, linear, and non-linear MLP maps for aligning two independently trained vision-language contrastive models by increasing expressiveness, how do the more expressive maps score on pointwise image-image cosine similarity, and how do they behave for text transfer and geometry-sensitive downstream metrics compared with the orthogonal map?
questions.question_ru: При сравнении ортогонального, линейного и нелинейного MLP-отображений для выравнивания двух независимо обученных контрастивных vision-language моделей по возрастанию выразительности: как более выразительные отображения показывают себя по точечной косинусной близости image-image и как они ведут себя при переносе на текст и на метриках, чувствительных к геометрии, по сравнению с ортогональным отображением?
questions.reference_answer: More expressive maps (linear and non-linear MLP) improve pointwise image-image cosine similarity, but they transfer poorly to the text modality and distort the image-text geometry. In contrast, the orthogonal map consistently performs best on both pointwise text cosine similarity and geometry-sensitive downstream metrics.

evidence.text: Here, we ablate the alignment design by comparing three maps of increasing expressiveness: (i) an orthogonal map $Q$, (ii) a linear map, and (iii) a non-linear MLP. As shown in Figure 7, more expressive maps improve *pointwise* image-image cosine similarity. However, these maps transfer poorly to the text modality and distort the image-text geometry. In contrast, the orthogonal map consistently performs best on both pointwise text cosine similarity and geometry-sensitive downstream metrics.

questions.question: Under the entropic optimal transport benchmark constructor, if a joint distribution π* has first marginal P0 and conditional density π*(y|x) = (1/Z_x)exp((f*(y)−c(x,y))/ε), what condition on the second marginal and on the expected cost guarantees that π* is the unique entropic optimal transport plan?
questions.question_ru: В конструкции бенчмарка энтропийной оптимальной транспортировки, если совместное распределение π* имеет первую маргиналь P0 и условную плотность π*(y|x) = (1/Z_x)exp((f*(y)−c(x,y))/ε), какое условие на вторую маргиналь и на ожидаемую стоимость гарантирует, что π* является единственным планом энтропийной оптимальной транспортировки?
questions.reference_answer: If the second marginal $\mathbb{P}_{1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{def}}}{{=}}\pi_{1}^{*}$ belongs to $\mathcal{P}_{p}(\mathcal{Y})$, then $\pi^{*}$ is an EOT plan for $\mathbb{P}_{0},\mathbb{P}_{1}$ and cost $C_{c,\epsilon}$; moreover, if $\int_{\mathcal{X}}C_{c,\epsilon}(x,\pi^{*}(\cdot|x))d\mathbb{P}_{0}(x)<\infty$, then $\pi^{*}$ is the unique EOT plan.

evidence.text: Then if ${\mathbb{P}}_{1}\!\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{def}}}{{=}}\!\pi_{1}^{*}$ belongs to $\mathcal{P}_{p}(\mathcal{Y})$, the distribution $\pi^{*}$ is an **EOT plan** for $\mathbb{P}_{0},\mathbb{P}_{1}$ and cost $C_{c,\epsilon}$. Moreover, if $\int_{\mathcal{X}}C_{c,\epsilon}\big(x,\pi^{*}(\cdot|x)\big)d\mathbb{P}_{0}(x)\!<\!\infty$, then $\pi^{*}$ is the **unique** EOT plan.

questions.doc_title: Building the Bridge of Schrödinger: A Continuous Entropic Optimal Transport Benchmark
questions.question: How is the conditional Bures-Wasserstein metric cBW_2^2-UVP, used to compare a learned conditional plan π̂(·|x) with the ground-truth EOT plan π*(·|x), defined and normalized on the benchmark?
questions.question_ru: Как определяется и нормируется условная метрика Бюреса–Вассерштейна cBW_2^2-UVP, используемая для сравнения выученного условного плана π̂(·|x) с эталонным планом EOT π*(·|x) в бенчмарке?
questions.reference_answer: It is defined as 100% divided by $\frac{1}{2}\text{Var}(\mathbb{P}_{1})$, multiplied by the integral over $\mathcal{X}$ of the Bures-Wasserstein distance $\text{B}\mathbb{W}_{2}^{2}$ between the Gaussian approximations of the conditional distributions $\widehat{\pi}(\cdot|x)$ and $\pi^{*}(\cdot|x)$, then averaged over $x\sim{\mathbb{P}}_{0}$.

evidence.text:
$$
\text{c}\text{B}\mathbb{W}_{2}^{2}\text{-UVP}\big(\widehat{\pi},\pi^{*}\big)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{def}}}{{=}}\frac{100\%}{\frac{1}{2}\text{Var}(\mathbb{P}_{1})}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\text{B}\mathbb{W}_{2}^{2}\big(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot|x),\pi^{*}(\cdot|x)\big)d\mathbb{P}_{0}(x). \tag{17}
$$

For each $x$ we compare **conditional** distributions $\widehat{\pi}(\cdot|x)$ and $\pi^{*}(\cdot|x)$ with each other by using the Bures-Wasserstein metric [16], i.e., the Wasserstein-2 distance between Gaussian approximations of distributions. Then we average this metric w.r.t. $x\sim{\mathbb{P}}_{0}$.

questions.doc_title: Conditional Optimal Transport on Function Spaces
questions.question: In the optimal transport theory on separable Hilbert spaces, what is a Gaussian null set, and when is a probability measure called regular with respect to such sets?
questions.question_ru: В теории оптимального транспорта в сепарабельных гильбертовых пространствах что такое гауссово нулевое множество и когда вероятностная мера называется регулярной относительно таких множеств?
questions.reference_answer: A set $B$ is a Gaussian null set if $\gamma(B)=0$ for any non-degenerate Gaussian measure $\gamma$ on the separable Hilbert space. A measure $\varrho$ is called regular if it assigns zero measure to all Gaussian null sets $B$.

evidence.text: **Definition 13.** Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ is a separable Hilbert space. We say $B\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{X})$ is a Gaussian null set if $\gamma(B)=0$ for any non-degenerate Gaussian measure $\gamma\in\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{X})$ \[Footnote: Recall that $\gamma$ is said to be a Gaussian measure if $\ell\#\gamma$ is a one-dimensional Gaussian distribution for all $\ell\in\mathcal{X}^{\star}$ the dual of $\mathcal{X}$ [ 20 ] .\]. Furthermore, we say that a measure $\varrho\in\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{X})$ is regular if $\varrho(B)=0$ for all Gaussian null sets $B$.

questions.doc_title: Conditional Optimal Transport on Function Spaces
questions.question: In the Conditional Wasserstein Monge GAN (WaMGAN) approach for amortized conditional simulation, how is the conditioning map $\widehat{T}_{\mathcal{U}}$ obtained by relaxing the conditional Monge problem?
questions.question_ru: В подходе Conditional Wasserstein Monge GAN (WaMGAN) для амортизированного условного моделирования как получается отображающее обусловливание $\widehat{T}_{\mathcal{U}}$ путём релаксации условной задачи Монжа?
questions.reference_answer: The map is parameterized by a neural net and found by minimizing the Monge term plus a divergence $D$ between $T\#\eta^{J}$ and $\nu^{J}$ weighted by $1/\lambda$, i.e., by replacing the hard constraint $T\#\eta=\nu$ with minimizing a divergence between the pushforward and the target.

evidence.text:
Our second algorithm follows Proposition 23 and aims to approximate the map $T^{\star}_{\mathcal{U}}$ by a relaxation of the conditional Monge problem. The idea here is to parameterize $T_{\mathcal{U}}^{\star}$ using an expressive function approximator, a neural net in our case, and solve a problem of the form

$$
\widehat{T}_{\mathcal{U}}=\arg\min_{T_{\mathcal{U}}\in\mathcal{T}}\int_{\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{U}}\|v-T_{\mathcal{U}}(z,v)\|^{2}_{\mathcal{U}}{\rm d}\eta(z,v)+\frac{1}{\lambda}D(T\#\eta^{J},\nu^{J}),\>\st\>T(z,v)=(z,T_{\mathcal{U}}(z,v)),
$$

where $\mathcal{T}$ is a parametric family of functions from $\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{U}\to\mathcal{U}$, $D$ is a divergence/discrepancy that distinguishes pairs of measures in $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{U})$, and $\lambda>0$ is a regularization parameter. Simply put, the above approach amounts to solving the conditional Monge problem Equation 3 for the empirical measures and by relaxing the constraint $T\#\eta=\nu$ to simply minimize a divergence between $T\#\eta$ and $\nu$.

questions.doc_title: Conditional Optimal Transport on Function Spaces
questions.question: Why is solving the conditional optimal transport problem for amortized Bayesian inference computationally advantageous compared to using function space MCMC algorithms such as pCN or MALA to sample a posterior?
questions.question_ru: Почему решение задачи условного оптимального транспорта для амортизированного байесовского вывода вычислительно выгоднее по сравнению с алгоритмами MCMC в функциональном пространстве, такими как pCN или MALA, для сэмплирования апостериорной меры?
questions.reference_answer: MCMC algorithms such as pCN or MALA require long sequential runs for each value of $y$, whereas the triangular transport map is approximated only once and can then simply be evaluated for any value of $y$ to generate posterior samples, avoiding the need to run an MCMC chain to convergence for every new $y$.

evidence.text: The standard approach for sampling $\nu(\cdot\mid y)$ is to use function space MCMC algorithms such as preconditioned-Crank-Nicolson (pCN) or Metropolis Adjusted Langevine (MALA) [32] but these algorithms require long sequential runs for each value of $y$. However, by solving 1 we can obtain an approximation $\widehat{T}_{\mathcal{U}}$ to the map $T^{\star}_{\mathcal{U}}$ such that $\widehat{T}_{\mathcal{U}}(y,\cdot)\#\mu\approx\nu(\cdot\mid y)$. We use this approach in Section 5.3 and compare the performance of a triangular map appraoch to that of MCMC; see in particular Figure 3. The advantage of this approach is that the map is only approximated once and can simply be evaluated for any value of $y$ to generate posterior samples, for comparison, an MCMC chain needs to be run to convergence for every new value of $y$.

questions.doc_title: Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms
questions.question: In the Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport literature, a base cost c on a space X can be called conditionally of negative type (CNT). What are the defining properties of such a cost, and which families of pairwise functions (distances) are known to belong to this class?
questions.question_ru: В литературе по оптимальному транспорту с метрикой Громова–Вассерштейна базовая стоимость c на пространстве X может называться условно отрицательно определённой (conditionally of negative type, CNT). Каковы определяющие свойства такой стоимости и какие семейства парных функций (расстояний) заведомо принадлежат этому классу?
questions.reference_answer: A cost c is CNT if it is symmetric, satisfies c(x,x)=0, and for any finite set of points and real coefficients summing to zero (Σλ_i=0) the quadratic form Σ λ_i λ_j c(x_i,x_j) is ≤ 0. This class includes tree distances, hyperbolic geodesic distances, spherical distances, and all p-powered Euclidean distances ||x−x'||^p with 0<p≤2.

evidence.text:
A non-negative, continuous cost $c:\!~\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}~\!\longrightarrow\!~\mathbb{R}^{+}$ is *conditionally of negative type* (CNT) if it is symmetric, satisfies $c(x,x)=0$ for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ \[Footnote: This condition can be relaxed by considering the cost $\tilde{c}(x,y)=c(x,y)-\frac{1}{2}(c(x,x)+c(y,y))$ .\] and is such that for any finite collection of points $x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in\mathcal{X}$ and coefficients $\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n}\in\mathbb{R}$:

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_{i}=0~~\Longrightarrow~~\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_{i}\lambda_{j}\cdot c(x_{i},x_{j})\leq 0~.
$$

Moreover, we say that a cost $c$ is *definite* CNT if $c(x,x^{\prime})=0$ if and only if $x=x^{\prime}$. We refer to (6, Appendix C) for an introduction to this class of pairwise functions that includes tree distances, hyperbolic geodesic distances, spherical distances and all $p$-powered Euclidean distances $c(x,x^{\prime})=\left\|x-x^{\prime}\right\|^{p}$ for $0<p\leq 2$.
section_path: Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms

questions.doc_title: Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms
questions.question: In a scalable solver for Gromov-Wasserstein matching with conditionally-negative-type costs, how is the current optimal transport coupling π encoded so that an explicit N×M matrix need not be stored, and what is the corresponding formula in terms of the dual potentials f and g?
questions.question_ru: В масштабируемом решателе для согласования по Громову–Вассерштейну с условно отрицательно определёнными стоимостями как кодируется текущая оптимальная транспортная связь π так, чтобы явную матрицу N×M можно было не хранить, и какова соответствующая формула через двойственные потенциалы f и g?
questions.reference_answer: Instead of storing the coupling matrix, the solver uses two dual vectors f∈R^N and g∈R^M and reconstructs each entry as π_ij = a_i b_j · exp( (8/ε)[f_i + g_j − ||X̄_i − Z̄_j||²] ), thereby avoiding a large N×M array in memory.

evidence.text:
Following Theorem 3.4 and Eq. (1), we use two dual vectors $(f_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{N}}$ and $(g_{j})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{M}}$ to encode the current optimal coupling $\pi_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{N}\times\mathrm{M}}$ as:

$$
\pi_{ij}~=~a_{i}b_{j}\cdot\exp\tfrac{8}{\varepsilon}[f_{i}+g_{j}-\|\,\overline{\!{X}}_{i}-\,\overline{\!{Z}}_{j}\|^{2}]
$$

without having to store a large $\mathrm{N}\times\mathrm{M}$ array in memory.

questions.doc_title: Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms
questions.question: In a review of computational Gromov-Wasserstein solvers, for what reasons were the Sampled-GW and Proximal-GW algorithms left out of the quantitative benchmark comparisons?
questions.question_ru: В обзоре вычислительных решателей Громова–Вассерштейна по каким причинам алгоритмы Sampled-GW и Proximal-GW были исключены из количественных сравнений бенчмарка?
questions.reference_answer: Sampled-GW was excluded because its stochastic sampling prevents effective convergence and reliable comparisons of convergence speed, and Proximal-GW was excluded because it addresses a distinct problem formulation and does not scale to N>10^4 points.

evidence.text:
Despite the wide variety of Gromov-Wasserstein solvers available, only entropic-regularized methods (Section A.2.2) scale to inputs containing thousands of points, and only accelerated approximations can handle tens of thousands. Consequently, we focus our benchmarks on two main competitors: Entropic-GW, the reference solver for exact EGW problems, and LowRank-GW, the current state-of-the-art for approximate solving.

We excluded other potential baselines for the following reasons:

- Sampled-GW relies on stochastic sampling: due to this randomness, the solver does not converges effectively which prevents reliable comparisons of convergence speed.
- Proximal-GW addresses a distinct problem formulation, and does not scale to $\mathrm{N}>10^{4}$ points.
- Methods such as Sparse-GW or ULOT rely on different computational backends or address different settings, making fair comparisons difficult to perform.

questions.doc_title: AuToMATo: An Out-Of-The-Box Persistence-Based Clustering Algorithm
questions.question: In the ToMATo clustering algorithm, how does the hill-climbing step on the neighborhood graph G construct the directed subgraph and produce a candidate clustering of the point cloud X?
questions.question_ru: Как в алгоритме кластеризации ToMATo шаг восхождения (hill-climbing) на графе окрестностей $G$ строит ориентированный подграф и порождает кандидатное разбиение облака точек $X$?
questions.reference_answer: At each vertex $v$, ToMATo places a directed edge from $v$ to its neighbor with the highest estimated density $\hat{f}$, provided that value exceeds $\hat{f}(v)$; vertices whose neighbors all have lower values are peaks. These directed edges form a spanning forest of $G$ with one tree per local maximum of $\hat{f}$, partitioning $X$ into pairwise disjoint sets that serve as a candidate clustering.

evidence.text: 2. **Apply a hill-climbing algorithm on $G$.** Construct the neighborhood graph $G$ on the points of $X$, and construct a directed subgraph $\Gamma$ of $G$ as follows: at each vertex $v$ of $G$, place a directed edge from $v$ to its neighbor with highest value of $\hat{f}$, provided that that value is higher than $\hat{f}(v)$. If all neighbors of $v$ have lower values, $v$ is a peak of $\hat{f}$. This yields a collection of directed edges that form a spanning forest of the graph $G$, consisting of one tree for each local maximum of $\hat{f}$. In particular, these trees yield a partition of the elements of $X$ into pairwise disjoint sets that serves as a candidate clustering on $X$.

questions.doc_title: AuToMATo: An Out-Of-The-Box Persistence-Based Clustering Algorithm
questions.question: What stability inequality relates the persistence diagrams of two functions f and g to the sup-norm distance between the functions, and under which assumptions on (X, f) and (X, g) does it hold?
questions.question_ru: Какое неравенство устойчивости связывает диаграммы персистентности двух функций $f$ и $g$ с расстоянием между функциями в супремум-норме, и при каких предположениях относительно $(X, f)$ и $(X, g)$ оно выполняется?
questions.reference_answer: Persistence diagrams are stable: for functions $f,g\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$ one has $W_{\infty}(\textrm{Dgm}(X,f),\textrm{Dgm}(X,g))\leq\|f-g\|_{\infty}$. This holds, for example, if $f,g$ are Morse functions on compact manifolds or piecewise linear functions on simplicial complexes.

evidence.text:
Persistence diagrams are stable with respect to small perturbations [CSEH07], i.e. for ${f,g\colon X\to\mathbb{R}}$

$$
W_{\infty}(\textrm{Dgm}(X,f),\textrm{Dgm}(X,g))\leq\|f-g\|_{\infty}
$$

under certain assumptions on $(X,f)$ and $(X,g)$. This holds, for example, if $f,g$ are Morse functions on compact manifolds, piecewise linear functions on simplicial complexes, etc. There are versions of the stability result that hold more generally, for example [CdSO14, CdSMS16, CCSG+09].
section_path: AuToMATo: An Out-Of-The-Box Persistence-Based Clustering Algorithm

questions.doc_title: AuToMATo: An Out-Of-The-Box Persistence-Based Clustering Algorithm
questions.question: Why does AuToMATo use a default confidence level of α=0.35 (i.e. merely a 65% confidence region for the persistence diagram) rather than a more common value such as α=0.05?
questions.question_ru: Почему в AuToMATo по умолчанию используется уровень доверия $\alpha=0.35$ (то есть лишь 65%-я доверительная область для диаграммы персистентности), а не более обычное значение, например $\alpha=0.05$?
questions.reference_answer: The value α=0.35 yields a 65% confidence region that is low enough to offset the negative influence of possibly non-optimized neighborhood graph and density estimators, while still being high enough to give good results when those estimators are chosen suitably.

evidence.text: By default, AuToMATo performs the bootstrap on $B=1000$ subsamples of the input point cloud, and sets the confidence level to $\alpha=0.35$. The choice of this latter parameter means that AuToMATo determines merely a 65% confidence region for the persistence diagram produced by the underlying ToMATo instance. While in bootstrapping the confidence level is often set to e.g. $\alpha=0.05$, the seemingly strange choice of $\alpha=0.35$ in the setting of AuToMATo is justified by experiments. The value of 65% seems to be low enough to offset some of the negative influence of using possibly non-optimized neighborhood graph and density estimators discussed in Section 6, while at the same time being high enough to yield good results when these estimators are chosen suitably.
section_path: AuToMATo: An Out-Of-The-Box Persistence-Based Clustering Algorithm

questions.doc_title: Geodesic Sinkhorn for Fast and Accurate Optimal Transport on Manifolds
questions.question: How is the Geodesic Sinkhorn distance between two distributions $\mu$ and $\nu$ supported on a graph ${\mathcal{G}}$ defined, and which divergence and kernel appear in its formula?
questions.question_ru: Как определяется расстояние Geodesic Sinkhorn между двумя распределениями $\mu$ и $\nu$, заданными на графе ${\mathcal{G}}$, и какие дивергенция и ядро входят в его формулу?
questions.reference_answer: The Geodesic Sinkhorn distance is the entropy-regularized optimal transport that uses the graph heat kernel ${\bm{H}}_{t}$ as the kernel and the Kullback-Leibler divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$: $W_{{\bm{H}}_{t}}(\mu,\nu):=4t^{1/2}\left(1+\min_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi|{\bm{H}}_{t})\right)^{1/2}$.

evidence.text:
**Definition 4.1.** The Geodesic Sinkhorn distance between two distributions $\mu$, $\nu$ on a graph ${\mathcal{G}}$ is

$$
W_{{\bm{H}}_{t}}(\mu,\nu):=4t^{1/2}\left(1+\min_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi|{\bm{H}}_{t})\right)^{1/2}.
$$
section_path: Geodesic Sinkhorn for Fast and Accurate Optimal Transport on Manifolds

questions.doc_title: Geodesic Sinkhorn for Fast and Accurate Optimal Transport on Manifolds
questions.question: In Geodesic Sinkhorn, Chebyshev polynomials are used to approximate the application of the graph heat kernel ${\bm{H}}_{t}=e^{-t{\bm{L}}}$ to a signal. What is the recursive definition of these polynomials and what series expansion of ${\bm{H}}_{t}$ do they provide?
questions.question_ru: В методе Geodesic Sinkhorn полиномы Чебышёва используются для аппроксимации применения теплового ядра графа ${\bm{H}}_{t}=e^{-t{\bm{L}}}$ к сигналу. Каково рекуррентное определение этих полиномов и какое разложение в ряд для ${\bm{H}}_{t}$ они дают?
questions.reference_answer: The Chebyshev polynomials satisfy $T_{0}(y)=0$, $T_{1}(y)=y$, and $T_{k}(y)=2yT_{k-1}(y)-T_{k-2}(y)$ for $k\geq 2$. Assuming the largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{n}\leq 2$, they express the heat operator as ${\bm{H}}_{t}=\frac{b_{0}}{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}b_{k}T_{k}({\bm{L}}-\bm{Id})$, with the approximation error decaying exponentially in the maximum degree $K$.

evidence.text:
Polynomial sequences are often used to approximate functions or operator. With Chebyshev polynomials, we can approximate the application of the matrix exponential ${\bm{H}}_{t}=e^{-t{\bm{L}}}$ to a signal ${\bm{f}}$ on the graph. An attractive property of Chebyshev polynomials is that the approximation error decays exponentially with the maximum degree $K$. They are defined by the recursive relation $\{T_{k}\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ with $T_{0}(y)=0$, $T_{1}(y)=y$ and $T_{k}(y)=2yT_{k-1}(y)-T_{k-2}(y)$ for $k\geq 2$. On $[-1,1]$ these polynomials are orthogonal w.r.t. the weight $(1-y)^{-1/2}$, and can be used to express the operator ${\bm{H}}_{t}$. Assuming the largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{n}\leq 2$, we can write

$$
{\bm{H}}_{t}=\frac{b_{0}}{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}b_{k}T_{k}({\bm{L}}-\bm{Id}),
$$

questions.doc_title: Geodesic Sinkhorn for Fast and Accurate Optimal Transport on Manifolds
questions.question: According to Varadhan's formula, how can the geodesic distance on a manifold be recovered from the heat kernel, and what heat-geodesic distance and associated kernel does this motivate for entropy-regularized optimal transport?
questions.question_ru: Согласно формуле Варадана, как геодезическое расстояние на многообразии восстанавливается из теплового ядра и какое тепловое геодезическое расстояние и связанное с ним ядро это мотивирует для энтропийно-регуляризованного оптимального транспорта?
questions.reference_answer: Varadhan's formula recovers the squared geodesic distance from heat transfer at small timescales as $d(x,y)^{2}=\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}-4t\ln\mathcal{H}_{t}(x,y)$. This motivates the heat-geodesic distance $d_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}(x,y):=-4t\ln\mathcal{H}_{t}(x,y)$ with associated kernel $K_{\lambda}(x,y)=\mathcal{H}_{\lambda/4}(x,y)$.

evidence.text:
The underlying metric $d(\cdot,\cdot)$ is generally unknown, thus the kernel $K_{\lambda}$ cannot be evaluated. The authors of [33] proposed to approximate $K_{\lambda}$ with the heat kernel $\mathcal{H}_{t}(x,y)$ on ${\mathcal{X}}$. According to Varadhan’s formula [39], the geodesic distance on a manifold can be recovered from the heat transfer at small timescales as

$$
d(x,y)^{2}=\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}-4t\ln\mathcal{H}_{t}(x,y). \tag{5}
$$

Hence, motivating the use of the heat-geodesic distance $d_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}(x,y):=-4t\ln\mathcal{H}_{t}(x,y)$, with associated kernel $K_{\lambda}(x,y)=\mathcal{H}_{\lambda/4}(x,y).$
