questions.doc_title: Cycle Registration in Persistent Homology with Applications in Topological Bootstrap
questions.question: In the cycle-registration framework for topological data analysis, under what condition are a $k$-cycle $\gamma$ in a space $X$ and a $k$-cycle $\delta$ in a space $Y$ said to match via a third reference space $Z$, using the induced homology maps $f_*: H_k(X)\to H_k(Z)$ and $g_*: H_k(Y)\to H_k(Z)$?
questions.question_ru: В рамках метода регистрации циклов в топологическом анализе данных при каком условии $k$-цикл $\gamma$ в пространстве $X$ и $k$-цикл $\delta$ в пространстве $Y$ считаются совпадающими через третье опорное пространство $Z$ с использованием индуцированных гомоморфизмов гомологий $f_*: H_k(X)\to H_k(Z)$ и $g_*: H_k(Y)\to H_k(Z)$?
questions.reference_answer: A $k$-cycle $\gamma\in H_k(X)$ and a $k$-cycle $\delta\in H_k(Y)$ match via $Z$ if their images under the induced maps are equal and nontrivial, that is $[f_{*}(\gamma)]=[g_{*}(\delta)]\neq[0]$; this relation is denoted $\gamma\overset{Z}{\sim}\delta$.

evidence.text:
**Definition 4.1.** Let $\gamma\in H_{k}(X)$ and $\delta\in H_{k}(Y)$. We say that $\gamma$ and $\delta$ match via $Z$ if

$$
[f_{*}(\gamma)]=[g_{*}(\delta)]\neq[0].
$$

We denote this by $\gamma\overset{Z}{\sim}\delta$.

questions.doc_title: Cycle Registration in Persistent Homology with Applications in Topological Bootstrap
questions.question: In persistent homology, what is a Morse filtration? State the conditions it imposes on the homology groups $H_k(X_t)$ of a filtration $\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ and on its Betti numbers $\beta_k$.
questions.question_ru: Что такое фильтрация Морса в персистентной гомологии? Сформулируйте условия, которые она накладывает на группы гомологий $H_k(X_t)$ фильтрации $\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ и на её числа Бетти $\beta_k$.
questions.reference_answer: A filtration is a Morse filtration if there exists a finite set $T_c$ such that outside $T_c$ the inclusion-induced map $i_*: H_k(X_{t-\epsilon'})\to H_k(X_{t+\epsilon'})$ is an isomorphism (homology does not change), while at each $t\in T_c$ this map is either injective with $\beta_k(X_{t+\epsilon'})=\beta_k(X_{t-\epsilon'})+1$ or surjective with $\beta_k(X_{t+\epsilon'})=\beta_k(X_{t-\epsilon'})-1$; that is, only a single cycle is created or terminated at each critical value.

evidence.text:
**Definition 4.4 (Morse filtration).** We say that a filtration $\{{X}_{t}\}_{t\in{\mathbb{R}}}$ is a **Morse filtration** if there exists a finite set $T_{c}\subset{\mathbb{R}}$, that satisfies the following.

1. For all $t\not\in T_{c}$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ small enough so that for any $0<\epsilon^{\prime}<\epsilon$, the map $i_{*}:H_{k}(X_{t-\epsilon^{\prime}})\to H_{k}(X_{t+\epsilon^{\prime}})$ induced by inclusion is an isomorphism. In other words, homology does not change at $t$.

2. For all $t\in T_{c}$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ small enough so that for any $0<\epsilon^{\prime}<\epsilon$, either

$$
\begin{split}&i_{*}:H_{k}(X_{t-\epsilon^{\prime}})\to H_{k}(X_{t+\epsilon^{\prime}})\text{ is injective, and }\beta_{k}(X_{t+\epsilon^{\prime}})=\beta_{k}(X_{t-\epsilon^{\prime}})+1,\text{ or}\\ &i_{*}:H_{k}(X_{t-\epsilon^{\prime}})\to H_{k}(X_{t+\epsilon^{\prime}})\text{ is surjective, and }\beta_{k}(X_{t+\epsilon^{\prime}})=\beta_{k}(X_{t-\epsilon^{\prime}})-1.\end{split}
$$

questions.doc_title: Cycle Registration in Persistent Homology with Applications in Topological Bootstrap
questions.question: Why does defining the significance of a persistent cycle solely as the probability that it reappears in a new sample fail to distinguish topological signal from noise as the sample size grows large?
questions.question_ru: Почему определение значимости персистентного цикла только через вероятность его повторного появления в новой выборке не позволяет отличить топологический сигнал от шума при увеличении размера выборки?
questions.reference_answer: As the sample size grows, large noisy cycles — whose generators are composed of a large number of simplexes and enclose a large amount of volume — tend to reappear frequently, since they are more likely to have overlapping cycles in an additional sample; this frequent reappearance makes the probability measure unable to differentiate signal from noise.

evidence.text: Our initial proposal was to represent this likelihood using the probability that an observed persistent cycle will reappear in a new sample. However, while experimenting with data, we noticed that as the sample size grows noisy generators tend to reappear frequently (see Figure 14), making it impossible to differentiate signal from noise. This phenomenon occurs due to the fact that large noisy cycles, i.e. cycles whose generators composed of a large number of simplexes, are more likely to appear in large samples. As can be seen in Figure 14, each of these cycles encloses a large amount of ‘volume’. Hence, they are more likely to have overlapping cycles in an additional sample, which in turn results in a greater chance for a match.

questions.doc_title: Unsupervised Latent Space Alignment with Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching
questions.question: In the latent space alignment method Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA), what exact objective function $J_{\sigma}(R)$ over orthonormal matrices $R\in O(d)$ is maximized in order to fit one normalized point set to another?
questions.question_ru: В методе выравнивания латентных пространств Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA), какую именно целевую функцию $J_{\sigma}(R)$ по ортогональным матрицам $R\in O(d)$ максимизируют, чтобы совместить одно нормированное множество точек с другим?
questions.reference_answer: HGA maximizes $J_{\sigma}(R)=\frac{1}{mn}\sum_{i,j}\exp\left(-\frac{\arccos^{2}((R\hat{S}_{\mathcal{M}}^{T})^{T}\hat{S}_{\mathcal{N}}^{T})_{ij}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)$, i.e. the average over all point pairs of an unnormalized Gaussian kernel of the geodesic (arccosine) distance between the rotated source points $R\hat{S}_{\mathcal{M}}$ and the target points $\hat{S}_{\mathcal{N}}$, with the optimum given by $\text{argmax}_{R\in O(d)}J_{\sigma}(R)$.

evidence.text:
Using geodesic distances on the unit sphere, we calculate the unnormalized Gaussian Kernel between each point:

$$
\exp\left(-\frac{\arccos^{2}\big(\!\big(R\hat{S}_{\mathcal{M}}^{T}\big)^{T}\hat{S}_{\mathcal{N}}^{T}\big)_{ij}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)
$$

We then average the sum over all pairs of points between the two spaces. This total affinity is our objective function:

$$
J_{\sigma}(R)=\frac{1}{mn}\sum_{i,j}\exp\left(-\frac{\arccos^{2}\big(\!\big(R\hat{S}_{\mathcal{M}}^{T}\big)^{T}\hat{S}_{\mathcal{N}}^{T}\big)_{ij}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)
$$

The goal of our optimization algorithm is find $\text{argmax}_{R\in O(d)}J_{\sigma}(R)$.
section_path: Unsupervised Latent Space Alignment with Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching

questions.doc_title: Unsupervised Latent Space Alignment with Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching
questions.question: Why does the Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA) optimization use a bandwidth continuation strategy that starts with a large kernel bandwidth $\sigma$ and progressively decreases it over the course of the optimization?
questions.question_ru: Почему в оптимизации Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA) используется стратегия продолжения по ширине ядра, которая начинается с большой ширины $\sigma$ и постепенно уменьшает её в ходе оптимизации?
questions.reference_answer: At large $\sigma$ the objective $J_\sigma$ is highly smooth, considers many pairs and is nearly concave, while at smaller $\sigma$ it only considers local nearby pairs and is highly nonconcave. The schedule lowers $\sigma$ through a sequence and initializes each stage from the previous solution, so the process can be seen as a continuation from global distribution alignment, to cluster alignment, to local point alignment.

evidence.text:
Instead of optimizing a single kernel, we lower the $\sigma$ hyperparameter, solving a sequence:

$$
\sigma_{1}>\sigma_{2}>\cdots>\sigma_{L}
$$

And at each stage, we initialize from the previous solution. Intuitively, at large $\sigma$, the objective function $J_{\sigma}$ will be highly smooth, considering many pairs and will be nearly concave. At smaller $\sigma$, it will only consider local nearby pairs and therefore be highly nonconcave. We can think of this process as a continuation from global distribution alignment, to cluster alignment, to local point alignment.

questions.question: When aligning English and French FastText word embeddings using a small number of anchor word pairs, how does Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA) compare with Latent Functional Maps (LFM) at translating words that are not present in the anchor set?
questions.question_ru: При выравнивании английских и французских векторных представлений слов FastText с использованием небольшого числа якорных пар слов, как Hyperspherical Geodesic Alignment (HGA) соотносится с Latent Functional Maps (LFM) при переводе слов, отсутствующих в наборе якорей?
questions.reference_answer: With extremely few anchors HGA finds word correspondences much better than the other methods: while other methods can effectively align the latent space only for particular words, HGA uses anchor labels as well as geometric information about the two latent spaces in order to translate words that are not anchored.

evidence.text: We find that in the setting of extremely few anchors, HGA manages much better at finding word correspondences, as seen in Figure 1. Qualitatively, we can see how this works in Figure 6. While other methods can effectively align the latent space for particular words, HGA manages to use anchor labels as well as geometric information about the two latent spaces in order to translate words that are not anchored.

questions.doc_title: Can Push-forward Generative Models Fit Multimodal Distributions?
questions.question: In the study of push-forward measures, how is the γ-surface area of a Borel set A defined for a probability measure γ, and how can it be interpreted?
questions.question_ru: Как в исследовании push-forward мер определяется γ-площадь поверхности борелевского множества A для вероятностной меры γ и как её можно интерпретировать?
questions.reference_answer: For a probability measure γ and a Borel set A, the γ-surface area is γ⁺(∂A) = liminf_{ε→0⁺} (γ(A_ε) − γ(A))/ε, where A_ε = {x : ∃a∈A, ‖x−a‖≤ε} is the ε-extension of A and ∂A is its boundary. It can be interpreted as the mass of γ on the hypersurface ∂A.

evidence.text:
First, for any probability measure $\gamma$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and any Borel set $\mathsf{A}$ of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we define the $\gamma$-surface area of $\mathsf{A}$ by

$$
\textstyle{\gamma^{+}(\partial\mathsf{A})=\liminf_{\varepsilon\rightarrow 0^{+}}(\gamma(\mathsf{A}_{\varepsilon})-\gamma(\mathsf{A}))/\varepsilon\;,} \tag{4}
$$

where $\mathsf{A}_{\varepsilon}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\,:\;\textrm{there exists }a\in\mathsf{A},\ \|x-a\|\leq\varepsilon\}$ is the $\varepsilon$-extension of $\mathsf{A}$ and $\partial\mathsf{A}$ is the boundary of $A$. The $\gamma$ - surface area can be interpreted as the mass of $\gamma$ on the hypersurface $\partial\mathsf{A}$.

questions.doc_title: Can Push-forward Generative Models Fit Multimodal Distributions?
questions.question: What happens when spectral normalization is applied to the generator of a GAN trained on a multimodal distribution, and what is this behavior called?
questions.question_ru: Что происходит, когда спектральная нормализация применяется к генератору GAN, обученного на мультимодальном распределении, и как называется такое поведение?
questions.reference_answer: This technique cannot be used when training GANs on multimodal distributions: because spectral normalization constrains the Lipschitz constant of the generator to be smaller than 1, the GAN is trained towards concentrating in one of the modes of the distribution over interpolating massively between them. This has been referred to as mode dropping.

evidence.text: Odena et al., 2018 suggested that the magnitude of the norm of the generator jacobian may be causally related to instability and mode collapse. This is why many state-of-the-art GANs apply spectral normalization Miyato et al., 2018 on their generators. In Figure 4 (left), we show that this technique cannot be used when training GANs on multimodal distributions: since spectral normalization constraints the Lipschitz constant of the generator to be smaller than $1$, the GAN is trained towards concentrating in one of the modes of the distribution over interpolating massively between them. This has been referred to as *mode dropping* by Khayatkhoei et al., 2018.

questions.doc_title: Cluster-Aware Matching via Laplacian Optimal Transport
questions.question: What is the objective function minimized by Laplacian Optimal Transport (LapOT), and how does it relate to entropic optimal transport?
questions.question_ru: Какую целевую функцию минимизирует задача Laplacian Optimal Transport (LapOT) и как она связана с энтропийным оптимальным транспортом?
questions.reference_answer: Laplacian Optimal Transport minimizes, over couplings π in Π_{a,b}, the quantity ⟨π,C⟩ + λx⟨π,LXπ⟩ + λy⟨π,πLY⟩ − λH(π), where λx, λy, λ > 0 are hyperparameters controlling the regularization strength. It is a generalization of entropic OT: when λx = λy = 0, LapOT reduces to entropic OT.

evidence.text:
In summary, given any $a\in\Delta_{n}$, $b\in\Delta_{m}$, $C\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, and $L_{X},L_{Y}$ defined as above, we define LapOT as follows:

$$
\mathsf{LapOT}_{\lambda_{x},\lambda_{y},\lambda}(a,b,C,L_{X},L_{Y})\triangleq\min_{\pi\in\Pi_{a,b}}\langle\pi,C\rangle+\lambda_{x}\langle\pi,L_{X}\pi\rangle+\lambda_{y}\langle\pi,\pi L_{Y}\rangle-\lambda H(\pi), \tag{6}
$$

where $\lambda_{x},\lambda_{y},\lambda>0$ are hyperparameters that control the strength of the regularization. We can view LapOT as a generalization of entropic OT: when $\lambda_{x}=\lambda_{y}=0$, LapOT reduces to entropic OT.

questions.doc_title: Cluster-Aware Matching via Laplacian Optimal Transport
questions.question: In Refined Simultaneous Clustering (RSC), after computing the optimal coupling via Laplacian Optimal Transport, how are the input similarity matrices and graph Laplacians modified before the final spectral clustering step?
questions.question_ru: В методе Refined Simultaneous Clustering (RSC) после вычисления оптимальной связки с помощью Laplacian Optimal Transport как модифицируются входные матрицы сходства и графовые лапласианы перед финальным шагом спектральной кластеризации?
questions.reference_answer: RSC refines the input similarity matrices K_X and K_Y by multiplying them element-wise with the switch matrices π^X_switch and π^Y_switch, then recalculates the refined graph Laplacians L̃_X and L̃_Y from the refined similarity matrices K̃_X and K̃_Y, followed by usual spectral clustering to obtain the final clusters of X and Y.

evidence.text: By applying k-means to the rows (resp. columns) of $\pi^{\star}$, we cluster together points in $X$ (resp. $Y$) that have a similar fuzzy matching with $Y$ (resp. $X$). Then, in Step 4 of Algorithm 1, we refine the original input similarity matrices $K_{X}$ and $K_{Y}$ by multiplying them element-wise with the switch matrices $\pi^{X}_{\mathsf{switch}}$ and $\pi^{Y}_{\mathsf{switch}}$, respectively. Then, we recalculate the refined graph Laplacians $\tilde{L}_{X}$ and $\tilde{L}_{Y}$ based on the refined similarity matrices $\tilde{K}_{X}$ and $\tilde{K}_{Y}$, followed by the usual spectral clustering procedure to obtain the final clusters of $X$ and $Y$.

questions.doc_title: Cluster-Aware Matching via Laplacian Optimal Transport
questions.question: Why is it problematic to obtain a region-to-region alignment by first clustering each point cloud independently and then matching the resulting clusters?
questions.question_ru: Почему проблематично получать выравнивание регион-регион, сначала кластеризуя каждое облако точек независимо, а затем сопоставляя полученные кластеры?
questions.reference_answer: This two-stage approach is problematic because clustering algorithms are unstable, which leads to inconsistent partitions across the point sets and severely degrades the quality of the subsequent matching. This motivates a cluster-aware matching framework that integrates cluster-structure information directly into the matching process.

evidence.text: A natural yet naive approach to achieve such a region-level alignment would be to first cluster each point cloud independently and then match the resulting clusters. However, this two-stage approach can be extremely problematic due to the instability of clustering algorithms [3, 34, 49], leading to inconsistent partitions across the point sets, which in turn severely degrades the quality of the subsequent matching. This instability is illustrated in Figure 1(a), where independent clustering fails to produce consistent partitions for two similar shapes. This motivates the need for a cluster-aware matching framework that integrates information about the cluster structure directly into the matching process.

questions.doc_title: It's a (Blind) Match! Towards Vision-Language Correspondence without Parallel Data
questions.question: How is the problem of matching vision and language embeddings without any paired data formalized as a quadratic assignment problem, and what define the permutation space Π^N and the set of permutation matrices P_N in this formulation?
questions.question_ru: Как задача сопоставления (matching) визуальных и языковых эмбеддингов без парных данных формализуется как задача квадратичного назначения (QAP), и что определяют пространство перестановок Π^N и множество матриц перестановок P_N в этой формулировке?
questions.reference_answer: Blind vision-language matching is cast as finding the permutation of indices that minimizes the summed pairwise distortion between the within-modality similarity matrices X and Y, i.e. π* = argmin_π Σ_{i,j} l(X_ij, Y_{π(i)π(j)}). Equivalently, using permutation matrices P ∈ P_N, it becomes the QAP P* = argmin_{P∈P_N} Σ_{i,j,k,l} l(X_ik, Y_jl) P_ij P_kl, where P_N is the set of binary matrices whose rows and columns each sum to one.

evidence.text:
Given unpaired vision and language data points, $\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\}$ and $\{\mathbf{y}_{i}\}$, we aim to find the permutation of rows and columns that minimizes their pairwise distortion, *i.e*.

$$
\displaystyle\pi^{*}\in \displaystyle\argmin_{\pi\in\Pi^{N}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{N}l\left(\mathbf{X}_{ij},\mathbf{Y}_{\pi(i)\pi(j)}\right), \tag{5}
$$

where $\Pi^{N}$ is the permutation space, defined by bijective mappings from $\{1,\dots,N\}^{N}$ to $\{1,\dots,N\}^{N}$. This is a quadratic assignment problem (QAP), since by exchanging the permutation space with permutation matrices, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle\mathbf{P}^{*}\in\argmin_{\mathbf{P}\in\mathcal{P}_{N}}\sum_{i,j,k,l=1}^{N}l\left(\mathbf{X}_{ik},\mathbf{Y}_{jl}\right)\mathbf{P}_{ij}\mathbf{P}_{kl}. \tag{6}
$$

Here, $\mathcal{P}_{N}$ is the group of permutation matrices, *i.e*. binary matrices in which the columns and the rows sum up to one:

$$
\mathcal{P}_{N}=\{\mathbf{P}\mid\mathbf{P}\in\{0,1\}^{N\times N},\mathbf{P}\mathbbm{1}=\mathbbm{1},\mathbf{P}^{T}\mathbbm{1}=\mathbbm{1}\}. \tag{7}
$$

questions.doc_title: It's a (Blind) Match! Towards Vision-Language Correspondence without Parallel Data
questions.question: What are the three key extensions that the factorized Hahn-Grant solver introduces over the original Hahn-Grant solver for vision-language matching, and in which two stages does it search for primal solutions?
questions.question_ru: Какие три ключевых расширения вносит факторизованный решатель Хана–Гранта (factorized Hahn-Grant solver) по сравнению с исходным решателем Хана–Гранта для сопоставления зрения и языка, и в два этапа он ищет прямые (primal) решения?
questions.reference_answer: The factorized solver adds three extensions: (1) it also searches for primal solutions, (2) it reduces memory complexity from O(N^4) to O(N^3), and (3) it uses a faster solver for the linear assignment problems (LAPs). It searches for primal solutions in two stages: first it initializes with the FAQ and 2opt heuristics using the best result from 100 random seeds, and second it evaluates the solution of each LAP on the QAP objective.

evidence.text:
We adapt the Hahn-Grant solver for vision-language matching with three key extensions: *(1)* We also search for primal solutions, *(2)* reduce the memory complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^{4})$ to $\mathcal{O}(N^{3})$, and *(3)* use a faster solver for the LAPs.

We search for primal solutions in two stages. First, we initialize the problem with the FAQ Vogelstein et al. 2015 and 2opt Croes 1958 heuristics, using the best result from 100 random seeds (Line 4). Second, we evaluate the solutions of each LAP on the QAP (Line 7 and Line 14). This does not add considerable overhead, because the assignment was already calculated as a by-product. Therefore, we only need to evaluate the QAP objective functions once more. If the algorithm converges to a solution, that solution also needs to solve at least one of the LAPs Hahn and Grant 1998, and our heuristic will find the global optimum. If the algorithm does not converge, we output the lowest-cost solution found during the run.

questions.doc_title: It's a (Blind) Match! Towards Vision-Language Correspondence without Parallel Data
questions.question: Under what condition on the distortion measure l(·,·) can the quadratic assignment problem for blind vision-language matching be rewritten as a Koopmans-Beckmann QAP with two cost matrices C^(1) and C^(2), and what are those matrices?
questions.question_ru: При каком условии на меру искажения l(·,·) задача квадратичного назначения для слепого сопоставления зрения и языка может быть переписана как QAP Купманса–Бекмана (Koopmans-Beckmann) с двумя матрицами стоимостей C^(1) и C^(2), и что это за матрицы?
questions.reference_answer: The reduction applies whenever the distortion measure is decomposable as l(A,B) = f_1(A) + f_2(B) − h_1(A)h_2(B), which includes the squared L_2 distance, the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and the negative Frobenius inner product used for CKA and Mutual k-NN. The QAP then becomes a Koopmans-Beckmann QAP with cost matrices C^(1) = −h_1(X) and C^(2) = h_2(Y).

evidence.text:
To reduce the memory requirements, we first observe that the commonly used distortion measures $l(\cdot,\cdot)$ are decomposable as

$$
l(A,B)=f_{1}(A)+f_{2}(B)-h_{1}(A)h_{2}(B). \tag{9}
$$

This includes the squared $L_{2}$-distance, Kullback-Leibler divergence Peyré et al. 2016, and the negative Frobenius inner product, which we use for the centered kernel alignment (CKA) and the Mutual k-NN. Given such a decomposable measure, the original QAP is equivalent to

$$
\displaystyle\mathbf{P}^{*}\in\argmin_{\mathbf{P}\in\mathcal{P}_{N}}\sum_{i,j,k,l=1}^{N}\mathbf{C}^{(1)}_{ik}\mathbf{C}^{(2)}_{jl}\mathbf{P}_{ij}\mathbf{P}_{kl}. \tag{10}
$$

This is an instance of a Koopmans-Beckmann QAP Koopmans and Beckmann 1957 with cost matrices $\mathbf{C}^{(1)}=-h_{1}(\mathbf{X})$ and $\mathbf{C}^{(2)}=h_{2}(\mathbf{Y})$.

questions.question: What objective does the Wasserstein Procrustes procedure minimize when jointly estimating a semi-orthogonal matrix ${ m{W}}$ and a transport plan ${ m{T}}$ between two sets of embeddings from independently trained models, and how is the optimal map obtained once a correspondence is fixed?
questions.question_ru: Какую целевую функцию минимизирует процедура Wasserstein Procrustes при совместном оценивании полуортогональной матрицы ${ m{W}}$ и транспортного плана ${ m{T}}$ между двумя множествами эмбеддингов независимо обученных моделей, и как получается оптимальное отображение при фиксированном соответствии?
questions.reference_answer: It minimizes $\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{m}{\bm{T}}_{ij}\|{\bm{W}}{\bm{x}}_{i}-{\bm{y}}_{j}\|_{2}^{2}$ over ${\bm{W}}\in\St(d_{X},d_{Y})$ and ${\bm{T}}\in\Pi({\bm{a}},{\bm{b}})$, equivalently maximizing $\Tr({\bm{X}}{\bm{W}}{\bm{Y}}^{\top}{\bm{T}}^{\top})$. Given a correspondence, the optimal map is the closed-form orthogonal Procrustes solution, and given a map, the optimal correspondence comes from linear assignment.

evidence.text:
**Wasserstein Procrustes.**  We jointly estimate a map ${\bm{W}}$ and a transport plan ${\bm{T}}\in\Pi({\bm{a}},{\bm{b}})$:

$$
{\bm{W}}^{\text{WP}},{\bm{T}}^{\text{WP}}\in\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\argmin_{{\bm{W}}\in\St(d_{X},d_{Y}),\;{\bm{T}}\in\Pi({\bm{a}},{\bm{b}})}\;\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{m}{\bm{T}}_{ij}\|{\bm{W}}{\bm{x}}_{i}-{\bm{y}}_{j}\|_{2}^{2}=\argmax\Tr({\bm{X}}{\bm{W}}{\bm{Y}}^{\top}{\bm{T}}^{\top}), \tag{1}
$$

with ${\bm{W}}\in\St(d_{X},d_{Y})$ a semi-orthogonal matrix. Given a correspondence, the optimal map is given in closed form by orthogonal Procrustes (Schönemann, 1966). Given a map, the optimal correspondence is found by linear assignment.

questions.doc_title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data
questions.question: In the coarse geometric initialization used to align two unpaired embedding spaces across modalities, how are cluster centers obtained and matched to produce an initial correspondence?
questions.question_ru: В грубой геометрической инициализации, используемой для выравнивания двух непарных пространств эмбеддингов разных модальностей, как получаются и сопоставляются центры кластеров для построения начального соответствия?
questions.reference_answer: For each of $S$ repetitions, both embedding spaces are independently sampled and clustered into $C$ centers ${\bm{A}}_{s}$ and ${\bm{B}}_{s}$ with $k$-means, and the centers are matched by the permutation ${\bm{P}}_{s}$ that maximizes their linear CKA, $\argmax_{{\bm{P}}\in\mathcal{P}_{C}}\cka({\bm{A}}_{s},{\bm{P}}{\bm{B}}_{s})$, which is a quadratic assignment problem (QAP).

evidence.text: **Coarse geometric initialization.**  We build on the cluster initialization of mini-vec2vec (Dar, 2025). For each of $S$ repetitions, we independently sample and cluster both spaces into $C$ centers ${\bm{A}}_{s}$ and ${\bm{B}}_{s}$ with $k$-means (Line 6). We match the centers by the permutation that maximizes their linear CKA, ${\bm{P}}_{s}\in\argmax_{{\bm{P}}\in\mathcal{P}_{C}}\cka({\bm{A}}_{s},{\bm{P}}{\bm{B}}_{s})$ (Line 7). This is a quadratic assignment problem (QAP). We replace 2-opt (Croes, 1958) with multiple initializations from mini-vec2vec with MPOpt with its primal heuristic (Hutschenreiter et al., 2021), since our ablations show that the quality of the QAP solution is the most important algorithmic choice (*cf*. Sec. A.2).

questions.doc_title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data
questions.question: According to the discussion of the shared-geometry approach to unpaired cross-modal alignment, why does the geometric similarity of two embedding spaces determine whether alignment succeeds, and what key limitation prevents deciding from unpaired data alone whether two spaces are alignable?
questions.question_ru: Согласно обсуждению подхода, основанного на общей геометрии, к непарному кросс-модальному выравниванию, почему геометрическое сходство двух пространств эмбеддингов определяет успех выравнивания и какое ключевое ограничение не позволяет по одним лишь непарным данным решить, выравниваемы ли два пространства?
questions.reference_answer: Related semantics alone are insufficient; both embedding spaces must also organize them in a similar geometric structure, and CKA strongly predicts alignment performance, which explains why unpaired alignment succeeds. The limitation is that one cannot reliably determine from unpaired data alone whether two spaces are sufficiently similar to be aligned, because usual alignment metrics need matching samples; developing fully unsupervised alignment prediction scores remains an open problem.

evidence.text: **What enables unpaired cross-modal alignment?**  Related semantics alone seem insufficient: both embedding spaces must also organize them in a similar geometric structure, as supported by our experiments, where CKA strongly predict our aligner’s performance. Models with more similar geometry are consistently better aligned. This relationship holds experimentally beyond vision and language, suggesting that the role of shared geometry is not specific to a particular pair of modalities. Thus, geometric similarity explains why unpaired alignment succeeds. This also highlights an important limitation. Currently, we cannot reliably determine from unpaired data alone whether two spaces are sufficiently similar to be aligned, as usual alignment metrics need matching samples. Developing fully unsupervised alignment prediction scores remains an open problem.

questions.doc_title: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching
questions.question: What is the Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) procedure for solving the Schrödinger Bridge problem, what must the initializing path measure satisfy, and which property do the iterates preserve that Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) does not?
questions.question_ru: В чём состоит процедура Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) для решения задачи Шрёдингера (Schrödinger Bridge), чему должна удовлетворять инициализирующая мера пути, и какое свойство сохраняют итерации IMF, в отличие от Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF)?
questions.reference_answer: IMF alternates Markovian and reciprocal projections via $\mathbb{P}^{2n+1}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\mathbb{P}^{2n})$ and $\mathbb{P}^{2n+2}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{Q})}(\mathbb{P}^{2n+1})$, starting from $\mathbb{P}^{0}$ with $\mathbb{P}^{0}_{0}=\pi_{0}$, $\mathbb{P}^{0}_{T}=\pi_{T}$ and $\mathbb{P}^{0}\in\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{Q})$. For every $n$, the iterates preserve the initial and terminal marginals $\mathbb{P}^{n}_{0}=\pi_{0}$, $\mathbb{P}^{n}_{T}=\pi_{T}$, whereas IPF does not preserve them.

evidence.text:
Based on Section 3.1, we propose a novel methodology called *Iterative Markovian Fitting* (IMF) to solve Schrödinger Bridges. We consider a sequence $(\mathbb{P}^{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that

$$
\mathbb{P}^{2n+1}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{M}}(\mathbb{P}^{2n}),\qquad\mathbb{P}^{2n+2}=\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{Q})}(\mathbb{P}^{2n+1}), \tag{14}
$$

with $\mathbb{P}^{0}$ such that $\mathbb{P}^{0}_{0}=\pi_{0}$, $\mathbb{P}^{0}_{T}=\pi_{T}$ and $\mathbb{P}^{0}\in\mathcal{R}(\mathbb{Q})$. These updates correspond to alternatively performing Markovian projections and reciprocal projections.

Combining Section 3.1 and Section 3.1, we get that for any $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{P}^{n}_{0}=\pi_{0}$ and $\mathbb{P}^{n}_{T}=\pi_{T}$. This property is in contrast to the IPF algorithm (10) for which the marginals at the initial and final times are *not* preserved.

questions.doc_title: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching
questions.question: What convergence guarantee does Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) provide for solving the Schrödinger Bridge problem, according to its convergence theorem?
questions.question_ru: Какую гарантию сходимости даёт Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) для решения задачи Шрёдингера согласно теореме о сходимости?
questions.reference_answer: Under mild assumptions, the IMF sequence admits a unique fixed point equal to the Schrödinger Bridge, $\mathbb{P}^{\star}=\mathbb{P}^{\textup{SB}}$, and the reverse KL divergence vanishes, $\lim_{n\to+\infty}\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb{P}^{n}|\mathbb{P}^{\star})=0$.

evidence.text:
Using Section 3.2, we finally prove the convergence of the IMF sequence $(\mathbb{P}^{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ to the Schrödinger Bridge. This result was first shown in the concurrent work (Peluchetti, 2023, Theorem 2). We present a simpler proof in Section C.6.

**Theorem 8.** Under mild assumptions, the IMF sequence $(\mathbb{P}^{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ admits a unique fixed point $\mathbb{P}^{\star}=\mathbb{P}^{\textup{SB}}$, and $\lim_{n\to+\infty}\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb{P}^{n}|\mathbb{P}^{\star})=0$.

questions.doc_title: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching
questions.question: What is the key theoretical distinction between Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching (DSBM) and Rectified Flow, and what does it imply about whether Rectified Flow converges to the dynamic optimal transport solution?
questions.question_ru: В чём ключевое теоретическое различие между Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching (DSBM) и Rectified Flow, и что оно означает для вопроса о сходимости Rectified Flow к решению задачи динамического оптимального переноса?
questions.reference_answer: DSBM adopts an SDE approach whereas Rectified Flow uses an ODE; because the uniqueness characterization of the Schrödinger Bridge is valid only when $\sigma_{t}>0$, Rectified Flow is not guaranteed to converge to the dynamic optimal transport solution, while DSBM connects to OT through its entropy-regularized version.

evidence.text: Firstly, we adopt the SDE approach as opposed to the ODE approach in Rectified Flow. This distinction is crucial in theory, as Section 3.1, which guarantees the uniqueness of the characterization of SB, is valid only when $\sigma_{t}>0$. Consequently, Rectified Flow is not guaranteed to converge to the dynamic optimal transport solution (see e.g. counterexample in Liu, 2022). In a following work, Liu, 2022 established formal connections between Rectified Flow and OT when restricting the class of vector fields to gradient fields. In DSBM, the connection to OT is obtained by considering its entropy-regularized version. Furthermore, by adopting the SDE approach, we observe significant improvements of sample quality in our experiments when performing transport between two general distributions. This is in line with the theoretical analysis in Albergo et al., 2023.

questions.doc_title: Towards Identifiable Unsupervised Domain Translation: A Diversified Distribution Matching Approach
questions.question: How is a measure-preserving automorphism (MPA) of a probability measure $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}$ defined, and what is the explicit MPA of a one-dimensional Gaussian distribution $x\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$?
questions.question_ru: Как определяется сохраняющий меру автоморфизм (MPA) вероятностной меры $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}$, и каков явный MPA одномерного гауссовского распределения $x\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$?
questions.reference_answer: An MPA of $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}$ is a continuous function $\bm{h}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X}$ whose push-forward leaves the measure unchanged, i.e. $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}=\bm{h}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}}$; equivalently, its output has the same PDF as $p(\bm{x})$. For a one-dimensional Gaussian $x\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$, the MPA is the reflection $h(x)=-x+2\mu$.

evidence.text:
**Definition 2.** (MPA) A measure-preserving automorphism (MPA) of $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}$ is a continuous function $\bm{h}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X}$ such that $\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}=\bm{h}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}}}$.

Simply speaking, MPA defined in this work is the continuous transformation $\bm{h}(\bm{x})$ whose output has the same PDF as $p(\bm{x})$. Take the one-dimensional Gaussian distribution $x\sim{\cal N}(\mu,\sigma^{2})$ as an example. The MPA of ${\cal N}(\mu,\sigma^{2})$ is $h(x)=-x+2\mu$.

questions.doc_title: Towards Identifiable Unsupervised Domain Translation: A Diversified Distribution Matching Approach
questions.question: In the diversified distribution matching framework for unsupervised domain translation, how does the proposed loss function use an auxiliary variable $u_i$ and multiple discriminators $\bm{d}_x^{(i)}, \bm{d}_y^{(i)}$ to match distribution pairs?
questions.question_ru: В рамках подхода согласования диверсифицированных распределений для перевода между доменами без учителя, как предлагаемая функция потерь использует вспомогательную переменную $u_i$ и несколько дискриминаторов $\bm{d}_x^{(i)}, \bm{d}_y^{(i)}$ для согласования пар распределений?
questions.reference_answer: The loss matches, for each $i=1,\ldots,I$, the conditional distribution pairs $(\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}|u_i},\bm{f}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{y}|u_i}})$ and $(\mathbb{P}_{\bm{y}|u_i},\bm{g}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}|u_i}})$, using a discriminator $\bm{d}_x^{(i)}$ (and $\bm{d}_y^{(i)}$ for the reverse direction) per pair. These per-pair GAN terms are summed over $i$ and combined with the cycle-consistency term weighted by $\lambda$.

evidence.text:
**Proposed Loss Function.** We propose to match multiple distribution pairs $(\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}|u_{i}},\bm{f}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{y}|u_{i}}})$ (as well as $(\mathbb{P}_{\bm{y}|u_{i}},\bm{g}_{\#\mathbb{P}_{\bm{x}|u_{i}}})$) for $i=1,\ldots,I$. For each pair, we use discriminator $\bm{d}_{x}^{(i)}:\mathcal{X}\to[0,1]$ (and $\bm{d}_{y}^{(i)}:\mathcal{Y}\to[0,1]$ in reverse direction). Then, our loss function is as follows:

$$
\displaystyle\min_{\bm{f},\bm{g}}\max_{\{\bm{d}_{x}^{(i)},\bm{d}_{y}^{(i)}\}}~\sum_{i=1}^{I}\left(\mathcal{L}_{\rm GAN}(\bm{g},\bm{d}_{y}^{(i)},\bm{x},\bm{y})+\mathcal{L}_{\rm GAN}(\bm{f},\bm{d}_{x}^{(i)},\bm{x},\bm{y})\right)+\lambda\mathcal{L}_{\rm cyc}(\bm{g},\bm{f}), \tag{7}
$$

questions.question: In unsupervised domain translation research, what structural assumptions on the target translation functions were previously used to establish translation identifiability, and why are those conditions considered restrictive?
questions.question_ru: В исследованиях перевода между доменами без учителя какие структурные предположения о целевых функциях перевода ранее использовались для установления идентифицируемости, и почему эти условия считаются ограничительными?
questions.reference_answer: Prior work argued that identifiability can be established if the target translation functions have known structures, such as linear or optimal transport structures. However, these conditions are restrictive, and establishing identifiability without such structural assumptions had remained unclear before the presented work.

evidence.text: Gulrajani & Hashimoto 2022 and de Bézenac et al. 2021 argued that if the target translation functions have known structures (e.g., linear or optimal transport structures), then translation identifiability can be established. However, these conditions can be restrictive. Translation identifiability without using such structural assumptions had remained unclear before our work.

questions.doc_title: Domain Transfer Becomes Identifiable via a Single Alignment
questions.question: How does the randomized masked finite-difference Jacobian sparsity regularizer avoid the cost of per-column Jacobian estimation, i.e., what sparse random mask z is used and what quantity replaces the individual Jacobian columns?
questions.question_ru: Как регуляризатор разреженности якобиана на основе рандомизированной маскированной конечной разности избегает затрат на покоординатную оценку якобиана, то есть какая разреженная случайная маска z используется и какая величина заменяет отдельные столбцы якобиана?
questions.reference_answer: Instead of perturbing one input dimension at a time (which needs D forward passes), it perturbs multiple dimensions at once using a random mask z with ||z||_0 = S << D. It then approximates ||J z||_0 by the finite difference ||(g(x+δz)-g(x))/δ||_0, enforcing that sparse input changes cause sparse output changes.

evidence.text:
To avoid repeated forward passes, we explore an alternative in which we apply the perturbation to multiple dimensions at once, i.e., consider a random mask $\boldsymbol{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{D}$, such that $\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{0}=S\ll D$. Now consider the following alternative finite difference approximation:

$$
\left\|\boldsymbol{J}_{\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}(\boldsymbol{x})\boldsymbol{z}\right\|_{0}\approx\left\|\frac{\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{x}+\delta\boldsymbol{z})-\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{x})}{\delta}\right\|_{0}. \tag{17}
$$

If we minimize $\|\boldsymbol{J}_{\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}(\boldsymbol{x})\boldsymbol{z}\|_{0}$ instead of $\|\boldsymbol{J}_{\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}(\boldsymbol{x})\boldsymbol{e}_{d}\|_{0}$, we are enforcing sparse changes in the input to $\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ to cause sparse changes to its output. This is intuitively linked to the Jacobian sparsity.

questions.doc_title: Domain Transfer Becomes Identifiable via a Single Alignment
questions.question: Why does diversified distribution matching (DDM) require more supervision than the single-anchor approach, and what makes its required side information hard to obtain in applications such as single-cell analysis?
questions.question_ru: Почему диверсифицированное сопоставление распределений (DDM) требует большего объёма супервизии, чем подход с одной опорной парой, и что делает требуемую им побочную информацию трудно доступной в приложениях вроде анализа отдельных клеток?
questions.reference_answer: DDM needs auxiliary information u for all samples, since each x and y must be annotated with the conditional distribution it is drawn from. This side information can be unavailable or costly, e.g., in single-cell analysis it is unclear what could serve as u across cell-development phases.

evidence.text: The DDM identifiability theory provides a practical and effective route to MPA elimination. However, DDM has a major drawback: it requires the availability of auxiliary information for all samples. Specifically, each $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}$ must be annotated with the variable $u$ that identifies which conditional distributions $p_{\boldsymbol{x}\mid u}$ and $p_{\boldsymbol{y}\mid u}$ it is drawn from. This auxiliary information may be unavailable or costly to obtain in many applications. For example, in single-cell analysis (43; 38), it is unclear what kind of side information could be used as $u$ across various phases of cell development.

questions.doc_title: scTopoGAN: unsupervised manifold alignment of single-cell data
questions.question: How does the topological autoencoder used for manifold projection in TopoGAN employ persistence homology to determine which structures of a single-cell dataset must be preserved in the low-dimensional representation?
questions.question_ru: Как топологический автоэнкодер, используемый в TopoGAN для проекции многообразия, применяет персистентную гомологию (persistence homology), чтобы определить, какие структуры набора данных single-cell должны сохраняться в низкоразмерном представлении?
questions.reference_answer: It uses persistence homology to selectively consider edges connecting point-pairs below a distance threshold, builds local neighborhoods from them, and repeats this over a wide range of thresholds to define persistent topological features called persistence pairings; preserving the distances between these pairings in the low-dimensional projection preserves the data topology.

evidence.text: A topological autoencoder is based on the concept of persistence homology (Edelsbrunner and Harer, 2008) which selectively considers edges connecting point-pairs below a certain distance threshold. These edges are used to construct local neighborhoods together constituting large-scale topological features. By repeating this procedure for a wide range of distance thresholds, persistent topological features are defined, where the point-pairs constituting them are known as persistence pairings. Preserving the distances between these pairings in a lower-dimensional projection of the data preserves the data topology.

questions.doc_title: scTopoGAN: unsupervised manifold alignment of single-cell data
questions.question: What exactly is TopoGAN's core assumption about the underlying manifolds of different single-cell modalities measured from the same tissue, and how does the method's discussion qualify or weaken that assumption?
questions.question_ru: В чём именно состоит основное предположение TopoGAN о лежащих в основе многообразиях различных модальностей single-cell, измеренных в одной и той же ткани, и как обсуждение метода ослабляет или уточняет это предположение?
questions.reference_answer: The assumption is that different single-cell modalities measured from the same tissue share the same underlying manifold structure; the discussion admits this is not completely true because each modality captures different molecular features and the manifolds are not identical, but argues there is still enough similarity between them to perform the integration.

evidence.text: The main assumption of TopoGAN, different modalities measured from the same tissue have the same underlying manifold structure, is not completely true. Although this assumption is based on the fact that the cell pool where different modalities sample from is the same, hence similar cellular structure, different modalities are measuring different molecular features capturing different views of this cellular structure. As a result, the underlying manifolds of each modality are not identical, however, we argue that there is enough similarity between these manifold that can be used to perform the data integration.

questions.question: What specific limitations of the integration methods UnionCom, MMD-MA and SCIM are identified as motivation for developing TopoGAN, especially regarding datasets whose single-cell modalities come from non-matching cells?
questions.question_ru: Какие конкретные ограничения методов интеграции UnionCom, MMD-MA и SCIM указаны как мотивация для разработки TopoGAN, особенно в отношении наборов данных, модальности single-cell в которых получены от несовпадающих клеток?
questions.reference_answer: UnionCom and MMD-MA were tested on single-cell multi-omics data whose modalities were measured from the same cell with perfect cell-to-cell correspondences, and their integration performance drops significantly when more realistic datasets lacking this correspondence are used; additionally, SCIM is not fully unsupervised because it requires partial cell type annotations for each modality.

evidence.text: These multi-modal alignment methods, however, suffer from several limitations. First, UnionCom and MMD-MA were tested on single-cell multi-omics data, in which the multiple modalities were measured from the same cell, with perfect cell-tocell correspondences. Although they did not exploit this correspondence in their methods, the integration performance drops significantly (as we show later) when, more realistic, datasets lacking this correspondence are used. Second, SCIM is not fully unsupervised as it requires (partial) cell type annotations for each of the different modalities in order to align the data.

questions.question: In the topological analysis of grayscale images, how is the V-construction defined, that is, how are the cubical grid complex and the filter function of a grayscale image specified, and why does it carry the name V-construction?
questions.question_ru: При топологическом анализе полутоновых изображений как определяется V-конструкция, то есть как задаются кубический решётчатый комплекс и функция фильтрации полутонового изображения, и почему она называется V-конструкцией?
questions.reference_answer: For a grayscale image I in R^{m×n} one takes the cubical grid complex K^{m,n} of all cubical cells contained in [1,m]×[1,n]; the filter function f_I equals the pixel value on the vertices and the maximum value of the vertices on all higher-dimensional cubes. Since f_I is order preserving, it induces the sublevel filtration D(I) and filtered cubical complex K_*(I). The construction is called the V-construction because pixels are treated as vertices of the cubical complex.

evidence.text: For a grayscale image ${\bm{I}}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m\times n}$ we consider the **cubical grid complex** $K^{m,n}$ consisting of all cubical cells contained in $[1,m]\times[1,n]\subseteq{\mathbb{R}}^{2}$. Its **filter function** $f_{I}$ is defined on the vertices of $K^{m,n}$ by the corresponding entry in ${\bm{I}}$, and on all higher-dimensional cubes as the maximum value of its vertices. Note that $f_{\bm{I}}$ is order preserving, so we can associate the sublevel filtration of $f_{\bm{I}}$ and its corresponding filtered cubical complex to the image ${\bm{I}}$ and denote them by $D({\bm{I}})$ and $K_{*}({\bm{I}})$, respectively. This construction is called the **V-construction** since pixels are treated as vertices in the cubical complex, see Fig. 3(b).

questions.doc_title: Topologically faithful image segmentation via induced matching of persistence barcodes
questions.question: In the analysis of the Wasserstein loss for segmentation, what happens in the false positive and false negative cases, that is, how does the loss affect the local contrast of a matched feature having no spatially corresponding ground-truth feature, and of an unmatched feature that does have a spatial correspondence?
questions.question_ru: В анализе функции потерь Васерштейна для сегментации что происходит в случаях ложноположительного и ложноотрицательного срабатывания, то есть как потеря влияет на локальный контраст сопоставленного признака, не имеющего пространственно соответствующего признака ground truth, и несопоставленного признака, у которого есть пространственное соответствие?
questions.reference_answer: In the false positive case (q matched but no spatially corresponding feature in G), because q is matched to (0,1) the Wasserstein loss is reduced by decreasing q1 and increasing q2, so the network wrongly increases the feature's local contrast. In the false negative case (q unmatched although a spatial counterpart exists), q is mapped to the diagonal and the loss is reduced by increasing q1 and decreasing q2, so the network wrongly decreases the local contrast.

evidence.text:
**case 1:** (**false positive**) $q$ is matched but there is no spatially corresponding feature in ${\bm{G}}$ :\
Since $q$ is matched to the point $(0,1)\in\Dgm({\bm{G}})$, the loss $l_{\text{W}}$ will be reduced by decreasing the value $q_{1}$ and increasing the value $q_{2}$. Hence, the segmentation network will learn to increase the local contrast of the feature described by the $q$ (see Sec. 3.2), but it should be decreased.

**case 2:** (**false negative**) $q$ is unmatched but there is a spatially corresponding feature in ${\bm{G}}$:\
Since $q$ is unmatched, the bijection $\gamma_{*}$ maps it to its closest point $((q_{1}+q_{2})/2,(q_{1}+q_{2})/2)$ on the diagonal $\Delta$ and the loss $l_{\text{W}}$ will be reduced by increasing the value $q_{1}$ and decreasing the value $q_{2}$. Hence, the segmentation network will learn to decrease the local contrast of the feature described by $q$ (see Sec. 3.2), but it should be increased.

questions.doc_title: Unpaired Multi-Domain Causal Representation Learning
questions.question: In the unpaired multi-domain causal representation (MDCR) model, what does it mean for an observed variable v to be a partial pure child of a shared latent node k, and does this definition forbid domain-specific latent parents of v?
questions.question_ru: В модели причинного представления для нескольких несвязанных доменов (MDCR) что означает, что наблюдаемая переменная v является частично чистым потомком (partial pure child) общей латентной вершины k, и запрещает ли это определение наличие домен-специфических латентных родителей у v?
questions.reference_answer: An observed node v is a partial pure child of a shared latent node k if the intersection of v's parents with the shared latent set L equals exactly {k}, i.e., pa(v)∩L={k}. It does not forbid domain-specific latent parents: it only requires that exactly one parent lies in L.

evidence.text:
**Definition 4.2.** Let $\mathcal{G}_{m}=(\mathcal{H}\cup V,D)$ be an $m$-domain graph with shared latent nodes $\mathcal{L}\subseteq\mathcal{H}$. For $k\in\mathcal{L}$, we say that an observed node $v\in V$ is a *partial pure child* of $k$ if $\text{pa}(v)\cap\mathcal{L}=\{k\}$.

For a partial pure child $v\in V$, there may still be domain-specific latent nodes that are parents of $v$. Definition 4.2 only requires that there is exactly one parent that is in the set $\mathcal{L}$. This explains the name *partial* pure child; see Example B.2 in the Appendix for further elaboration.

questions.doc_title: Unpaired Multi-Domain Causal Representation Learning
questions.question: What two-step strategy is used to establish identifiability in unpaired multi-domain causal representation learning, and what role does exploiting sparsity in the overall mixing matrix play in identifying the causal structure among shared latent variables?
questions.question_ru: Какая двухэтапная стратегия используется для установления идентифицируемости в задаче несвязанного многодоменного причинного представления и какую роль играет использование разреженности в общей матрице смешивания при идентификации причинной структуры среди общих латентных переменных?
questions.reference_answer: First, identifiability of linear independent component analysis is extended to the multi-domain setup, which identifies the joint distribution and distinguishes shared from domain-specific latent variables. Second, an overall mixing matrix is identified and sparsity constraints in that matrix are exploited to identify the causal structure among the shared latent variables.

evidence.text: We circumvent this problem via a two-step approach: First, we extend the identifiability of linear independent component analysis (Comon, 1994; Hyvärinen and Oja, 2000; Eriksson and Koivunen, 2004; Mesters and Zwiernik, 2022) to the multi-domain setup, which allows us to identify the joint distribution and distinguish between shared and domain-specific latent variables. Moreover, we identify an “overall mixing matrix” and, in a second step, exploit sparsity constraints in this matrix to identify the causal structure among the shared latent variables. This leverages recent results on causal discovery under measurement error in single domains that also exploit sparsity (Xie et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022; Xie et al., 2022; Huang et al., 2022).

questions.doc_title: Unpaired Multi-Domain Causal Representation Learning
questions.question: How does the unpaired multi-domain causal representation learning setting differ from the methods of Adams et al. (2021) and Zeng et al. (2021) with respect to the dimensions of the domains, the treatment of shared versus domain-specific latent variables, and the assumptions needed to identify the shared latent graph?
questions.question_ru: Чем постановка задачи несвязанного многодоменного причинного представления отличается от методов Adams et al. (2021) и Zeng et al. (2021) в отношении размерностей доменов, трактовки общих и домен-специфических латентных переменных, а также предположений, необходимых для идентификации общего латентного графа?
questions.reference_answer: Unlike Adams et al. (2021), which assumes the number of observed variables is the same in every domain and that all latent variables are shared, the MDCR setup considers domains of different dimensions and allows both shared and domain-specific latent variables with an unknown number of shared nodes. Unlike Zeng et al. (2021), it uses a general but fixed number of observed variables and requires only two partial pure children (weaker than two pure children) to identify the shared latent graph.

evidence.text: The works of Adams et al., 2021 and Zeng et al., 2021 may be considered closest to ours as they also treat a setting with multiple domains and unpaired data. However, our setup and results are more general. Adams et al., 2021 assume that the number of observed variables are the same in each domain, whereas we consider domains of *different dimensions* corresponding to the fact that observations may be of very different nature. Further, we allow for *shared and domain-specific* latent variables, where the number of shared latent variables is unknown, while in Adams et al., 2021 it is assumed that all latent variables are shared. Compared to Zeng et al., 2021, we consider a general but fixed number of observed variables, while Zeng et al., 2021 only show identifiability of the full model in a setup where the number of observed variables in each domain increases to infinity. On a more technical level, the conditions in Zeng et al., 2021 require two pure children to identify the shared latent graph, while we prove identifiability under the weaker assumption of two partial pure children; see Section 4 for precise definitions.

questions.doc_title: The persistent homology of a sampled map: From a viewpoint of quiver representations
questions.question: For a correspondence $F$ between topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, with canonical projections $p\colon F\to X$ and $q\colon F\to Y$ and their homology induced maps $p_{*}$ and $q_{*}$, what two conditions on $p_{*}$ and $q_{*}$ are required, by name, and how is the induced map $F_{*}$ then defined?
questions.question_ru: Для соответствия $F$ между топологическими пространствами $X$ и $Y$ с каноническими проекциями $p\colon F\to X$ и $q\colon F\to Y$ и их индуцированными отображениями гомологий $p_{*}$ и $q_{*}$: какие два условия на $p_{*}$ и $q_{*}$ требуются (назовите их) и как после этого определяется индуцированное отображение $F_{*}$?
questions.reference_answer: The two conditions are being *homologically complete*, $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits p_{*}=HX$, and *homologically consistent*, $q_{*}(\Ker p_{*})=0$. Under these, the induced map is defined by $F_{*}:=q_{*}\circ p_{*}^{-1}\colon HX\to HY$ and is well-defined.

evidence.text:
**Definition 1.3.** For a correspondence $F$, let $p\colon F\to X$ and $q\colon F\to Y$ be canonical projections, and $p_{*}\colon HF\to HX$ and $q_{*}\colon HF\to HY$ be their homology induced maps. If $p_{*}$ and $q_{*}$ satisfy two properties

- $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits p_{*}=HX$ (*homologically complete*)
- $q_{*}(\Ker p_{*})=0$ (*homologically consistent*),

then the *induced map* of $F$ is defined by $F_{*}:=q_{*}\circ p_{*}^{-1}\colon HX\to HY$, and is well-defined.

questions.doc_title: The persistent homology of a sampled map: From a viewpoint of quiver representations
questions.question: In the persistent homology analysis of a sampled map built from quiver representations, what advantage does it have over the method of Edelsbrunner et al. 2015 that uses eigenspace functors, specifically regarding the assumptions on the two spaces and the need for prior information about the map?
questions.question_ru: В анализе персистентных гомологий сэмплированного отображения, построенном на представлениях колчанов: какое преимущество он имеет перед методом Эдельсбруннера и др. 2015, использующим функторы собственных подпространств, в частности относительно предположений о двух пространствах и необходимости априорной информации об отображении?
questions.reference_answer: Because it does not use the eigenspace functor, the two spaces need not be the same, so the assumption $f\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{S}\colon S\to S$ can be weakened to $f\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{S}\colon S\to f(S)$ and another filtration can be taken on $f(S)$ (or on $S\cup f(S)$). Also, unlike the earlier method, it does not need to set an eigenvalue and thus needs no prior information about the map.

evidence.text: This persistence diagram does not provide any information about eigenvectors, unlike [Edelsbrunner et al. 2015]; however, it can be widely applied. First, since our method does not use the eigenspace functor, we need not require both sides’ spaces to be the same. Therefore, even in the case of sampled dynamical systems $X=Y$ like the previous research, we can weaken the assumption $f\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{S}\colon S\to S$ to $f\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{S}\colon S\to f(S)$ and take another filtration on $f(S)$. (If $f(S)$ is not dense enough for sampling $X$, then we can take $S\cup f(S)$ instead.) Moreover, since the previous method needs to set an eigenvalue before analysis, they have to predict some behavior of $f$ in advance, but our method does not need any prior information.

questions.doc_title: The persistent homology of a sampled map: From a viewpoint of quiver representations
questions.question: In a computer implementation of persistent homology where every map is represented as a matrix over a finite field, why is it preferable to choose a large prime number $p$ rather than $p=2$ as the coefficient field $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$?
questions.question_ru: Почему при компьютерной реализации персистентных гомологий, где каждое отображение записывается матрицей над конечным полем, предпочтительнее выбирать большое простое число $p$, а не $p=2$, в качестве поля коэффициентов $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$?
questions.reference_answer: Over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ every matrix entry with prime factor 2 becomes 0, so a homology generator $a$ mapped as $f_{*}(a)=2a$ is ignored; choosing a larger prime $p$ for $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ retrieves more generators.

evidence.text: To implement the persistence analysis on computers, we must use finite fields as the coefficient. Here, every map is written as a matrix. If we choose the field $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ as the coefficient, then every entry with the prime factor $2$ in the matrix is regarded as $0$. For example, a homology generator $a$ mapped as $f_{*}(a)=2a$, such as the example discussed later and in Figure 4, is ignored. Therefore, it is better to choose a larger prime number $p$ as the coefficient $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to retrieve more generators.

questions.doc_title: Identifiable Shared Component Analysis of Unpaired Multimodal Mixtures
questions.question: In the multimodal linear mixture model where each modality is generated as x^(q) = A^(q) z^(q), how is the latent code z^(q) decomposed, and what do the shared components c and the modality-private components p^(q) denote?
questions.question_ru: В модели линейной смеси, где каждая модальность порождается как x^(q) = A^(q) z^(q), как раскладывается латентный код z^(q) и что обозначают общие компоненты c и приватные компоненты p^(q)?
questions.reference_answer: The latent code is decomposed as z^(q)=[c^⊤,(p^(q))^⊤]^⊤, where c∈R^{d_C} stands for the shared components and p^(q)∈R^{d_P^(q)} for the modality-private components, with x^(q)∈R^{d^(q)} and z^(q)∈R^{d_C+d_P^(q)}. The observed data are generated as x^(q)=A^(q)z^(q).

evidence.text:
Following the classical settings in [2, 1, 15, 16, 18], we consider modeling the multi-modal data as linear mixtures. More specifically, we adopt the model in [2, 1]that splits the latent representation of data into shared components and private components:

$$
\displaystyle\boldsymbol{x}^{(q)}=\boldsymbol{A}^{(q)}\boldsymbol{z}^{(q)},\quad\bm{z}^{(q)}=[\bm{c}^{\top},(\bm{p}^{(q)})^{\top}]^{\top},~q=1,2, \tag{1}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{x}^{(q)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{(q)}}$ represents the data from the $q$th modality, $\boldsymbol{z}^{(q)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\rm C}+d_{\rm P}^{(q)}}$ represents the corresponding latent code, $\bm{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\rm C}}$ and $\bm{p}^{(q)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{(q)}_{\rm P}}$ stand for the shared components and the private components, respectively.

questions.doc_title: Identifiable Shared Component Analysis of Unpaired Multimodal Mixtures
questions.question: For unaligned shared component analysis, what adversarial objective is optimized over the linear transforms Q^(1) and Q^(2) and the discriminator f, and when is its minimax optimal point attained?
questions.question_ru: В задаче анализа общих компонент без выравнивания какая состязательная целевая функция оптимизируется по линейным преобразованиям Q^(1), Q^(2) и дискриминатору f, и когда достигается её минимаксная оптимальная точка?
questions.reference_answer: The objective is the min over Q^(1),Q^(2) and max over f of E_{x^(1)} log(f(Q^(1)x^(1))) + E_{x^(2)} log(1−f(Q^(2)x^(2))) + λ∑_{q=1}^2 R(Q^(q)). Q^(q) is trained to confuse the best-possible discriminator f:R^{d_C}→R, and the minimax optimal point of the first two terms is attained when the distribution-matching constraint (6b), Q^(1)x^(1) ⟶^(d) Q^(2)x^(2), is met.

evidence.text:
We use the adversarial loss:

$$
\displaystyle\min_{{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{(1)},{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{(2)}}\max_{f}~\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{x}^{(1)}}\log\left(f({\boldsymbol{Q}}^{(1)}{\boldsymbol{x}}^{(1)})\right)+\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{x}^{(2)}}\log\left(1-f({\boldsymbol{Q}}^{(2)}{\boldsymbol{x}}^{(2)})\right)+\lambda\sum_{q=1}^{2}{\cal R}\left({\boldsymbol{Q}}^{(q)}\right), \tag{7}
$$

The first and second terms comprise the adversarial loss from GAN [38]. It finds $\bm{Q}^{(q)}$ to confuse the best-possible discriminator $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_{\rm C}}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$, where $f$ is represented by a neural network in practice. It is well known that the minimax optimal point of the first two terms is attained when (6b) is met [38].

questions.doc_title: Identifiable Shared Component Analysis of Unpaired Multimodal Mixtures
questions.question: How many aligned cross-modality sample pairs does the weakly supervised unaligned shared component formulation need to establish identifiability, and how does this compare with the number required by canonical correlation analysis (CCA)?
questions.question_ru: Сколько выровненных межмодальных пар образцов требуется слабо контролируемой формулировке анализа общих компонент без выравнивания для установления идентифицируемости, и сколько пар для этого требуется каноническому корреляционному анализу (CCA)?
questions.reference_answer: The weakly supervised formulation needs as few as d_C aligned cross-modality pairs of (x_ℓ^(1),x_ℓ^(2)) to establish identifiability of the shared component, whereas CCA requires at least d_C+d_P^(1)+d_P^(2) pairs to attain the same identifiability.

evidence.text: A remark is that our weakly supervised formulation can use as few as $d_{\rm C}$ pairs of $(\boldsymbol{x}_{\ell}^{(1)},\boldsymbol{x}_{\ell}^{(2)})$ to establish identifiability of shared component. In contrast, CCA requires at least $d_{\rm C}+d_{\rm P}^{(1)}+d_{\rm P}^{(2)}$ pairs to attain the same identifiability (cf. Appendix. E.1).

questions.doc_title: Improving and generalizing flow-based generative models with minibatch optimal transport
questions.question: What stochastic training objective, called conditional flow matching (CFM), regresses a neural-network vector field $v_\theta(t,x)$ onto a marginal vector field $u_t(x)$, and which quantities need only be samplable or computable to evaluate its gradient?
questions.question_ru: Какая стохастическая цель обучения, называемая conditional flow matching (CFM), выполняет регрессию векторного поля $v_\theta(t,x)$, задаваемого нейронной сетью, к маргинальному векторному полю $u_t(x)$, и какие величины достаточно уметь сэмплировать или вычислять, чтобы оценить её градиент?
questions.reference_answer: The CFM objective is $\mathcal{L}_{\rm CFM}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{t,q(z),p_{t}(x|z)}\|v_{\theta}(t,x)-u_{t}(x|z)\|^{2}$, which regresses the network against the conditional vector field $u_{t}(x|z)$ so as to match the marginal field $u_{t}(x)$. It needs only samples from $q(z)$ and from the conditional probability path $p_{t}(x|z)$, plus the computable conditional vector field $u_{t}(x|z)$.

evidence.text:
Let $v_{\theta}(\cdot,\cdot):[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a time-dependent vector field parametrized as a neural network with weights $\theta$. Define the **conditional flow matching (CFM)** objective:

$$
{\mathcal{L}}_{\rm CFM}(\theta):=\mathbb{E}_{t,q(z),p_{t}(x|z)}\|v_{\theta}(t,x)-u_{t}(x|z)\|^{2}. \tag{10}
$$

The CFM objective describes how to regress against the marginal vector field $u_{t}(x)$ given by (9) with access only to samples from the conditional probability path $p_{t}(x|z)$ and conditional vector fields $u_{t}(x|z)$.

questions.doc_title: Improving and generalizing flow-based generative models with minibatch optimal transport
questions.question: When the marginal probability path $p_t(x)$ of a continuous normalizing flow is written as a mixture $p_t(x)=\int p_t(x|z)q(z)\,dz$ of conditional paths, each generated by a conditional vector field $u_t(x|z)$, what expression gives the marginal vector field $u_t(x)$ that generates the mixture, and what does the corresponding theorem assert?
questions.question_ru: Если маргинальный вероятностный путь $p_t(x)$ непрерывного нормализующего потока записан как смесь $p_t(x)=\int p_t(x|z)q(z)\,dz$ условных путей, каждый из которых порождается условным векторным полем $u_t(x|z)$, каким выражением задаётся маргинальное векторное поле $u_t(x)$, порождающее эту смесь, и что утверждает соответствующая теорема?
questions.reference_answer: The marginal vector field is $u_{t}(x):=\mathbb{E}_{q(z)}\frac{u_{t}(x|z)p_{t}(x|z)}{p_{t}(x)}$, and Theorem 3.1 states that this marginal vector field generates the probability path $p_{t}(x)=\int p_{t}(x|z)q(z)\,dz$ from the initial conditions $p_{0}(x)$.

evidence.text:
Suppose that the marginal probability path $p_{t}(x)$ is a mixture of probability paths $p_{t}(x|z)$ that vary with some conditioning variable $z$, that is,

$$
p_{t}(x)=\int p_{t}(x|z)q(z)\,dz, \tag{8}
$$

where $q(z)$ is some distribution over the conditioning variable. If the probability path $p_{t}(x|z)$ is generated by the vector field $u_{t}(x|z)$ from initial conditions $p_{0}(x|z)$ (see §2.1), then the vector field

$$
u_{t}(x):=\mathbb{E}_{q(z)}\frac{u_{t}(x|z)p_{t}(x|z)}{p_{t}(x)} \tag{9}
$$

generates the probability path $p_{t}(x)$, under some mild conditions: arxiv-pratenddefaultcategory.tex

**Theorem 3.1.** The marginal vector field (9) generates the probability path (8) from initial conditions $p_{0}(x)$.

questions.doc_title: Improving and generalizing flow-based generative models with minibatch optimal transport
questions.question: Why can computing the optimal transport plan $\pi$ between source and target samples be impractical for large datasets in optimal transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM), and what does the method do instead when this cost is prohibitive?
questions.question_ru: Почему вычисление плана оптимального транспорта $\pi$ между исходными и целевыми сэмплами может быть непрактичным для больших наборов данных в optimal transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM), и что метод использует вместо этого, когда эта стоимость слишком высока?
questions.reference_answer: The transport plan can be hard to compute and store because optimal transport has cubic time and quadratic memory complexity in the number of samples. When this is prohibitive, OT-CFM uses a minibatch approximation of OT, which introduces error relative to the exact OT solution but works well in practice.

evidence.text: For large datasets, the transport plan $\pi$ can be difficult to compute and store due to OT’s cubic time and quadratic memory complexity in the number of samples (Cuturi 2013; Tong et al. 2020). If this cost is prohibitive, we can use a minibatch approximation of OT similar to Fatras et al. 2021b. Although minibatch OT incurs an error relative to the exact OT solution, it has been successfully used in many applications like domain adaptation or generative modeling (Damodaran et al. 2018; Genevay et al. 2018).

questions.doc_title: UVCGAN v2: An Improved Cycle-Consistent GAN for Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation
questions.question: In the UVCGANv2 unpaired image-to-image translation model, how does source-driven style modulation modify the convolution weights of the generator's decoding branch, and by what formula are the resulting weights demodulated to preserve activation magnitude?
questions.question_ru: В модели непарного перевода изображение-в-изображение UVCGANv2 как модуляция стиля, управляемая источником, изменяет веса свёртки в декодирующей ветви генератора и по какой формуле выполняется демодуляция полученных весов для сохранения амплитуды активаций?
questions.reference_answer: Style modulation scales each convolution weight by the supplied style vector, yielding $w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}=s_{i}\cdot w_{i,j,x,y}$, where $i,j$ index input/output feature maps and $x,y$ the spatial dimensions. To preserve activation magnitude the scaled weights are demodulated as $w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime\prime}=w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}/\sqrt{\sum_{i,x,y}(w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime})^{2}+\epsilon}$, with $\epsilon$ a small constant preventing numerical instability.

evidence.text:
The style modulation [21] effectively scales weights $w_{i,j,x,y}$ of the convolutional operator by the supplied style vector $s_{i}$, yielding modulated weights:

$$
w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}=s_{i}\cdot w_{i,j,x,y} \tag{6}
$$

where $i$, $j$ refer to the input and output feature maps and $x$, $y$ enumerate the spatial dimensions. To preserve the magnitude of the activations, the scaled weights $w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}$ need to be demodulated. The demodulation operation further renormalizes the convolution weights as follows:

$$
w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime\prime}=\frac{w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}}{\sqrt{\sum_{i,x,y}\left(w_{i,j,x,y}^{\prime}\right)^{2}+\epsilon}} \tag{7}
$$

where $\epsilon$ is a small number to prevent numerical instability.

questions.doc_title: UVCGAN v2: An Improved Cycle-Consistent GAN for Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation
questions.question: How does the UVCGANv2 discriminator use a memory-bank cache together with a batch head to obtain minibatch discrimination without requiring a large batch size, and how are its feature caches organized and updated during training?
questions.question_ru: Как дискриминатор UVCGANv2 использует кэш типа «memory bank» вместе с batch head, чтобы обеспечить minibatch discrimination без большого размера батча, и как организованы и обновляются его кэши признаков во время обучения?
questions.reference_answer: The discriminator is split into a main body plus a batch head made of a batch-statistics layer followed by two convolutional layers, which allows swapping bodies while preserving minibatch discrimination power. During training the batch features are stored in four separate fixed-size caches (real domain-$a$, real domain-$b$, and fake images from both domains) that follow a first-in-first-out (FIFO) update policy.

evidence.text: We design a composite discriminator made of a main *body* and a *batch head*. The composite discriminator body can be any common discriminator, but, for the purposes of this work, we use UVCGAN’s discriminator without the last layer. The batch head is made of a layer that captures batch statistics, followed by two convolutional layers (Figure 2). This modular discriminator architecture allows for easily swapping different discriminator bodies while still preserving the minibatch discrimination power. During training, the batch features are stored in four separate caches: real images from domain $a$, real images from domain $b$, and fake images from both domains. All the caches have a fixed size and follow the first-in-first-out (FIFO) update policy.
section_path: UVCGAN v2: An Improved Cycle-Consistent GAN for Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation

questions.doc_title: UVCGAN v2: An Improved Cycle-Consistent GAN for Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation
questions.question: Why do the developers of the UVCGANv2 unpaired translation method build on the classic CycleGAN architecture rather than diffusion-based models, and what intrinsic consistency advantage does the cycle-consistency constraint offer over simple pixel-wise consistency measures?
questions.question_ru: Почему разработчики метода непарного перевода UVCGANv2 строят решение на классической архитектуре CycleGAN, а не на диффузионных моделях, и какое внутреннее преимущество в согласованности даёт ограничение cycle-consistency по сравнению с простыми попиксельными мерами согласованности?
questions.reference_answer: Because revisiting classic neural architectures and adding modern improvements has repeatedly led to large performance gains, UVCGAN modernized the classic CycleGAN. Unlike DM-based models, CycleGAN's training can utilize source and target domain images effectively and simultaneously, and its cycle-consistency constraint maintains an intrinsic consistency between source and translated images that simple pixel-wise consistency measures cannot achieve.

evidence.text: On multiple occasions, revisiting a classic neural architecture and improving it with a number of modern additions has led to vast improvements in performance [28, 21, 2]. Based on this observation, UVCGAN [42] modernizes the classic CycleGAN architecture and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several I2I tasks. Unlike the DM-based models, CycleGAN’s training procedure is able to utilize images from the source and target domains effectively and simultaneously. Moreover, CycleGAN maintains an intrinsic consistency between the source and translated images (via the cycle-consistency constraint)—a feature that cannot be achieved by simple pixel-wise consistency measures.
